core_passport.why: Most discriminating property in all 20 industries; every machine holds its sample/product/test article between a documented lowest and highest temperature (DR plate, PPMS chamber, freezer set-point range, LN2 dewar storage space -196 C liquid to -190 C top box, freeze-dryer shelf, TVAC platen, microtome specimen head, probe-station chuck, Stirling cold tip). point_within/range_within/at_most/at_least all work on a range, so one documented range decides most pairs and a range that excludes the needed temperature gives DOES_NOT_MEET immediately. Already on 25/26 configurations. Single stated temperature -> lo = hi.

Existing mK profiles are written as temperature.base at_most X; every machine has a lowest temperature, so it is always documentable (= temperature.range.lo unless a separate base is stated) and lets existing quantum profiles decide against new machines (a -80 C freezer immediately fails base <= 20 mK).

Hard requirement in magnetometry, quantum transport, NMR/MRI, conductor testing, DNP; for most new machines (freezers, dewars, freeze dryers, TVAC, cryocoolers) the honest entry is install=not_available backed by the complete spec, which turns field-requiring pairs into DOES_NOT_MEET instead of NEED_MORE_INFORMATION.

Splits equipment into evacuated sample spaces (cryostats, TVAC, freeze dryers, cryo-FIB, UHV/ARPES, matrix isolation, boil-off calorimeters) and atmospheric/vapour storage (freezers, dewars, microtomes, climatic chambers, Charpy baths); many procedures require it (GEVS, lyophilisation, ice analogues), others forbid it. Trivially documentable flag.

Quantifies the vacuum the procedure needs: GEVS < 1.33e-3 Pa, freeze drying 10-30 Pa, UHV astrochemistry/ARPES ~1e-8 Pa. Machines without vacuum record a sourced absence (not_available), which decides vacuum-requiring experiments. Torr/mbar convert exactly.
Needed by every spectroscopy, microscopy, photonics, laser, detector, solar-simulation and visual-inspection procedure; always documentable as windows/viewports present or none.

Any powered or measured DUT (TVAC payload, battery cell, qubit, detector, HTS tape, transport sample) needs feedthroughs; storage equipment normally has none (a probe access port is not sample wiring). Simple flag every spec sheet settles.

Universal lateral size gate (wafer 51-300 mm, vial/straw/box footprint, puck/bore, TVAC test-article envelope, 3 mm grids, 6 mm HPF carriers). Existing sample.width.max/length.max are documented on only 3 and 1 of 26 configurations and caused NEED_MORE_INFORMATION. Rule: clear diameter perpendicular to the loading direction; rectangular space -> smaller cross-section dimension; experiments give the circumscribed diameter of their sample footprint.

Second universal size gate: usable length along the loading axis (freezer/dewar inside height, rack/canister height, TVAC chamber length, stage clearance, freeze-dryer shelf spacing). Together with sample.diameter.max it replaces width/length for new profiles.

Documented on all 26 existing configurations; every machine either runs on electricity alone or consumes a liquid cryogen. Field, space, MRI siting, defense and helium-shortage experiments state it as a requirement.

Existing set key never filled. Listing the liquid cryogens used/held lets bath and immersion procedures decide: ASTM E1450 needs liquid_helium, -196 C Charpy / IEC 61788-26 / valve tests need liquid_nitrogen, plunge freezing needs liquid_ethane, LH2 materials tests need liquid_hydrogen, LAr TPCs need liquid_argon. Closed-cycle/mechanical machines document the empty set, which decides set_contains requirements. Controlled tokens: liquid_nitrogen, liquid_helium, liquid_argon, liquid_hydrogen, liquid_oxygen, liquid_neon, lng, liquid_ethane, dry_ice, compressed_argon_jt, compressed_helium_jt.

new_keys.description: Usable internal volume of the sample/storage/test space (freezer cabinet, controlled-rate-freezer chamber, environmental/thermal-vacuum chamber, freeze-dryer product chamber, archive freezer). Example: Planer Kryo 560-16 'Chamber volume 16 litres'.
Documented maximum number of 1.2/2.0 mL cryovials held with the standard inventory system (LN2 freezers, dewars, CRFs, freezers when stated in vials). Example: MVE HEco 815P-190 '15,600'.
Documented maximum number of 0.5 mL (1/2 cc) straws (semen/embryo banking, IVF, livestock genetics). Example: MVE HE 800 C 'over 22,000 1/2cc straws'.

Static holding time: how long one cryogen charge keeps the storage/sample space at its rated temperature without refill or external power (LN2 dewars, vapour freezers, dry shippers, LHe cryostats). Days convert exactly (x24). Example: MVE dry shipper 'STATIC HOLD TIME ... 18 DAYS'.

Temperature range of the thermal shroud/cold wall of a thermal-vacuum or space-simulation chamber (radiative environment); the platen/test-article range stays in temperature.range. Example: 'Shroud temperature control range: -180 to +150 C'.
Lowest documented temperature of the freeze-dryer ice condenser / cold trap (aqueous -50 C vs solvent/low-collapse -80 to -85 C). Example: Christ Epsilon 2-4 condenser minimum -85 C.
Documented maximum ice load of the freeze-dryer condenser before defrost, in kg; capacities printed in litres are a different dimension and must not be converted.

Range of controlled cooling-rate magnitudes the machine can impose (controlled-rate freezers, cryo-stages, DSC, climatic chambers); point_within checks -1 C/min or 0.3 C/min protocols. Example: Planer Kryo 560 'Cooling Rates -0.01 C/min to -50 C/min'.
Documented cooling power at 77 K (tactical IR Stirling coolers, HTS cable/SFCL coolers, reliquefiers); ambient condition kept in evidence. Example: Ricor K508 '550mW@77K@71C'.
Documented cooling power at 80 K, the standard rating point of space and long-life pulse-tube/Stirling coolers. Example: NICMOS cryocooler '7 W at 80 K'.

Maximum allowable working pressure of the sample vessel/chamber/flow loop (cryogenic test vessels, supercritical-He loops, high-pressure freezers 2100 bar, hydrate cells, LH2/LNG tanks). bar converts exactly; psi only as a bound rounded down with the printed value in the quote.

Maximum liquid-cryogen flow delivered to the process or meter under test (cryogenic machining, LN2 tunnel freezers, LNG/LN2 flow calibration, transfer systems); gas flow stays in gas.flow_rate.max. m3/h converts exactly only if divisible by 3.

Maximum transport current of installed current leads to the sample (HTS tape/cable Ic tests, magnet and fusion conductor tests); distinct from electrical.current.max of a measurement module. Example: SPARC TFMC '50 kA capacity ... current leads'.
Controllable relative-humidity range of the sample chamber (cryo-EM plunge freezers, climatic/damp-heat chambers, cloud chambers). Example: Vitrobot SOP 'Humidity 100%, Temperature 4 C - 22 C'.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 scientific_research experiment profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\scientific_research\experiments.json. They have 52 requirements in total. Each requirement carries keys, a constraint, mandatory, rationale, source_url, document_title, location, a verbatim quote of at most 50 words, evidence_status and accessed (2026-11-01).

How the quotes were checked:
- For the arXiv sources I read the PDF text directly and looked up page numbers.
- The EPR quotes (PMC2556177) come from a WebFetch extraction of the PMC page, not a direct PDF read.
- The Cryostream manual quote comes from a text extraction another agent left in the shared scratchpad folder (txt/cryostream800.txt). I did not fetch the SFU URL myself.

I left out several ideas so the profiles would not duplicate other work:
- Relaxation heat capacity and Orange-cryostat neutron work: profiles already exist (expa_relaxation_heat_capacity, expa_magnetic_powder_neutrons), and the ILL page is an equipment list, not a procedure.
- MPMS ZFC/FC on nanoparticles: this belongs to the materials industry. I replaced it with ZFC/FC plus magnetization loops of an Hg-1223 superconductor measured with a SQUID-VSM.
- TTK 600 low-temperature powder XRD: the Malvern leaflet is the chemistry agent's source.

Caveats:
1. Two profiles use the same paper, the SSRF endstation paper arXiv:2102.09915. ARPES uses the gold Fermi-edge test at 7 K below 1E-10 mbar. STM uses NbSe2 at 5 K and 2e-10 mbar. In the STM profile, the 380 mK base temperature and the 14 T field are facility capabilities, so I marked them non-mandatory.
2. Cryocrystallography relies on a CCP4/DLS lecture by E. Garman ("collect data at around 100K") and the Cryostream 800 manual, marked as reference_data and manufacturer_specification. I could not reach a methods paper: the RSC and IUCr links returned 404 and 403, and Tavily was over quota.
3. No source stated a maximum field for EPR or the Hg-1223 loops, so neither profile has a magnetic_field.max requirement. The EPR profile has mandatory rf.power.max (at least 2 mW) and rf.frequency.range (9.48 GHz), but few machines document these keys, so EPR may still come out NEED_MORE_INFORMATION on non-EPR equipment.
4. sample.diameter.max values are the circumscribed diameter of the stated sample footprint, rounded up: 11.42 mm (graphite), 4.13 mm (PdGa), 1.78 mm (Hg-1223). The rationale shows the calculation.
5. For the Hg-1223 profile, the requirement that the temperature range reach at least 129 K uses at_least on a range. I assume it checks that the top of the machine's range is at least 129 K. Please confirm the checker reads at_least on a range that way.
6. Flags use {"kind":"present"}, as in the existing profiles. Pressures are exact decimal strings in mbar ("0.0000000001", "0.0000000002").
7. Where a source names no specific equipment model, reported_equipment uses the generic wording from the paper (for example, the graphene paper names no cryostat).

eq.notes: Output file: C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\scientific_research\equipment.json (8 machines, 8 configurations, 103 capabilities, 13 not_found; every capability also carries accessed=2026-11-01 in the file). Manufacturers (7): Quantum Design (MPMS 3, OptiCool), Oxford Cryosystems (Cryostream 800), Anton Paar (TTK 600), Oxford Instruments (HelioxVT), Quantum Design Oxford / Oxford NanoScience (Proteox MX), Lake Shore / Janis (ST-500), attocube (attoDRY2100). None duplicates data/cryostats. All values are manufacturer specifications read from the cited PDFs and pages. PDF quotes are whitespace-normalised text extractions: superscripts are lost (e.g. '10-2 mbar' means 1e-2 mbar, '1mm3' means 1 mm^3) and bullet glyphs are rendered as '•'. Sourced absences: no magnet on Cryostream 800, TTK 600 and the HelioxVT system; no evacuated sample space on the MPMS 3 (pumped-helium chamber), attoDRY2100 (exchange gas) and Cryostream (open stream). Of the 88 core-key cells, 76 are decided and 12 are in not_found. Values that are typical only: ST-500 stability and base pressure, and the MPMS 3 sweep rate. Conservative choices: attoDRY2100 base temperature 1.8 K; Proteox cooling power at 100 mK is the guaranteed value; TTK 600 maximum working pressure is stored as the 2 bar gauge value. Categories left uncovered because no reachable complete datasheet was found: UHV ARPES/STM manipulators (the Scienta Omicron cryo-manipulator brochure lacks base pressure and sample size, and the LT STM III brochure exceeds 10 MB), neutron Orange cryostats (only facility-specific ILL tables), the ESR900 EPR cryostat (no datasheet online) and LHe storage dewars (the Cryofab CMSH sheet has a garbled font encoding). The Tavily quota ran out early, so documents were read with WebFetch (PDFs it saved were text-extracted with pymupdf) and with the built-in browser in read-only mode. One mishap: opening the LT STM III brochure URL in the built-in browser started a file download and showed the user a save dialog; that URL was not retried.

vexp.summary:
I checked 45 requirements in 10 profiles. 44 are accepted, 6 of them with a corrected constraint, and 1 is rejected.

**Quotes:** I downloaded every cited source (7 arXiv PDFs, PMC2556177, the Garman CCP4 slides and the Cryostream 800 manual) and compared the extracted text against each quote. All 41 distinct quotes are really there. Where the match was not exact, the only differences were special characters lost in extraction (x, ±, µ, en-dashes, alpha), footnote markers and page-break artifacts.

**Numbers and units:** all check out, including the derived values:
- Sample diagonals: 11.42 mm, 4.13 mm and 1.78 mm, each rounded up.
- Sweep rates: 30 mT/min = 0.5 mT/s, and 200 Oe/s.
- Pressures: 1e-10 mbar and 2e-10 mbar.

Every unit symbol exists in `cryolean/units.py`.

**Corrected (6):** every `cryogen.type` `set_contains` requirement uses `{"x": ...}`. The code reads `"needed": [...]`, so these fail validation and would raise a KeyError in `serialize.py`. The fixed constraints are in `fixed_value`. The six are:
- `sci_pdga_quantum_oscillations_18t#6`
- `sci_arpes_gold_fermi_edge#6`
- `sci_ltstm_nbse2_atomic#6`
- `sci_epr_ethe1_iron#4`
- `sci_cryocrystallography_100k#2` (liquid nitrogen)

That is five profiles; the sixth is the remaining optional liquid-helium requirement in the same group. Separately, no seeded cryostat in `data/cryostats` declares `cryogen.type`, so these optional checks will come back unknown there. The `research/v4` equipment files do use it.

**Rejected (1):** `sci_epr_ethe1_iron#2` makes the exact 9.48 GHz X-band point mandatory. The same paper's Methods used 9.63 GHz on a second spectrometer, and the frequency is set by cavity tuning. It should be optional or an X-band interval.

**Smaller points (accepted):**
- The ARPES 1e-10 mbar quote says pumps are "typically used" to reach it.
- The PdGa 4 mA is an rms value; the peak is 5.66 mA.
- The dilatometer's electrical-leads requirement is inferred from its capacitance readout, not stated outright.

**Duplicates:**
- `sci_cryocrystallography_100k` duplicates `bio_mx_cryocrystallography_100k` and `chem_scxrd_cryostream_100k` in `research/v4`.
- `sci_ltstm_nbse2_atomic` is effectively the same measurement as `mat_lt_stm_fe_adatoms_bi2te3`.

**Not flagged:** `sci_hg1223_magnetization_loops` overlaps `data/experiments/mat_magnetometry_vsm.json` (VSM M-T and M-H) and `research/v4` `mat_zfc_fc_magnetite_nanoparticles` (ZFC/FC and loops). Its sweep-rate dynamic-relaxation study and the need to reach at least 129 K set it apart. None of the 10 plain_names is identical to an existing one.

The quote is there, but it only shows how the sample is cooled. It does not say the sample space cannot be evacuated. The same document (p.7, Oven) says the oven option adds 'a turbo pump unit for generating high vacuum in the sample chamber'. So vacuum is an existing option, and the repo convention (PPMS classic, TeslatronPT) would be flag true / optional_not_installed, not false / installed.

This absence is inferred from the cooling description. It is not an explicit statement or a complete spec. The oven option evacuates the sample chamber with a turbo pump, so 'no base pressure exists' is wrong. At most it is optional_not_installed with an unknown value.

Brochure 1500-103 Rev. E1 p.10 has the FOSH quote verbatim, and M320 is listed. Note the compatibility table on p.14: FOSH works with DC Scan but NOT with SQUID-VSM, so optical and VSM measurements cannot run together.

'Sample chamber I.D. 9 mm' is the bore of the temperature-control insert ('9 mm sample bore'), not the largest sample. The repo stores bores as sample.bore_diameter (see the PPMS 25 mm). 'Liquid helium usage 4 L/day (typical) + 0.05 L per sample cooldown'. The non-EverCool base consumes liquid helium.

Same quote; 1.7 K.

Rests on the complete §5.1 technical data and component list (coldhead, controller, gas pump, AD51, Varibeam, ES60 dewar), which has no magnet, plus the §4 intended use (open gas stream on a sub-mm3 crystal). Acceptable as a complete specification.
§4 explicitly says: 'The nozzle is not designed to be enclosed or to cool samples that are enclosed inside any kind of sample holder, chamber or vessel.'
The absence rests on the same explicit statement: open stream of gas, never enclosed. So there is no evacuated sample space.

The §6.10 crosshairs quote is verbatim. The sample sits unenclosed in open air and is viewed by the diffractometer telescope or camera. Acceptable, though optical access is inherent to the open geometry rather than a Cryostream component.
The complete technical data and component list has no sample wiring or feedthrough. The intended use (crystal in an open gas stream, not in any holder or chamber) supports the absence.

'Centre 2 mm of the gas stream' is a positioning tolerance, not a sample-size limit. §4 limits the sample to 'less than 1mm3', and a 2 mm-diameter crystal would exceed that (a 2 mm sphere is about 4.2 mm3). This overstates the capability.
'Liquid Nitrogen Consumption 0.6 litres/hour at 5 litres/minute gas flow'.
§4: 'To be used with liquid nitrogen only.'
0.6 L/h = exactly 0.01 L/min at the 5 L/min flow, as documented. At 10 L/min it is 1.2 L/h (0.02 L/min), so the stored value applies to the normal 5 L/min flow.
'Nitrogen Gas Flow Rate 5 or 10 litres/minute'; max 10 L/min.

3He sorption refrigerator: 'Extension of sample temperature range to below 280 mK of existing or new VTI's'.
ProteoxMX brochure Key Specifications: 'Temperature control range 10 mK to 30 K with magnet at full field'.
'Base temperature < 10 mK' (also on p.6). Stored as 10 mK, which is conservative.
Family brochure MX450 column: '± 1 mK < 100 mK, ± 1 % > 100 mK'.
'> 12 µW cooling power available at 20 mK' (MX brochure), and MX450 '> 12 µW' in the family brochure. 12000 nW correct.
Family brochure MX450: 'Guaranteed: > 450 µW', 'Expected: > 500 µW'. The guaranteed value is used. 450000 nW correct.
'Magnet options Solenoid: up to 14 T' and 'Standard solenoid 1T to 14T'. 14000 mT.
Solenoid magnets: 'Central field homogeneity of 0.1 % over 10 mm D.S.V across the range' = 1000 ppm.
Customised Magnets lists 'Split pair configurations for optical access'. It exists as a bespoke option and is not in the solenoid configuration, so optional_not_installed is correct.
'Up to 28 RF and 96 DC connections on a single sample puck'. Every bottom-loader puck option carries 96 DC lines, so the flag holds whichever puck fits the 14 T magnet.
Both puck options (60 mm and 72 mm) carry 96 DC, so 96 holds regardless of which puck the 14 T magnet accepts.

Bottom-loader options are '60 mm, 96 DC, 22 coax / 72 mm, 96 DC, 28 coax / Dependent on magnet selection'. Solenoid bores run 77-150 mm across 1-14 T, and the magnet table only says 'Up to 14 T ... Puck Dia. Up to 72'. Nothing documents that the 14 T solenoid takes the 72 mm, 28-coax puck. The 14 T + 72 mm configuration is undocumented, so 28 is not supported. At best it is 22 with the 60 mm puck, and that fit is unconfirmed too.

72 mm is the puck diameter, not the largest sample, and the 14 T + 72 mm puck pairing is 'Dependent on magnet selection' and undocumented. This matches the known gap: no documented puck sample limit, so it should stay unknown.
The brochure title is 'ProteoxMX Cryofree dilution refrigerator', and it is pulse-tube (PTR) cooled.

Datasheet p.2, ST-500 column: 'Temperature range 3.5 K to 475 K'.

'Typical temperature stability ±50 mK' (one row covering all models, measured with the temperature controller). This is a typical value, as the configuration says.

Key features: 'Sample in vacuum'.
'Typical base pressure during operation ~10-5 Torr', stored as '0.00001' Torr. Torr is registered.
Optical microscopy cryostat with selectable top windows (fused silica, ZnSe, sapphire, CaF2). The quote is verbatim.
'We offer a variety of both unwired and wired feedthroughs'. Wired is an option; this configuration is unwired.
'Sample mount diameter 19.05 mm (0.75 in)' for the ST-500. The bore (inner diameter at the sample region) is 73 mm, so the mount diameter is the tighter, conservative sample bound.
'Cryogen consumption (LHe at 5 K) 1.1 L/h'. Infinite Helium (cryogen-free) is an optional add-on and is not fitted.
Consumption rows for LHe and for 'LN2 at 80 K 0.1 L/h', and 'High-efficiency, flexible LHe/LN2 transfer line'.
'Nominal vibration amplitude <12 nm', measured on a vibration isolation table.

The datasheet says 'temperature range 1.65 .. 300 K', but 'base temperature 1.65 .. 1.8 K (for standard inserts)' depends on the insert. The configuration itself uses the conservative 1.8 K base, so range.lo is raised to 1800 mK to match.
'base temperature 1.65 .. 1.8 K (for standard inserts)'. 1.8 K is conservative.
'< ± 10 mK guaranteed (1.5 .. 10 K)'.

The sample runs in 'He exchange gas', but the datasheet lists an optional 'pumping kit turbomolecular pump with suitable backing pump for sample space preparation', so the sample space can be evacuated. The repo convention (PPMS, TeslatronPT) would be flag true / optional_not_installed, or at least not an installed 'false'.

No base pressure is specified, but the sample space is pumped by the optional turbo kit. 'Exchange gas' describes the operating atmosphere; it does not show that no evacuated state exists. This should be unknown, not a documented absence.
'designed for magneto-optical applications'. Compatibility: confocal microscopes attoCFM I, attoCFM IV. The attoCFM I is installed.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source and re-read the text, either from the PDFs (curl plus pdftotext) or from the Anton Paar page fetched with curl. Of 107 capabilities across 8 machines, I accepted 94 (one with a corrected value) and rejected 13.

Value corrected:
- attoDRY2100 temperature.range: I raised the lower end to 1800 mK so it matches the configuration's own conservative 1.8 K base.

Rejected, and why:
- **Bore stored as largest sample size** (MPMS3 9 mm, HelioxVT 25 mm, attoDRY2100 48 mm). These are chamber or insert inner diameters. The repo stores those as sample.bore_diameter, not sample.diameter.max.
- **Cryostream sample.diameter.max (2 mm)**: this is a positioning tolerance. The manual limits the sample to less than 1 mm3.
- **Proteox MX450 coax lines (28) and sample.diameter.max (72 mm)**: the brochure says puck choice is "Dependent on magnet selection", and nothing shows the 14 T solenoid takes the 72 mm puck. This matches the known 14 T gap: no documented puck sample limit.
- **"No vacuum" on MPMS3 and attoDRY2100** (vacuum.available false, pressure.base not_available). Both systems offer optional turbo-pumping of the sample space: the MPMS3 through its oven option, the attoDRY2100 through its pumping kit. By repo convention that is flag true / optional_not_installed.
- **HelioxVT magnet marked not_available**: the same guide offers integration with split-pair magnets and a sample holder for high-field magnets, so a magnet is an option.
- **TTK 600 magnet marked not_available**: this rests only on the silence of the product page and a short spec list.

Accepted, worth knowing:
- MPMS3: the fibre-optic sample holder (FOSH) cannot be used with SQUID-VSM mode, so optical and VSM measurements can't run together.

Duplicates: none of the 8 is in data/cryostats. Six of them (all but HelioxVT and ST-500) already appear in other research/v4 industry equipment files. The Cryostream 800 and TTK 600 even reuse identical configuration ids there.

exp.notes: Wrote C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\healthcare_and_medicine\experiments.json (10 profiles; each requirement there also carries evidence_status and accessed=2026-11-01). Celsius converted exactly to mK. Mandatory requirements use core-passport keys wherever possible (temperature.range, temperature.base, cryogen.type, vacuum.available, magnetic_field.max, sample.diameter.max), plus the new v4 keys temperature.cooling_rate.range and holding_time.static and the existing module.magnetic_shielding. Storage procedures use temperature.range at_most X: the machine must reach X or colder. The mRNA vaccine window from -90 C to -60 C is written as at_most -60 C plus at_least -90 C, so the machine range must overlap the window. Psi values (4,300 and 2,200 psi in the cryoablation paper) appear only in quotes and were not converted. Not duplicated: the existing profiles for Cryotop oocyte vitrification, intercostal cryoneurolysis, breast-cell freeze-thaw, PBMC controlled-rate freezing (bio) and OCT cryosectioning (bio). A CAR-T leukapheresis protocol (1 C/min to -80 C) was dropped because it would nearly duplicate the PBMC profile. Philips BlueSeal 1.5 T was replaced by the Siemens MAGNETOM Free.Max because the Philips documents give no bore diameter. Caveats: (1) The Tavily quota was exhausted. Sources were read with WebFetch, pdftotext on the fetched PDFs, and Europe PMC full text. The quotes from the renal-cryoablation paper (PMC4041687, author manuscript) came through WebFetch's extraction, not raw text, so they should be spot-checked. (2) The AABB Circular text layer shows the temperature as '−18 C' and '−65 C' without a degree sign. The page numbers given are PDF pages, not printed page numbers. (3) The cord-blood and RBC sources do not name the freezer or tank models; reported_equipment says so. eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\healthcare_and_medicine\equipment.json (identical content). 8 configurations in 7 equipment entries from 4 manufacturers (MVE Biological Solutions, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Epredia, Helmer Scientific). NIST is used only as reference data. None of them duplicates a catalog machine. Catalog sources were accessed on 2026-11-01. Every configuration documents all 11 core-passport keys. The one gap is sample.height.max for the Epredia CryoStar NX70: no source states a maximum specimen height, so it is recorded as unknown and listed in not_found. Absences (magnet, sample vacuum, base pressure, viewport, sample wiring) are install=not_available. Each quotes the complete spec sheet or technical-data section that sets the machine's scope. Temperature conventions: (1) A single stated storage temperature gives lo = hi. The MVE HEco uses its -190 C top-box value. (2) The XC 47/11 uses the LN2 normal boiling point, 77.34 K, from NIST, because MVE documents only 'liquid storage' with no number. (3) The vapour shippers use the -150 to -190 C range from the MVE manual. Size conventions: (1) Front-loading CryoMed controlled-rate freezer: diameter is the smaller cross-section perpendicular to loading (30.5 cm height); height is the depth along the loading axis (33 cm). (2) Upright freezers follow the family mapping: diameter is the smaller of interior width and depth; height is the interior height. Conservative choices: (1) XC 47/11-6 straw and vial counts disagree between the 2024 spec sheet (4,500+ straws per cane, 6,216 in bulk) and the MVE product page (3900+ straws, 1320 vials). The lower cane-inventory figures are used. (2) CryoMed 48 L vial capacity is 1,185, not 1,195. Not recorded: (1) HEco static hold time, because the source gives only a 'typical performance' graph. (2) XC 47/11 static hold time, because the source gives only a nominal evaporation rate and a working duration it calls arbitrary. The consumption rate is stored instead, rounded up to 0.000271 L/min. Considered but excluded because core keys could not be sourced: (1) Philips BlueSeal 1.5 T sealed MRI magnet. Its brochure documents a 1.5 T field, 70 cm bore and about 7 L of sealed helium that never needs refilling, but gives no patient-bore temperature, vacuum or viewport data. (2) Cytiva VIA Freeze Quad, because no manufacturer datasheet could be reached. Quotes from PDFs come from text extracted from the manufacturers' PDFs. The Thermo TSX and Fisher NX70 quotes are rows of the web specification tables, written as 'Name: value'. The CryoMed medical-device brochure is hosted on a Thermo Fisher China asset server (qa1-assets.thermofisher.cn).

results.note: Verified on PMC11214401 (Ellison et al. 2024): Kryo 560-16 program, 4 C hold for 5 min, ramps of -1/-2/-20 C/min to -180 C. range_within -180..+4 C (93150..277150 mK) is correct and mandatory is justified.
Same quote verified. Cooling-rate magnitudes of 1, 2 and 20 C/min give 1000..20000 mK_per_min, which is correct. The key temperature.cooling_rate.range is in the vocabulary.
Verified: 'Hold at −180°C until unloaded into VPLN upon completion of program.' -180 C = 93150 mK. Non-mandatory and redundant with #0, which is fine.

Verified: product of 20 ± 2.5 mL stored in VPLN at -130 C or less (143150 mK). This describes the later storage step, not the freezer, and is implied by #0. It is acceptable only because it is non-mandatory.

Verified in the full text (Europe PMC XML of PMC13505624): 'After cryoprotectant addition, units underwent controlled-rate freezing and were stored in the liquid phase of liquid nitrogen at −196 °C.' point_within 77150 mK is correct.
Same verified sentence. Liquid-phase LN2 storage justifies set_contains liquid_nitrogen as mandatory.

Verified word for word in the Discussion: glass transition of water at about -130 C, so cells 'can theoretically be stored indefinitely.' 143150 mK is correct. This is physical background, so non-mandatory is right.

Verified in the Ontario PDF v8.0 (Oct 22, 2024), Table 2, page 3: 'Store at ultra-low temperature freezer at -90oC to -60oC until printed expiry date or otherwise noted.' at_most -60 C (213150 mK) on a range means lo <= -60 C, which is correct.
Same quote. at_least 183150 mK on a range means hi >= -90 C. Together with #0 this correctly requires the range to overlap the -90..-60 C window, as the code shows (smt.py _value_formula).

Quote verified, but the location is wrong. 'Vaccines placed in an ULT portable unit (-90°C to -60°C) can go back into an ULT unit.' is on page 7 of the PDF, not page 6. The value is correct and the requirement is non-mandatory.
Verified against the PubMed 15318853 abstract (Background): 40% wt/vol glycerol RBCs approved by FDA/AABB for storage at -80 C for up to 10 years. point_within 193150 mK is correct.

Verified in the AABB Circular of Information, PDF page 21: 'FROZEN RED BLOOD CELLS and FROZEN REJUVENATED RED BLOOD CELLS are prepared by adding glycerol ... before freezing at −65 C or colder.' at_most 208150 mK is correct.
Verified in the abstract, Study design and methods: 20 RBC units in 40% glycerol stored at -80 C for up to 22 years. Non-mandatory base <= 193150 mK is correct.
Verified on PMC6580834 (Dhantole et al. 2019), Discussion: core temperature -30 C or below within 1 h preserves factor VIII. at_most 243150 mK is correct.
Verified in the AABB Circular, Fresh Frozen Plasma description, PDF page 24: FFP frozen at −18 C or colder. at_most 255150 mK is correct.
Verified in Materials and methods: CSF Dometic MBF 21, stored at −40°C in stack position for 2 weeks in a Sanyo deep freezer. point_within 233150 mK, non-mandatory, is correct.
Verified in the Discussion: CSF operating temperature −50°C, core reached −30°C in 40 min. Non-mandatory base <= 223150 mK is correct.

The quote is in Section 3.1, but it describes the reliquefier COLD HEAD cooling to 4.2 K in about 5 h, not the SQUID sensors. The steady cold-head temperature is 4.06 K. The sensors are cooled by the LHe helmet; the abstract says 'direct thermal contact with the liquid helium helmet.' Fix: cite the abstract sentence about low-temperature SQUID gradiometers in thermal contact with the LHe helmet. Use at_most 4200 mK (the machine must reach LHe temperature) instead of point_within on a cold-head figure.

Verified in the abstract of Lee et al., SUST 30 (2017) 084003: gradiometers in the vacuum space of the helmet dewar, in direct thermal contact with the liquid helium helmet. set_contains liquid_helium, mandatory, is justified.

Quote verified ('Sources of magnetic noises measured by SQUID gradiometers inside the MSR can be divided into three major parts'), but it is in Section 3.2, not Section 4. The MSR (two Mumetal layers) is clearly part of the setup, so magnetic_shielding present, mandatory, is justified.
Verified in Section 2.1: Cryomech PT415RM, 1.4 W at 4.2 K. W converts to the vocabulary unit nW. Informative and non-mandatory, which is fine.
Verified in Section 3.1: reservoir capacity of 90 l, boil-off 13–14 l/day. at_least 90 L, non-mandatory, is correct.
Verified in the Siemens flyer text, page 2: '... pulmonary imaging, guided intervention and therapy with a 0.55 T field strength.' at_least 550 mT is correct.

Verified on page 2: an 80 cm bore can accommodate obese, severely claustrophobic and anxious patients, and children. at_least 80 cm on sample.diameter.max (um) converts exactly. Mandatory is acceptable because the procedure is defined by patients who need the 80 cm bore.
Verified: 'Accommodate very large patients with 320 kg table load option.' Non-mandatory at_least 320 kg is correct (kg converts to ug).

The quote is there ('DryCool technology, operating on < 700 ml of helium, and no quench pipe'), but it does not say the helium is liquid. The same flyer also calls the system a 'helium-free infrastructure'. The rationale itself says the procedure does not need helium, so adding set_contains liquid_helium, even as non-mandatory, would wrongly favour helium-using machines. Drop this requirement or move the fact to reported_conditions.

Verified in the PMC4041687 full text (NCBI E-utilities), Materials and methods: 'A Presice™ Cryoablation System was used with argon gas at 4,300 psi.' compressed_argon_jt is a v4 vocabulary token. Mandatory is acceptable because the procedure is defined as argon JT cryoablation.

Quote verified ('Active thaw with helium gas at 2,200 psi was then given until the same sensor showed 0C.'). However, mandatory is not justified: the procedure needs an active thaw, and helium JT is only how this system does it; electrically heated thaw systems would do the same job. Set mandatory=false. The constraint itself (set_contains compressed_helium_jt) is fine.

Quote verified, but its location is wrong. It is in Materials and methods ('According to manufacturer recommendations at the end of the second 10-minute freeze cycle the IceRod attains −40C in a 16 × 41 mm area...'), not the Discussion. at_most 233150 mK is correct.
Verified in the abstract and methods: 'Time based trials consisted of a double 10-minute freeze separated by a 5-minute thaw.' at_least 10 min, non-mandatory, is correct (converts to s).

Verified on PMC12559775 (Karppinen et al., Obesity 2025): 'Supervised sessions included brief precooling in −30°C and −60°C chambers, followed by 3–4 min in a −110°C chamber.' range_within 163150..243150 mK is correct. Equipment: Univers Cryo-Combi three-chamber system.

Verified in the Introduction: brief exposures (1–4 min) to extremely cold air (−110°C to −160°C). A person breathing cold air rules out an evacuated space, so vacuum.available absent is a reasonable proxy. pressure.operating.range would express it more directly.

Verified on PMC12608988 (Ritter et al. 2025): 'The majority of the cryotherapy takes place in the third, at approximately −110 °C up to 3 min.' Non-mandatory base <= 163150 mK is correct. Note that this centre's first chamber is about -16 C.
Verified on PMC11255121 (Kumar et al., Regen Ther 2024): 'The temperature had to be lower than −130 °C throughout the transport.' at_most 143150 mK is correct and mandatory.

Verified: three transits took 56 h 12 min, 76 h 17 min and 178 h (7 days), and arrival temperatures were -193/-194 C, so the shipper held for at least 178 h. The key holding_time.static (unit h) is defined only in research/v4/vocabulary.json new_keys and is not yet in data/capability_vocabulary.json. It must be promoted before build-db.
Verified: transport 'in the vapour phase of liquid nitrogen in a dry shipper provided by the courier at less than −150 °C'. set_contains liquid_nitrogen is justified.
Verified: 'The dry shipper can keep a temperature of at least −150 °C over 12 days, as has been validated by the courier.' at_most 123150 mK, non-mandatory, is correct.

vexp.summary:
I checked all 35 requirements in the 10 Healthcare and medicine profiles against their sources. 31 are accepted and 4 rejected. Duplicates: none were found among these 10 or against the 60 data/experiments profiles. The closest existing profile is expansion_b_bio_pbmc_controlled_freezing, which uses a different cell product and freezing program.

Rejected:
1. **med_meg_reliquefier_squid#0**: the 4.2 K quote is about the reliquefier cold head cooling down, not the SQUID sensors. Suggested fix: at_most 4200 mK, citing the abstract sentence about the liquid-helium helmet.
2. **med_wide_bore_low_helium_mri#3**: the flyer does not say the helium is liquid and calls the system 'helium-free infrastructure'. Drop the requirement.
3. **med_renal_argon_cryoablation#1**: helium thaw should not be mandatory. The procedure needs an active thaw, and helium is just how this system provides it. Set mandatory to false.

Location fixes on accepted items:
- **Ontario PDF:** the ULT portable unit sentence is on page 7, not page 6.
- **MEG paper:** the MSR sentence is in Section 3.2, not Section 4.
- **Renal paper:** the IceRod -40 C sentence is in Materials and methods, not the Discussion.

Also, holding_time.static is defined only in research/v4/vocabulary.json and is not yet in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so it must be added there before build-db.

How sources were checked:
- **PMC articles:** via WebFetch, plus Europe PMC full-text XML and NCBI E-utilities.
- **PDFs** (Ontario, AABB, Siemens, Lee et al. 2017): extracted locally with pdftotext.
- **Lecak et al. RBC abstract:** fetched from PubMed E-utilities.

Tavily was unavailable because the plan's usage limit was exceeded.

experiments.name: Blot-and-plunge vitrification of protein cryo-EM grids in a Vitrobot Mark IV (4 °C, 100% RH, liquid ethane cooled by liquid nitrogen)
experiments.plain_name: Flash-freeze purified protein on a grid in liquid ethane
experiments.description: A 3 mm EM grid carrying a few microlitres of purified protein is blotted inside a humidity- and temperature-controlled chamber (4 °C, 100% relative humidity) and plunged into liquid ethane held in a liquid-nitrogen-cooled cup, producing a vitreous ice film for single-particle cryo-EM.

requirements.rationale: The environmental chamber is held at 100% relative humidity so the thin sample film does not evaporate before plunging.
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.location: Methods, 'Preparation of biological specimens for cryo-EM single particle analysis'

requirements.quote: blotted for 10 s with blot force + 7 before plunge-freezing in liquid ethane using a Vitrobot Mark IV (ThermoScientific) with the environmental chamber set to 4 °C and 100% humidity.

requirements.rationale: Vitrification requires plunging into liquid ethane, the rapid cryogen held in the brass cup.

requirements.location: Section 4.2 'Cooling the Ethane', safety note, page 2 of 4
requirements.quote: Liquid ethane is a rapid cryogen and can burn and cause damage to your skin and eyes.

requirements.rationale: The ethane cup is cooled by liquid nitrogen in the foam base, and finished grids go into liquid-nitrogen storage.
requirements.document_title: Common Vitrobot Standard Operating Procedure, version 1.2 (MBSOP_VBOT_1020_1-2), Hecksel, Mulligan, Zimanyi; NCCAT CryoEM Merit Badges

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 biology_and_biotechnology experiment profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\biology_and_biotechnology\experiments.json. The file format is {industry, accessed: 2026-11-01, experiments, notes}, the same layout the materials agent used. Each requirement in the file also carries evidence_status and accessed.

Checks run:
- All 39 quotes come from full texts or PDFs I actually fetched, and none is longer than 50 words.
- Quotes from Europe PMC papers were checked programmatically as exact substrings of the JATS XML text. They all match after one Krios quote was trimmed.
- Quotes from the NCCAT Vitrobot SOP and the SPEX handbook were checked against the PDF text layer. The SPEX quote uses "-80º C" with the ordinal symbol, exactly as printed.
- The Addgene quotes were confirmed verbatim through WebFetch only, because a direct curl was blocked.
- Every key exists in data/capability_vocabulary.json or the v4 new_keys, and every constraint kind fits its key's shape.
- All units are allowed symbols and passed cryolean.units.to_si. All plain_names are unique, and none repeats an existing profile.

Decisions to review:
1. Temperature requirements use the procedure's own operating point:
   - Vitrobot: 4 °C. The NCCAT SOP says 4-22 °C is typical, but both papers report 4 °C.
   - Krios: about 80 K. Cryo-FIB: -180 °C. MX: 100 K. Freezer/Mill: about -196 °C. Glycerol stocks: -80 °C.
   - A machine whose documented range misses that point will get DOES_NOT_MEET. For example, an LN2 dewar fails the -80 °C glycerol-stock storage requirement because the protocol states -80 °C.
2. The requirement that electron-beam work happens in vacuum (Krios and cryo-FIB) and the 3 mm grid size are both sourced to the Introduction and Discussion of Zhang et al. 2025, marked as reference_data.
3. The freeze-substitution warming rate of 10 °C/h is 166.67 mK/min, which does not terminate. I rounded the requirement up to 167 and made it non-mandatory.
4. The Tokuyasu block size of about 1 mm cubed became a circumscribed diameter of 1.42 mm, non-mandatory.
5. The Aquilos 2 datasheet (DS0303) is listed only as an equipment reference. Useful capability values it gives for the equipment agent: "Fully rotatable cryo-stage (<-170°C at the sample)" and "Chamber vacuum at cryo-conditions: <8e−5Pa".
6. Several mandatory requirements use family keys that most machines will not document: humidity.range, pressure.max_working, section_thickness.range, temperature.condenser.min. Plunge freezers, high-pressure freezers, cryo-ultramicrotomes and freeze dryers need these documented, or those pairs will come out NEED_MORE_INFORMATION.

Tools and process:
- Tavily was over its plan limit, so I read sources through WebFetch and the Europe PMC REST API instead.
- PDFs that WebFetch saved under the session tool-results folder were read with pymupdf/pdftotext. I did not run any separate downloads.
- Another agent overwrote a helper script in the shared scratchpad, so my scripts are in scratchpad\biobio\ (build_bio.py builds the file).

Not used:
- The academia.edu freeze-drying source and the ResearchGate Tokuyasu source from the idea list could not be read. I replaced them with Bodzen et al. 2021 (BMC Biotechnology) and De Mazière et al. 2022 (Autophagy).
- I dropped the NMR cryoprobe idea. The sample in that experiment sits at room temperature, so its requirements would not map onto the passport keys.

eq.notes: Output written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\biology_and_biotechnology\equipment.json (same content as this result). 8 configurations from 7 manufacturers: Thermo Fisher Scientific (Vitrobot Mark IV, CryoStar NX70), Leica Microsystems (EM GP2, EM AFS2), Oxford Cryosystems (Cryostream 800), Chart/MVE (HEco 815P-190), PHC (MDF-DU702VH), Martin Christ (Epsilon 2-4 LSCplus). None of them is already in the catalog (Leica CM1950, Planer Kryo 560, Retsch CryoMill, Labconco FreeZone 6 and Kitazato Cryotop are there). Temperatures are converted exactly from Celsius ((C+273.15)x1000 mK). An absence (install not_available) is recorded only where a complete technical specification or component list exists, such as a manual's technical-data chapter or a data sheet. The Leica EM AFS2 has only a brochure, so its magnet and sample-wiring entries stay unknown. For the plunge freezers, humidity control starts at room humidity, so the lower bound recorded is the manufacturer's maximum allowed room humidity (85 % for the Vitrobot, 55 % for the EM GP2). The MVE vapour-phase LN2 storage temperature is the stated -190 C top-box value (lo = hi). The Christ final vacuum (about 0.005 mbar) depends on the pump. Not covered because no reachable full specification was found: Leica EM ICE high-pressure freezer (the brochure and spec page give no pressure, temperature or carrier data), Leica EM FC7 cryo-ultramicrotome (the manual is over 10 MB and the brochure's technical pages could not be retrieved), SPEX Freezer/Mill (the electromagnetic coil field at the vial is not specified, so a magnet absence cannot be claimed) and Thermo CryoMed controlled-rate freezer (manual not retrievable). Tavily was unavailable (plan usage limit), so sources were read with WebFetch and pdftotext. The built-in browser pane is shared with other agents and was not used for evidence. accessed = 2026-11-01. Most remaining gaps are sample size on the grid and freeze-substitution machines (grid diameter is not printed in either plunge-freezer manual). Experiment writers should prefer temperature/humidity/cryogen.type requirements for those machines.

results.note: Quote is in the source (Zhang et al. 2025, PMC12227703). The value of 100% RH is right, and so is mandatory. But 'humidity.range' is not a key in data/capability_vocabulary.json (185 established keys, none for humidity), so no equipment can match it. Add a humidity.range key (range, percent) to the vocabulary first, then re-submit.

Quote is in the source (Gemin et al. 2024, PMC11461667): Vitrobot Mark IV, chamber at 4 °C and 100% humidity. The NCCAT SOP section 4.1.7.3 also gives 'temperature 4 °C - 22 °C'. 277150 mK is correct. temperature.chamber.range would be a more precise key for the environmental chamber, but temperature.range is defensible.

Quote is in the NCCAT Vitrobot SOP v1.2, section 4.2 safety note, page 2. Liquid ethane is the vitrification cryogen, so mandatory is justified. No equipment record uses cryogen.type yet, so the token 'liquid_ethane' needs to match whatever naming the equipment records adopt.
Quote is in the SOP, step 4.2.2, page 2 of 4. Liquid nitrogen cools the ethane cup, so mandatory is justified.
Quote is in the Discussion of Zhang et al. 2025 ('standard EM grid of 3 mm diameter'). at_least 3 mm on sample.diameter.max (max shape, um) is consistent.
Profile-level acceptance; see per-requirement entries below.

Quote 'The temperature of the specimen was ≈80K' is in Dickerson et al. 2024 (PMC10782223), section 2.2, on a Titan Krios G2 at 300 kV. That sentence is about the gold-foil measurement, not a biological sample, but it is the same class of microscope and specimen stage. 80000 mK is correct.
Quote is verbatim in the Introduction of Zhang et al. 2025. Vacuum is inherent to TEM imaging, so mandatory is justified.
Same verified 3 mm grid quote. Mandatory is justified because the Krios autoloader takes standard 3 mm grids (clipped into AutoGrids).
Quote is in Dickerson et al. section 2.1. Marked non-mandatory, which is appropriate.

Quote is in Watanabe 2016 (PMC4990539), and 2100 bar = 210000000 Pa is correct. But 'pressure.max_working' is not in the capability vocabulary; the only pressure keys are pressure.base, pressure.stability and pressure.operating.range. Add a key for freezing pressure first, or use pressure.operating.range with point_within 210 MPa if that key is meant to cover this.
Quote is verbatim in the Methods of Watanabe 2016. Pressurized liquid nitrogen is the freezing medium, so mandatory is justified.
Quote is in the Discussion. The Methods also confirm it ('The sapphire disk is mounted on the countersink of a 6-mm middle plate'). 6 mm is correct.

The quote is there, but it states how thick a specimen high-pressure freezing can vitrify, not how thick this specimen is. Here the cells are a monolayer on sapphire inside a 100 um spacer ring, with two 200 um spacer rings filling the rest of the carrier. A 200 um sample.height.max requirement therefore misreads a method limit as an experiment requirement.
Quote is in the Discussion ('Comparisons among three instruments'). Optical stimulation is needed only for the flash-and-freeze variant, so non-mandatory is right.
Quote is verbatim in Watanabe 2016, Methods ('-90°C for 5-30 h, 5°C/h to -20°C, 12 h at -20°C, 10°C/h to 20°C'), using a Leica AFS2. 183150-293150 mK is correct.
Quote is in Rachid et al. 2026 (PMC12884447), section 2.5, which uses a Leica AFS2 pre-cooled to -90 °C. Correct, but redundant with #0, whose range already contains 183150 mK.

vexp.summary:
I re-fetched every cited source: the 9 Europe PMC full-text XMLs, the NCCAT Vitrobot SOP PDF, the SPEX Freezer/Mill handbook PDF and the Addgene page. All 40 quotes are present, verbatim or with only whitespace, dash or citation differences, and every unit conversion checks out.

I rejected 5 requirements because of their keys or what they claim, not their quotes. Four use keys that are not in data/capability_vocabulary.json:
- humidity.range (plunge freezing #0)
- pressure.max_working (high-pressure freezing #0)
- storage.capacity.vials_2ml (glycerol stock #1)
- temperature.condenser.min (freeze-drying #3); the existing key is condenser.temperature.min

The fifth, high-pressure freezing #3 (sample.height.max of at least 200 um), takes the method's 200 um vitrification limit as if it were the experiment's specimen thickness.

Minor notes:
- Several requirements repeat another one in the same profile: freeze substitution #1, MX #1 and Freezer/Mill #1.
- Tokuyasu #3 is a derived value but is labelled experimental_observation.
- The cryo-FIB vacuum quote comes from a general TEM sentence rather than a FIB source.
- No equipment record uses cryogen.type yet, so the tokens liquid_ethane, liquid_nitrogen and dry_ice are not checked against anything.
- The freeze-drying profile lacks the process.freeze_drying flag that the existing lyophilization profiles use.

No duplicates were found within this set or against the existing data/experiments profiles; none share a measurement or a plain_name. Source texts are cached in C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\bio.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched all eight sources (seven PDFs, plus the Leica GP2 spec page and the Danaher AFS2 page) and checked them as text. 99 of 104 capabilities pass. 5 are rejected:

- **Cryostream 800, sample.diameter.max:** the 2 mm figure is where the crystal should sit in the gas stream, not a size limit. The documented limit is a volume under 1 mm3, so this should be unknown.
- **PHC MDF-DU702VH, sample.height.max:** 1400 mm is the empty cabinet height, but the configuration has 3 shelves fitted. Should be unknown.
- **PHC MDF-DU702VH, sample.mass.max:** 515 kg is the total load for the whole cabinet. Corrected to the 50 kg per-shelf limit.
- **Christ Epsilon 2-4, pressure.base:** the 0.005 mbar figure is a general statement about all Christ freeze dryers and depends on the vacuum pump, which the configuration does not name.
- **Christ Epsilon 2-4, electrical.sample_connections:** an optional wired PT100 sensor can sit in the product, so "not available" is not supported. Should be unknown.

Two values pass with caveats:
- **Leica GP2, temperature.base:** -196 C is the documented container temperature, but pure ethane or propane is solid at that point.
- **Cryostream, optical_access:** the viewing optics belong to the diffractometer; the sample is simply unenclosed.

Some PDFs scramble their tables when converted to text. For the PHC control range and the NX70 stroke, chuck and trimming values, I confirmed the column order from the raw text.

No duplicates: none of the 8 machines is already in data/cryostats, and none repeats within this batch.

Six keys used here are missing from data/capability_vocabulary.json and need adding before import: humidity.range, holding_time.static, storage.capacity.vials_2ml, chamber.volume, condenser.ice_capacity, temperature.condenser.min.

experiments.plain_name: Detect unpaired electrons in a deep-frozen catalyst sample
experiments.description: Chromium-doped silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieves are characterised by continuous-wave X-band EPR (about 9.5 GHz) with the sample cell in a liquid-nitrogen finger dewar at 77 K, and by Q-band (about 33.8 GHz) pulsed HYSCORE at 1224.1 mT and 40 K, to locate the chromium site and its coordination. experiments.name: Variable-temperature X-ray powder diffraction of a drug solvate from 293 K to 103 K in 10 K steps in a capillary
experiments.plain_name: Cool a drug powder step by step and watch its X-ray pattern change
experiments.description: Nifedipine solvates are loaded into 0.7 mm borosilicate capillaries and measured on a Cu-K-alpha-1 powder diffractometer while an open-flow nitrogen cryostream steps the temperature from 293 K down to 103 K, capturing patterns every 10 K with a 5 minute hold at each step, which reveals a phase transition at 143 K. Variable-temperature powder diffraction is the standard way to map solid-form stability of an active pharmaceutical ingredient.

requirements.rationale: The series runs continuously from room temperature (293 K) down to 103 K, so the machine must cover that whole span on one sample.
requirements.document_title: Exploring the thermal behaviour of the solvated structures of nifedipine (Acta Cryst. B 2023, 79, 164-175)
requirements.quote: captured every 10 K from 293 K down to 103 K

requirements.rationale: The lowest point of the series is 103 K; a machine that stops warmer cannot follow the low-temperature phase.

requirements.quote: captured every 10 K from 293 K down to 103 K

exp.notes:
Wrote C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\chemistry_and_pharmaceuticals\experiments.json with 10 distinct, real chemistry/pharma cryogenic procedures (53 requirements total). Nothing under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ was touched.

Coverage: matrix-isolation IR (15 K), SCXRD in a 100 K nitrogen cryostream, a full lyophilization cycle (-50 C freeze / -10 C and 180 mTorr primary / 40 C secondary), modulated DSC of a frozen formulation (-70 C equilibration, 1 C/min), cryogenic impact milling of a drug under LN2 (9 Hz, 2.5 h), continuous-flow n-BuLi chemistry at -60 C, DNP MAS NMR of an amorphous PROTAC at 100 K / 9.39 T / 264 GHz, cryogenic messenger-tagging IR ion spectroscopy (30-45 K, 2e-6 mbar), frozen-sample EPR (77 K finger dewar + 40 K pulsed at 1224.1 mT), and variable-temperature PXRD of a drug solvate (293 -> 103 K).

Decidability: every profile carries mandatory requirements on core-passport keys - temperature.range and temperature.base on all 10, plus vacuum.available and pressure.base (3 profiles), optical_access (2), sample.diameter.max (2), magnetic_field.max (2), cryogen.type (4, tokens liquid_nitrogen and dry_ice), cryogen.cryogen_free (1). Family keys were added only where the procedure genuinely needs them: process.freeze_drying, temperature.condenser.min, pressure.operating.range, process.dsc, process.cryogenic_milling, milling.frequency.range, milling.duration.max, milling.jar_volume, purge.gas, chamber.volume, rf.frequency.range, optical.transmission_range, temperature.stability, temperature.sweep_rate.max, gas.flow_rate.max.

Shape/constraint check: constraints were checked against data/capability_vocabulary.json shapes via cryolean/validation.py's SHAPE_TO_CONSTRAINTS (range -> point_within/range_within/at_least/at_most, max -> at_least, min -> at_most, flag -> present/flag_is, set -> set_contains). set_contains uses the field name "needed" (a list), as cryolean/serialize.py and lean/CryoLean/Json.lean require - not "x".

Units: all temperatures in mK with exact Celsius conversion ((C+273.15)*1000: -196 C = 77150, -70 C = 203150, -60 C = 213150, -50 C = 223150, -10 C = 263150, 40 C = 313150, 100 C = 373150). 4000-400 cm-1 converted exactly to 2500-25000 nm. 180 mTorr written as 0.18 Torr; 50-200 mTorr as 0.05-0.2 Torr; 3.5e-5 mbar and 2e-6 mbar as exact decimal strings. 2.5 h = 9000 s; 20 mL = 0.02 L; 4.0 mL = 0.004 L; 3.2 mm = 3200 um; 0.7 mm = 700 um; 9.39 T = 9390 mT.

Sourcing: every number has a reachable URL (Europe PMC / PMC article pages, the Oxford Cryosystems Cryostream 800 manual PDF, and the RETSCH CryoMill technical data reproduced on AZoM), a document title, a section location, and a verbatim quote of at most 50 words containing the value. Evidence is experimental_observation for the paper procedures and manufacturer_specification for the Cryostream and CryoMill rows. No value is inferred: I deliberately dropped a DNP candidate whose field was only given as "400 MHz" and used the PROTAC paper that states 9.39 T outright, and I sourced the cryomill's -196 C from RETSCH's own technical data rather than inferring it from "immersed in liquid nitrogen".

Caveats worth a reviewer's eye: (1) two quotes are verbatim sentence fragments rather than whole sentences, because the sentences exceeded the extraction tool's length limit - "was used for temperature control at 100 K" (PMC13029089) and "a freezing step at -50 C, followed by a primary drying step at -10 C and 180 mTorr," (PMC11476828); both contain their values. (2) The Cryostream manual's technical-data rows are table cells, so the quotes pair label and value as the table prints them ("Temperature Stability 0.1 Kelvin"). (3) The lyophilization condenser and primary-drying pressure-window requirements come from the 2023 Pharm Res practical-design update rather than the cycle paper, so both are mandatory=false. (4) Tavily's quota was exhausted this session, so PDFs were read via WebFetch plus local pdftotext, and one Europe PMC fetch was refused by the extraction sub-model; I routed around it with a different source.

vexp.summary:
I re-checked all 10 chemistry_and_pharmaceuticals profiles against their sources: 13 PMC papers downloaded and text-searched, the Cryostream 800 manual PDF and the AZoM/Retsch CryoMill page. Every quote is really in its source, allowing for typography and spacing differences. 18 of the 54 requirements are rejected for wrong keys, made-up bounds, or mandatory flags the procedure does not support. Fixes, where I could give one, are in fixed_value.

Wrong or non-vocabulary keys:
- temperature.condenser.min should be the established condenser.temperature.min; its -70 C bound also comes from general advice, not this recipe.
- chamber.volume is only a research/v4 proposal and does not fit a flow reactor's coil.
- purge.gas (reagent nitrogen blanket, not a chamber purge).
- milling.jar_volume (filled from the feed-quantity spec).
- temperature.stability (filled from an mDSC modulation amplitude).

Over-strict or equipment-derived requirements:
- Liquid nitrogen marked mandatory for the 100 K single-crystal and variable-temperature powder X-ray profiles; the procedures need the temperature, not that cryogen.
- Cryostream stability and gas-flow specs presented as procedure requirements.
- 9000 s milling duration; the paper ran 12 min grinding periods with cool-downs, so 720 s is enough.

Mis-merged instruments and incomplete values:
- The EPR profile merges two spectrometers: the 40-77 K range and the 9.5-33.8 GHz range are replaced by 40-50 K and a 33.8 GHz point.
- Lyophilization base pressure must be 50 mTorr, from the same sentence's secondary-drying step.
- Lyophilization operating pressure range should be 0.05-0.18 Torr, from the recipe itself.

No duplicates: none of these profiles repeats another one here or an existing data/experiments profile, and no plain_name collides. Source texts are under C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\vchem.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source and checked it: the Cryostream, TTK 600, Christ, CryoAdvance and Bruker PDFs through text extraction (pdftotext) after WebFetch, with the Christ tables also rendered as images; the Anton Paar, Syrris and Montana pages in the built-in browser; the Rostock page with WebFetch. Tavily was unavailable because the account hit its usage limit. All quotes were found.

13 capabilities rejected:
- **Cryostream sample.diameter.max and sample.height.max (both configurations):** the "centre 2 mm" text is placement advice to avoid icing. The documented limit is sample volume under 1 mm3, so 2 mm on both axes overstates capability.
- **Cryostream electrical.sample_connections=false (both configurations):** inferred, not stated anywhere.
- **TTK 600 magnetic_field absence:** rests only on the silence of a short product-page spec table.
- **Syrris temperature.range:** the +250 °C upper limit is not shown to apply to the Cryo Controller with the low-temperature microreactor chip.
- **Syrris magnetic_field, vacuum.available and pressure.base absences:** marketing-page silence or inference only.
- **Montana magnetic_field 0.7 T option:** the value comes from a video caption about the predecessor Cryostation's Magneto-Optic module, not the CryoAdvance 50.

All other capabilities are accepted with no value corrections, and no fixed_value was needed. Checks against the tables rendered as images confirmed the Christ standard (filled-dot) PAT tools and the 2-6D standard 3-shelf row. There are no duplicates in data/cryostats; the only "ttk" grep hits are unrelated substrings in data/evidence/expansion_c.json and data/experiments/expansion_c_semiconductor_dlts.json.

experiments.name: Tension testing of structural alloys fully submerged in liquid helium (ASTM E1450, 4 K, strain rate <= 1e-3 s-1)
experiments.plain_name: Pull a metal test bar apart while it sits in liquid helium
experiments.description: Standard tensile test (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation, reduction of area) of structural alloys with the specimen fully submerged in normal liquid helium (He I) inside a cryostat, under crosshead displacement control at a nominal strain rate of 1e-3 s-1 or less. The standard designates the test temperature 4 K (He I boils at 4.2 K at sea level, 4.0 K at 1677 m).

exp.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\materials_and_nanotechnology\experiments.json (10 profiles; all keys checked to exist in data/capability_vocabulary.json or research/v4/vocabulary.json new_keys; units from the allowed list; Celsius converted exactly to mK). Sources were read in full text (open PDFs and arXiv via the alphaXiv page reader; ASTM E1450 scope from the public store page). Tavily extract was over quota and Lune's corpus had no materials papers, so neither was used. Quotes are verbatim and at most 50 words. Caveats: (1) No vocabulary key identifies the probe instrument for XRD, STM, TEM, TMA/dilatometry or PL. Those profiles rely on temperature, vacuum, optical-access, wiring and size gates, so a generic cryostat that passes them would also 'meet' them. A future module key (module.stm, module.electron_beam, module.xrd, module.dilatometer) would make them stricter. (2) The free ASTM E1450 scope gives no specimen dimensions, so that profile has no size gate. The temperature point is 4.2 K (He I at sea level, Note 1); the standard designates it 4 K. (3) The TMA sample-length (20 mm) and heating-rate (10 K/min) quotes are verbatim Russian from the original paper; the English abstract gives 130-800 K. (4) Derived sizes: Charpy diameter is the circumscribed diameter of the 5x10 mm section, rounded up to 11.19 mm; the thermal-conductivity footprint of 5x1 mm gives 5.1 mm. (5) The Ozdemir 2002 hysteresis loops (AGFM, about 15-295 K, 1.5 T) are covered by the stricter MPMS-2 SIRM cycle requirements (5-300 K, 2.5 T). (6) These profiles do not duplicate the existing expa_relaxation_heat_capacity, expc_energy_insulation_boiloff, expc_semiconductor_cryo_hall, hydrogen tensile and mat_magnetometry_vsm profiles. (7) The ASTM store page carries a notice prohibiting AI use of ASTM standards; only the short public scope text was quoted, as a citation.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\materials_and_nanotechnology\equipment.json (keys and value shapes checked against data/capability_vocabulary.json plus the v4 new_keys). It holds 8 configurations from 8 manufacturers: Quantum Design, Anton Paar, Montana Instruments, NETZSCH, Oxford Cryosystems, attocube, Cryogenic Ltd and SP Industries. None of them repeats a machine already in data/cryostats. Categories covered: SQUID magnetometer (MPMS 3), low-temperature XRD chambers (TTK 600, PheniX), optical cryostat (CryoAdvance 50), low-temperature dilatometer (DIL 402 Expedis Supreme), superconducting magnet systems with a VTI or exchange-gas sample space (CFMS 9 T, attoDRY2100 9 T), and a Charpy bath (CharpyCool CC880). No cryostat for load frames is included: Instron 3119-600 spec pages returned 403, and one Instron literature link opened a file-download dialog in the browser pane, so I did not retry it. Accessed 2026-11-01. Every value is a manufacturer specification from a datasheet or product page. PDF tables were extracted with pdftotext, and the quotes keep the printed label and value text. Some quotes join non-adjacent text with '...', and a few label-plus-value quotes are rebuilt from table cells that pdftotext split apart. Conservative choices: CryoAdvance '<3.2 K' is stored as 3.2 K. The attoDRY2100 base of '1.65 .. 1.8 K (standard inserts)' is stored as 1.8 K for both the range low end and the base. CFMS stability is stored as the worst value (50 mK at 300 K). TTK 600 '2 bar above atmospheric' is stored as 200000 Pa. CharpyCool usable depth is 22.9 cm minus the 1.9 cm stirrer, so 21.0 cm. MPMS 3, attoDRY2100 and the CFMS VTI hold the sample in helium exchange or flow gas, so they are recorded as vacuum.available=false and pressure.base=not_available, citing the sample-environment statement. For the XRD chambers, the dilatometer and the Charpy bath, the magnet, wiring and window absences cite each product's complete specification table, which lists none of them. Reviewers may prefer to downgrade these absences. TTK 600 and PheniX have only X-ray windows, so their optical_access is left in not_found rather than guessed. Options the family offers but this configuration does not fit are optional_not_installed: MPMS 3 FOSH and ETO, CryoAdvance magnet, TTK 600 battery holder, attoDRY2100 optical and transport inserts, and the CFMS optical base, heat capacity and He-3 insert. The CryoAdvance magnet and the TTK 600 battery holder are recorded this way from product-page wording ('Numerous options incl. ... magnet'; 'in-operando studies on batteries'), with no option datasheet seen. The CharpyCool entry also uses the proposed v4 key chamber.volume. Core-passport gaps (9 of 88 entries) are listed in not_found: sample.height.max on 5 configurations, pressure.base on 2 and optical_access on 2. The Tavily quota was exhausted, so sources were read with WebFetch, WebSearch and the built-in browser (read-only). WebFetch also saved the source PDFs automatically under the session tool-results folder, and pdftotext read them from there.

results.note: Verified on the ASTM store page (scope 1.2), word for word: specimen in a cryostat 'fully submerged in normal liquid helium (He I)', crosshead displacement control, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1 or less. liquid_helium is a valid cryogen.type value. Mandatory is justified because the method requires the specimen to be immersed.

Verified: the Note 1 text under scope 1.3 gives the He I boiling point as 4.2 K at sea level and 4.0 K at NIST Boulder (1677 m), and says 'In this standard the temperature is designated 4 K.' point_within 4.2 K is consistent with that.

Verified scope 1.1 word for word ('special apparatus, smaller specimens...'). module.cryogenic_tensile_test is in the vocabulary and is the key the existing expansion_a_hydrogen_304l_tensile uses, so it is consistent.

The polimi PDF URL is blocked by a Cloudflare challenge or 403 for automated fetches. Verified the same paper through Europe PMC (PMC12195355). The abstract reads 'from 25 °C to −196 °C using Charpy V-notch impact tests', and 77.15 K to 298.15 K is converted correctly. Consider adding the DOI or PMC URL as a fetchable source.
Verified in PMC full text, section 2, word for word: specimens 'soaked for more than 30 min in a cryogenic apparatus ... or in liquid nitrogen (−196 °C)'. LN2 is needed for the −196 °C condition.

The quote is verified (5 x 10 x 55 mm half-size CVN). Two problems. (1) The rationale is wrong: in a Charpy test the strike is perpendicular to the 55 mm length, which spans the anvils; it does not lie along a loading axis. (2) sample.height.max means 'height / thickness'. The 55 mm dimension is a length, so the correct key is sample.length.max at_least 55 mm ({"kind":"at_least","q":{"value":55,"unit":"mm"}} on sample.length.max). The bar can lie flat in a soak bath, so a height requirement is not justified as mandatory.

11.19 mm is derived (circumscribed diameter of 5x10 mm, sqrt(125) = 11.18). It is not stated in the source, and the 'opening perpendicular to loading' rationale has no basis in the procedure: specimens are soaked in a bath or chamber and removed with tongs. If a cross-section check is wanted, use sample.width.max at_least 10 mm and sample.height.max at_least 5 mm. As written, the requirement is not justified as mandatory.

The quote is verified (soaked >30 min). However, holding_time.static is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json; it exists only in research/v4/vocabulary.json. Its meaning there is a dewar or storage static hold time per cryogen charge, which is not what a 30-min specimen soak needs. Wrong key; drop it, or keep it only as a reported_condition.

Verified in arXiv:1801.01181 (English abstract): 'temperature range 130 to 800 K (–143 to 526 °С) using thermomechanical analyzer TMA7100'. The data points actually span 129 to 800 K, so the 130 to 800 K bound holds.

Verified on p.2 (Russian): 'три образца длиной 20 мм' (three samples 20 mm long), mounted under the quartz probe (0.2 N) per Fig. 1. In the vertical push-rod geometry the sample length is its height, so sample.height.max at_least 20 mm is acceptable. (The PDF text extraction shows the artefact 'и змеряли'.)
Verified on p.2: 'Последующий нагрев проводили со скоростью 10 K/мин.' (subsequent heating at 10 K/min). 10000 mK_per_min is converted correctly, and the requirement is optional as it should be.

Verified in the TTK 600 brochure p.1 application example: five ammonium nitrate phases from −40 °C to 135 °C, and 'The Pccn phase remains stable down to -190 °C'. 83.15 K to 408.15 K is correct. Note that the source is a manufacturer application example, not a peer-reviewed paper.

Verified on p.2: with LN2 cooling the range is −150 °C to +450 °C in dry air or inert gas and −190 °C to +600 °C in vacuum (10^-2 mbar). Reaching −190 °C therefore requires vacuum, so mandatory is justified.
Verified: the atmospheres list gives 'Vacuum 10-2 mbar'. at_most 0.01 mbar is in the right direction for pressure.base, and the requirement is optional.
Verified word for word: 'Choice between liquid nitrogen and compressed air cooling'. Optional is appropriate, because only LN2 reaches −190 °C and the source names no other method.
Verified in arXiv:0901.3891 p.5 word for word: ZFC/FC on an MPMS XL 'between 5 K and 280 K, with cooling field HFC = 100 Oe'.
Verified word for word: 'cooling ... in zero applied field (ZFC process) to the basal temperature (5 K)'.
Verified word for word: 'Low-temperature hysteresis loops (5-280 K) were obtained in applied fields up to 5 T.'

Verified in the EPSL 194 (2002) PDF, section 4 (journal p.348): SIRM 'in a field of 2.5 T at room temperature, then cooled in zero field to 5 K and back to 300 K' on an MPMS-2. The PDF renders 'fi' as the ligature ¢.
Verified; same passage (cooled to 5 K).
Verified: a 2.5 T SIRM field. The field is applied at 300 K, but the magnetometer still has to deliver 2.5 T. The hysteresis loops use 1.5 T maximum, as the rationale states.

Verified in section 3: 'Princeton Measurements Corporation AGFM (MicroMag Model 2900) with a liquid He cryostat'. The loops actually run from about 15 K to 295 K because of icing below 15 K. Optional is appropriate.

Verified in arXiv:2608.02770v2, section II Methods, word for word: 'All STM measurements were conducted at 4.5 K in an ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) system (10−11 mbar) using a CreaTec LT-STM system.' Deposition with the sample held at 4.5 K is also confirmed.
Verified: UHV is required (same sentence).
Verified: 10^-11 mbar, entered correctly as 0.00000000001 mbar. Optional.

Verified word for word: lock-in dI/dV with an 877 Hz AC bias modulation. Applying a bias to the sample needs electrical connections, so mandatory is reasonable. The profile has no STM-module requirement; the vocabulary has no such key.

The unversioned URL arxiv.org/pdf/2607.18423 now serves v2, which has a different title ('Long lived localized defect states in monolayer WSe2...'). The quoted title and passages match v1 exactly (verified at /pdf/2607.18423v1). Section 4.2 'attoDRY800 closed Helium cryostat with base temperature of 4 kelvin on sample' appears in both versions. Recommend pinning source_url to 2607.18423v1.

The v1 abstract matches word for word ('from 4 to 120 K'). v2 has the equivalent 'temperature range of 4 K to 120 K'. Pin the URL to v1. Optional is appropriate; the PL above 77 K used the LN2 Linkam cryostat, as the rationale says.
Verified in section 4.2: the 525 nm laser is focused through the objective onto the flake and the PL is collected. Optical access is mandatory.

Verified NA 0.82. The rationale is supported: v1 says 'The high-NA objective employed in the present experiment therefore permits partial collection of emission from dark excitonic species.' The objective sits inside the cryostat chamber. Optional.

Verified in arXiv:2507.12608 p.4: 'At 300 K we find that κ(T) is approximately 6-10 W/m·K.' A single range_within 7-300 K would express this better than two point_within entries, but it is acceptable as written.
Verified word for word: TmFeO3 'minimum is reached at 25 K followed by a small peak of 5.5 W/m·K at 7 K'.

Verified word for word: a 10 kΩ surface-mount resistor heater and bare-element Cernox thermometers, measured in a Quantum Design PPMS with proprietary software (so not necessarily the QD TTO module). Electrical connections are mandatory.

The quote is verified (5 mm x 1 mm x 0.5 mm). However, 5.1 mm is a derived circumscribed diameter that the source does not state, and the existing mat_* profiles express footprint through sample.length.max and sample.width.max. Use sample.length.max at_least 5 mm (and sample.width.max at_least 1 mm) instead of sample.diameter.max at_least 5.1 mm.

Verified in arXiv:2509.16730 Results: 'cool the flakes to base temperature (either 20 K or 100 K using liquid helium or liquid nitrogen cryo-TEM holders, respectively)'. The Fig. 2 flake melts at 70-90 K, so a 20 K base is required. Mandatory is justified.

Verified word for word: 'CDW transition temperature ranging between 210 K and 230 K for bulk samples'. Warming actually continues to room temperature in 10–20 K steps, so 20-230 K is a conservative minimum.
Verified word for word: 'The ultra cold liquid helium cryo-TEM holder uses continuous liquid helium flow to provide high stability...'. Optional.

vexp.summary:
I re-fetched every source for the 10 materials profiles and checked all 35 requirements: 31 accepted and 4 rejected.

**How each source was checked**
- **ASTM E1450:** read on the store page. All quotes match: full immersion in He I, 4.2 K / 4 K, and special apparatus.
- **Charpy paper:** the polimi.it PDF returns 403 or a Cloudflare challenge, so I verified it through Europe PMC (PMC12195355). Adding the DOI or PMC URL would make it fetchable.
- **Other PDFs:** downloaded to the scratchpad and text-extracted:
  - TMA arXiv 1801.01181 (Russian passages)
  - TTK 600 brochure
  - arXiv 0901.3891
  - EPSL 2002 Ozdemir paper
  - arXiv 2608.02770, 2507.12608 and 2509.16730
  - arXiv 2607.18423
- **WSe2 (arXiv 2607.18423):** the unversioned URL now serves v2, which has a different title and reworded abstract. The profile's quotes match v1 exactly, and v2 contains equivalent passages, so pin source_url to 2607.18423v1.

**Rejected requirements**
- **Charpy #2:** sample.height.max is the wrong key for the 55 mm bar length, and the "loading axis" rationale is wrong (the strike is perpendicular to the length). Use sample.length.max at least 55 mm.
- **Charpy #3:** the 11.19 mm circumscribed diameter is derived, not stated in the source, and the "opening" rationale is not justified as mandatory. Use sample.width.max at least 10 mm and sample.height.max at least 5 mm, or drop it.
- **Charpy #4:** holding_time.static is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json (only in research/v4/vocabulary.json). It also means a dewar's static hold time per cryogen charge, which is the wrong property for a 30-min specimen soak.
- **Thermal conductivity #3:** the 5.1 mm diameter is derived. Use sample.length.max at least 5 mm and sample.width.max at least 1 mm, as the existing mat_* profiles do.

**Duplicates**
- **mat_zfc_fc_magnetite_nanoparticles** duplicates the existing mat_magnetometry_vsm. Both measure M(T) and M(H) on nanoparticles, and its 5-280 K / 5 T requirements are a subset of that profile's 5-300 K / 9 T.
- **Overlaps I did not flag:**
  - The Verwey SIRM profile is also magnetite magnetometry, but its remanence-cycling protocol is different.
  - The WSe2 PL profile overlaps the existing chem_temperature_dependent_photoluminescence (4-300 K PL), but adds TRPL and high-NA collection in a different industry.
  - No identical plain_name exists.

**Gaps that are not errors**
- The STM profile has no STM-module key, because the vocabulary has none.
- The TTK profile's source is a manufacturer application example, not a peer-reviewed paper.

My first batch download used a bad directory and wrote the files into the repo root. I moved them all to the scratchpad and the repo is back to its original state.
