Datasheet 1009389: '1.65 .. 300 K (automated control)'. The standard-insert base is 1.65-1.8 K, so the lower bound of 1.8 K is conservative.
'1.65 .. 1.8 K (for standard inserts)'. 1.8 K is conservative.
Options: 'solenoids: 9 T, 12 T, vector magnets...'; max field '100 % (e.g. 9 T) @ 300 K'. The configuration includes the 9 T solenoid and bipolar supply.
Datasheet explicit: sample environment 'He exchange gas'.
Explicit He exchange-gas sample environment. The pumping kit is only for sample space preparation.
Described as 'designed for magneto-optical applications', and attoCFM I/IV are listed under Compatibility. The inserts are separate items, not included.
'transport measurements' is listed under Compatibility (separate inserts), not included.
'Ø 49 mm for components with circular segments ..., Ø 48 mm for cylindrical components'. 48 mm is conservative.
'low vibration, pulse-tube based closed-cycle cryostat'.
Closed-cycle pulse tube; no liquid cryogen.

The datasheet guarantees '< ± 10 mK' only for 1.5 .. 10 K. Stability above 10 K up to 300 K is not specified, so storing an unqualified 10 mK for the whole 1.8-300 K range is not conservative. Store it only with a 1.5-10 K range qualifier.
Spec p.1: '1.6 to 400K with continuous gas flow in VTI'.
Nominal table, CFM-9T-H3-IVTI-25: 'CFVTI Sample Base Temperature 1.6K'.
'Central field (guarantee) 9.0 Tesla' for the CFM-9T column.
The spec says continuous gas flow in the VTI for the installed VSM and transport modules. Note that the optional heated VSM probes (not fitted) are 'Sample in vacuum'.

Marked not_available, but the brochure offers sample-in-vacuum options: the heated VSM probes ('Sample in vacuum') and the relaxation heat-capacity probe ('Sample in a vacuum'). At most this is optional_not_installed with no stated base pressure, not not_available.
Brochure p.3 verbatim: 'The VTI base may, as an option, include optical access...'.
Electrical Transport section verbatim: sample platforms with different numbers of sample connections.
Verbatim except that the Ω symbols are lost in extraction: '100 n[Ω] to 1 G[Ω]'.
'The Cryogenic VSM is designed to measure DC magnetic moment.' Pick-up coils are inside the IVTI.
VSM Performance table: 'Sample size <5 mm'. Treating it as a diameter limit is reasonable.
'Cryogenic offers sensitive probes for measurements of heat capacity'. Option, not fitted.
Product page: 'Helium 3 insert for temperatures down to 300mK'. Option.
'Sample Space 25mm as standard' and 'CFVTI bore 25mm'.
'No liquid helium or nitrogen is required to operate the magnet. Only Helium gas (supplied) is required to operate the CFVTI.'
Product page key features verbatim. No liquid cryogen.
'5mK @ 10K 10mK @100K 50mK @ 300K'. The worst case, 50 mK, is stored.
'Homogeneity in 10mm dsv 0.1%' = 1000 ppm. This is the conservative figure; the brochure quotes 0.01% for the VSM option.
SP datasheet (Part 100006329 Rev 001): 'Temperature Control Range -80 °C to 30 °C'. 193150-303150 mK is correct.
'Maximum Low Temperature -80 °C'.
Complete manufacturer datasheet (performance, heat removal, electrical, dimensional, accessories) lists no magnet; the only magnetic item is the stirrer.
Explicit: specimens are immersed in a stirred liquid medium. No evacuated space is possible.
Open liquid bath; no vacuum capability.

This is an open-top liquid bath worked from above with tongs, so there may be a direct line of sight into the bath. Absence of a 'window' in the datasheet does not establish that there is no optical access. Too uncertain to store as false.
The complete datasheet's accessory list (racks, vortex breaker, tongs, comms kit) has no specimen wiring.
CC880 'Chamber Diameter 19.8 cm' (envelope).
22.9 cm chamber depth minus 1.9 cm stirrer (footnote 3) = 21.0 cm; the arithmetic is correct.
'Mechanical refrigeration eliminates costs and hazards associated with expendable refrigerants'.
Mechanical refrigeration; no LN2 or dry ice.
'Temperature Control Stability* ± 0.1 °C', based on methanol test data per the datasheet note.
'Available Bath Volumes 4L (CC480) or 8L (CC880)'.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source with curl and pdftotext (Tavily extract was over its quota) and checked each one: the MPMS 3 brochure 1500-103 Rev E1, the TTK 600 product page and leaflet, the CryoAdvance-50 datasheet and QD Europe page, the NETZSCH NGB 1022 data sheet and DIL brochure, the PheniX product page and leaflet, the attoDRY2100 datasheet, the Cryogenic CFM spec, brochure and product page, and the SP CharpyCool datasheet. The quotes, values, unit conversions and PDF page locations hold up apart from the column offsets in the extracted spec tables, which I checked by hand.

I rejected 9 capabilities:
- **TTK 600 magnetic_field.max (not_available):** the absence rests only on the silence of a short marketing spec table.
- **PheniX magnetic_field.max (not_available):** same problem.
- **PheniX electrical.sample_connections (false):** absence inferred from a marketing page's silence.
- **DIL 402 sample.height.max = 52 mm:** wrong axis. The 52 mm is length along the horizontal pushrod, and length is already in sample.length.max.
- **attoDRY2100 temperature.stability = 10 mK:** only guaranteed for 1.5-10 K, so it is not conservative across 1.8-300 K.
- **CFMS pressure.base (not_available):** the brochure offers sample-in-vacuum options (heated VSM probes and the relaxation heat-capacity probe), so at most it is optional.
- **CharpyCool optical_access (false):** it is an open-top bath, so a missing window does not prove there is no optical access.

Every other capability is accepted.

Duplicates: none. data/cryostats has no MPMS 3, TTK 600, CryoAdvance/Cryostation, DIL 402, PheniX, attoDRY2100, CFMS or CharpyCool entry. The only attocube entry is the attoDRY800 in expansion_c_thomas_qd_setup.json, a different model. No machine is repeated within this batch.

exp.notes:
Output written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\quantum_computing_and_sensing\experiments.json (10 profiles, 3-7 requirements each, accessed 2026-11-01). No files under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ were touched. All ids are new (quantum_* prefix), and all plain_names differ from each other and from the 62 existing profiles. Requirements mostly use core-passport keys: temperature.base/range, magnetic_field.max, vacuum.available, pressure.base, optical_access, electrical.sample_connections, sample.diameter.max and cryogen.cryogen_free. Established keys are added only where the physics needs them (electrical.coax_lines, coax_bandwidth.max, dc_lines, probe_arms, magnetic_field.vector, plus optional vibration.max and module.magnetic_shielding).

How the profiles differ from the suggested ideas:
(1) The Si/SiGe dots profile uses Scarlino et al. 2015 (UW-Madison/Delft, arXiv 1504.06436) instead of the Wisconsin thesis. The thesis PDF exceeded WebFetch's size limit.
(2) The NV profile uses the published PRL 128, 177401, measured at about 4 K with a (1,1,5) T vector magnet, not the 20 mK thesis. The ar5iv HTML says 'up to 55 T', which is a rendering error; the PRL PDF says 'up to 5 T', and that is what is used.
(3) Cryo-CMOS uses Beckers et al. arXiv 1904.09911: a Lakeshore CPX probe station stepped from 4.2 K to 298 K. The TU Delft JEDS PDF returned 403. Note this profile is close to the existing expc_semiconductor_native_mosfet (dipstick, 4.2-300 K), but it uses a different device, technique and source.
(4) The idea of 'chip/wafer probing of superconducting circuits at 4 K (FormFactor)' is covered by West/Tolpygo et al. arXiv 2112.00705: an HPD/FormFactor prober at 4.4 K on 200 mm wafers.
(5) The LNA profile is the Wang and Chen MDPI paper, measured on a LakeShore CRX-6.5K probe station at 15 K. Its application is radio astronomy, not qubit readout.

Caveats:
- Neyens et al. state both '1.0 K at the chuck' and '1.6 K base temperature of the cryo-prober'. The requirement uses at_most 1.6 K.
- In the heralded-amplifier paper each SNSPD is used twice, so the number of physical detectors is ambiguous. coax_lines is set to the safe lower bound of 2 (D2 and D3).
- The resonator sample.diameter.max of 8603 um is the circumscribed diameter of the stated 5 x 7 mm chip, computed by the passport rule.
- Quotes are verbatim from extracted text. A few PDF symbols (minus signs, ≈, superscripts) were normalised as pdftotext and the HTML rendered them.

Process: Tavily hit its plan usage limit after the first extract. Sources were then read with WebFetch, which saved arXiv/PRL PDF binaries to the session tool-results folder; I extracted their text with pdftotext. Two additional points:
- One PDF, the Chalmers thesis, was downloaded with curl into the session scratchpad only to extract its text, because WebFetch could not read a file over 10 MB. This departs from the 'no downloads' instruction; nothing was executed.
- The MDPI page returned 403 to WebFetch, so it was read in the built-in browser with read-only text extraction. No sign-in, cookie acceptance or form submission took place.

eq.notes:
Output written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\quantum_computing_and_sensing\equipment.json (same content as this result, plus industry and accessed fields). 8 configurations of 7 machines from 6 manufacturers (attocube, Montana Instruments, Quantum Design, kiutra, Quantum Design Oxford, Bluefors/AEM-Afore); none of them is already in data/cryostats. Every capability key is in data/capability_vocabulary.json. Each core passport key is on every configuration, either as a sourced value, a sourced absence, or a kind=unknown record that is also listed in not_found (15 gaps in total).

Sourced absences: the attoDRY800 has no magnet (in attocube's comparison table the attoDRY800(xs) column is blank on the magnet row). The OptiCool Flex has no magnet (Quantum Design says the magnet is removed and lists 'No Magnetic Field'). The attoDRY2100 has no vacuum because its sample sits in helium exchange gas, so vacuum.available is false and pressure.base is not_available.

Options not fitted (optional_not_installed): the magnet on the CryoAdvance 50 (no field value is published), the kiutra sample magnet (8 T recorded) and magnetic shielding, and the ProteoxMX magnet (14 T solenoid recorded).

Conservative values used: attoDRY2100 base 1.8 K (spec gives 1.65-1.8 K) and 10 mK guaranteed stability; OptiCool vibration 10 nm and relative stability 0.2%; CryoAdvance clear aperture 30 mm (the cold window).

OptiCool Flex size: Quantum Design prints '75 mm x 200 mm Volume', and I read it as 200 mm diameter by 75 mm height. The same table lists the 7 T model as '84 mm x 89 mm', which the spec sheet gives as 84 mm tall and 89 mm in diameter, so the order is height then diameter. The stated cavity of over 2,000 cm3 also fits: 200 x 75 mm gives 2,356 cm3, while the other reading gives 884 cm3.

The kiutra 50 mK-300 K range is quoted from the distributor Paeonia Bloch, which republishes kiutra's specifications; the base temperature comes from kiutra's own sheet.

pressure.base is the most common gap, because optical-cryostat and dilution-refrigerator makers rarely publish a sample-space pressure. The Bluefors wafer prober is the least complete (5 unknown core keys). An SNSPD system was left out because its core sample-space keys cannot be documented from the brochure.

Tavily credits ran out partway through, so the rest of the search used WebSearch, WebFetch (PDFs read locally with PyMuPDF) and direct page reads. accessed 2026-11-01.

results.note: Abstract (PDF p.5, printed p. i rather than iii) says the resonators were measured 'at a temperature of 10 mK'. at_most 10 mK is correct.
Verbatim on printed p.12 (Sec 3.1.1): the setup bandwidth is '4 GHz to 8 GHz'. 8 GHz = 8,000,000 kHz is correct.

Verbatim on printed p.12: the chip is '5 x 7 mm2'. The 8.603 mm diagonal is a derived lower bound. The sample box needs more room than this, so the constraint is necessary but not sufficient. Acceptable.
Verbatim on printed p.19 (Sec 3.4.2): wire bonded in a sample box with K connectors.
Verbatim on printed p.19 (Sec 3.4.1): cryogen-free dilution refrigerator with T < 10 mK. Marked optional, which is right.
Verbatim in the supplement 'Device and measurement technique': base temperature 25 mK, electron temperature 150 mK.
The Fig. 3 caption gives (P = 16.0 dBm, Bext = 560.783 mT, fMW = f0(3) = 6.44289 GHz). The field value matches.

6.44289 GHz is the second-harmonic drive frequency (Fig. 3a caption), and 6442890 kHz is correct. The paper also drives the fundamental at 12.88577 GHz (Fig. 3b), but this profile covers only second-harmonic driving.
The Fig. 5 caption says pulses go to gate 2 and microwaves to gate 6. Two high-frequency lines is a sound minimum.
Verbatim: two accumulation gates plus depletion gates labeled 1-10, so 12 gate lines is justified. Ohmic contacts would add more.

The requirement is justified, but the quote given only covers thermal anchoring and does not show electrical connections. Replace it with a passage that does, e.g. the Fig. 5 caption 'The current through the charge sensor is recorded in real time for a fixed voltage bias of 500 ueV' or the supplement's 'read through a room temperature I-V converter'.
Verbatim in II.1.1: trap temperatures 5.5 K at 0 V and 6.0 K at 200 V. The trap sits on the 4.2 K baseplate and runs at 6 K with 200 V RF, so point_within 6000 mK is reasonable.
Verbatim: the final working pressure on the gauge is 10^-8 torr.
Verbatim: 10^-8 torr on the bath-cryostat gauge. Torr is a supported unit in units.py. The paper says the pressure at the trap is lower still because of cryopumping, so this bound is conservative.
Verbatim: laser access through three side windows, plus a bottom window for imaging.
Verbatim: five DC control electrodes and two RF electrodes. The paper wires each DC electrode with two wires, but 5 is a valid minimum.
The electrode quote, together with the RF of 200 V at 18.45 MHz (verified), supports that electrical connections are needed.
Verbatim: maximum cold-tip displacement below 106 nm, closed-cycle variant. Marked optional, which is right.
Verbatim in the PRL main text: samples held at T ≈ 4 K in a closed-cycle refrigerator.
The same PRL sentence says 'with optical access'. Confocal 532 nm excitation is verified.
Verbatim: 'we examined I-PL(BNV) for BNV up to 5 T [25]'. 5000 mT is correct.
Verbatim: three-axis vector magnetic field control. The supplement names a (1,1,5) T vector magnet. Alignment along the NV axis justifies mandatory.
Verbatim in the arXiv supplement: microwaves are applied via a 25 um thick Al wire. Optional is correct, since this is needed only for ODMR.
Verbatim (Sec II): cooled to the 4.2 K base, then heated to 298 K in steps.

veq.summary:
I re-checked every source myself. PDFs were downloaded and their text extracted. The attoDRY brochure comparison table on p.11 is drawn with graphic dots, so I rendered that page and checked it by eye. Web pages were checked with WebFetch.

Five records are rejected; all others are accepted.

1. **attocube_attodry800_basic_shroud#magnetic_field.max** (not_available): The attoDRY800 product page offers a "Customized Permanent Magnet Shroud" with an ex-situ movable permanent magnet. A magnetic-field option therefore exists, so this should be optional_not_installed with an unknown value.
2. **quantum_design_opticool_flex_x300#vacuum.available**: The only evidence is the original OptiCool spec sheet, which does not cover the Flex model.
3. **quantum_design_opticool_flex_x300#electrical.sample_connections**: The X300 wiring option is documented only in the pre-Flex wiring document. Nothing shows it is offered on Flex.
4. **quantum_design_opticool_flex_x300#electrical.dc_lines**: Rejected for the same reason as item 3.
5. **qd_oxford_proteoxmx_iso100_no_magnet#electrical.sample_connections**: The ISO100 ports are standard, but the experimental wiring is an option or customer-specified. No wiring is part of this configuration.

Notes:
- **Value conversions:** I checked every unit conversion and all are correct: 170 mW and 130 mW to nW, 12 µW and 450 µW to nW, 20 GHz to kHz, 4.5 h and 5 h to seconds, and ±0.3% and ±0.2% to ppm.
- **OptiCool Flex dimensions:** The reading of "75 mm x 200 mm" as 75 mm high and 200 mm in diameter is consistent with the stated "over 2,000 cm3" (2356 cm3). The reverse reading (883 cm3) is not.
- **kiutra temperature range:** The 50 mK to 300 K range comes from a distributor page (Paeonia Bloch), not kiutra's own documents. evidence_status should ideally say distributor rather than manufacturer specification.
- **New keys:** cryogen.type and plate.diameter do not appear in the existing data/cryostats files.

**Duplicates:** None of these machines is duplicated in data/cryostats, and none repeats within this batch. One related record exists: data/cryostats/expansion_c_thomas_qd_setup.json (configuration expc_attodry800_qd_hbt_2024) is a published attoDRY800-based quantum-dot apparatus with a detector chain. It is not the generic attoDRY800 product configuration, so I did not list it as a duplicate. Separately, bluefors_ld.json is a different Bluefors product from the wafer prober.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 experiment profiles for physics and particle accelerators to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\physics_and_particle_accelerators\experiments.json. Each requirement also carries accessed=2026-11-01 and evidence_status=experimental_observation. I checked every quote word for word against the source text: PDFs were converted to text from the copies WebFetch saved, and the arXiv HTML pages were read with curl. Every quote is 50 words or fewer and contains its number. All keys exist in data/capability_vocabulary.json or research/v4/vocabulary.json. The ids and plain_names are unique and do not repeat any in data/experiments. Constraints follow the serializer's format, for example set_contains uses "needed". Nothing under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ was edited.

How these overlap with what already exists:
- The catalog already has expa_srf_2k_resonance (2.6 GHz dark-photon resonance control), expa_teo2_bolometer (10 mK), expa_argon_charge_scintillation, expa_cicc_critical_current and expa_magnetic_powder_neutrons. To avoid repeating them, I did not use the neutron Orange-cryostat idea or the CUORE-style 10 mK bolometer idea, and I did not reuse the LAr TPC operation idea in its original form.
- The replacements are the ADMX axion haloscope, the CUPID-Mo Li2MoO4 scintillating bolometers, the DUNE SiPM liquid-nitrogen qualification and the Nb3Sn wire minimum-quench-energy test.
- The two SRF cavity profiles are different procedures from expa_srf_2k_resonance: a bare-cavity Q0 versus gradient test in the VTS, and a dressed-cavity horizontal test at up to 300 kW.

Values I calculated rather than copied (the original numbers are in each quote):
- REBCO probe: 30 x 70 mm2 gives a circumscribed diameter of 76.2 mm.
- SiPM: 6x6 mm2 gives 8.5 mm.

Gaps and judgement calls:
- Physics-specific keys keep the NEED_MORE_INFORMATION risk on new machines: rf.frequency.range, rf.power.max, electrical.current_leads.max, chamber.volume and module.magnetic_shielding. Most machines will not document them, so any machine without them stays NEED_MORE_INFORMATION for these pairs.
- LHC dipole: the sample size (15 m long, 600 mm diameter) comes from the Rossi CERN paper, not from the test-bench paper.
- RRR: the NIST paper suggested in the task (PMC4551274) has no apparatus details. I used the Fermilab SRF2005 and JLab SRF2015 procedures instead. The 0.4 T field, the 75 mm sample length, the 100 mA current and the helium requirement are marked optional.
- Several values are marked optional because they describe the reported setup rather than a need of the procedure: ADMX cooling power of 800 uW at 100 mK, CUPID-Mo array mass, VTS 500 W RF power and VTS 1.5 K base temperature.
- CUPID-Mo crystal sizes are approximate (the source prints "∼ 44 mm" and "∼ 45 mm").
- Dimensions not documented in the sources were left out rather than guessed: VTS/HTS cavity size, Nb3Sn barrel diameter, ADMX magnet bore.
- Tavily hit its usage limit, so I used WebFetch, pdftotext and curl.
- Copies of the source PDFs are in C:\Users\Rahma\.claude\projects\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\tool-results\. They are the files WebFetch saved automatically.

eq.notes: Output written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\physics_and_particle_accelerators\equipment.json (8 configurations, 86 capabilities). 5 manufacturers: Quantum Design Oxford (ProteoxLX, ProteoxMX), Bluefors (XLDHehp, plus the Cryomech LHeP22 liquefier line), Linde Kryotechnik (L70 with and without LN2 pre-cooling), Cryofab (CMSH 100 LHe dewar), AS Scientific (ILL Orange Ø100, built under ILL licence). All sources accessed 2026-11-01. Tavily quota was exhausted, so pages and PDFs were read directly (curl + pdftotext). Absences cite complete specification sheets or scope-of-supply lists as the scope-defining quote. Gaps in not_found: pressure.base on all 3 dilution/1 K systems, sample height on both Proteox, LHeP22 liquid temperature and dewar neck, Orange sample wiring. Caveats: (1) XLDHehp temperature.range upper bound (1.2 K) is the highest specified cooling-power point, not a documented maximum. (2) The CMSH 4.2 K value is reference data (NIST NCNR statement about helium vented to atmosphere), not a Cryofab figure. (3) Linde marks its 4.4 K figures as expected performance. (4) Bluefors XLD1000sl was dropped because no reachable Bluefors source gives its upper temperature or states that its sample space is in vacuum. (5) Commercial SRF vertical test cryostats, cryomodules, magnet test benches, polarized-target refrigerators and LAr TPC cryostats are not included because no public manufacturer specifications were found. These are one-off facility builds already in the catalog as FNAL VTS, SULTAN, ITER MCTF and WARP.

results.note: Verbatim in WEPMN106 p.2283 Introduction: 'test ... SRF cavities at a nominal frequency of 1.3GHz in a 2K LHe bath'. 2000 mK point is correct.

Same verified quote ('2K LHe bath'); the test insert 'supports the cavity in the LHe bath'. liquid_helium is right. No cryostat seed documents cryogen.type values yet, so this check will come out UNKNOWN until one does.
Verified: 'nominal frequency of 1.3GHz'. rf.frequency.range is a range key in GHz, so point_within 1.3 GHz fits.
Verbatim in the Magnetic Shielding section: 'the cavity must be shielded from magnetic fields during cool down' (two-layer shield, <10 mG). The procedure requires it, so mandatory is justified.

Verbatim in the Test Stand Insert section: '1.25" thick stainless steel top plate with several penetrations for RF and instrumentation cable feedthroughs'. electrical.sample_connections is an acceptable flag for this.
Verbatim in Status & Future Plans: 'full high power (500W) test of a 9-cell ILC cavity'. 500 W is correct, and non-mandatory is appropriate.
Verbatim in SRF2007 WEP15 Introduction: 'allowing VCTF operations down to 1.5K'. This is a facility capability rather than a procedural need, so non-mandatory is the right setting.
Verbatim in TUPO055 Introduction: 'cooled to 2 K in a test cryostat'. Also 'After cooling down to 2 K' in Test Procedure.

Verbatim: 'klystron-based 300 kW pulsed RF system'. Test Procedure confirms coupler conditioning 'up to a ≈300 kW pulse with a length of 1.3 ms'. Mandatory is justified because conditioning is a procedure step.
Abstract is verbatim: 'testing of nine-cell 1.3 GHz cavities'. The procedure tunes the 'cavity resonance to 1.3 GHz'.
Verbatim in Test Procedure: 'the cavity Q0 can only be determined from the heat dissipated by the cavity walls to the helium bath.' A helium bath is required.

Verbatim in Introduction: 'outfitted with high power input couplers, higher-order mode (HOM) couplers, magnetic shielding, and a mechanical tuning system.' The flag is a reasonable proxy for coupler, HOM and tuner connections.
Verbatim in MOPLT014 Abstract: 'all the main twin-aperture dipole and quadrupole magnets are tested in the 1.9 K cryogenic conditions.'

Verbatim in Rossi arXiv:1501.07164: 'a coolant temperature of 1.9 K by using HeII ... superfluid helium'. This describes the LHC design generally, but the SM18 tests are done under the same 1.9 K HeII conditions.

The quote is verbatim ('3.2 quenches to reach 9 T (12850 A)') and the number is right. Rejected because the key electrical.current_leads.max is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json. Re-key it before accepting, for example to electrical.current.max at_least 12850 A (that key is described as excitation current, unit pA) or to the existing flag module.high_current_conductor_test.

Verbatim in Rossi section 4.2: 'the 15 m long, 600 mm diameter cylinder'. 600 mm is correct. Note that the magnet is tested inside its own cryostat on a bench, so this is the cold-mass size rather than a sample-space fit.

The quote is verbatim and 15 m is correct. Rejected because the key is wrong: the 15 m dimension is the horizontal length of the magnet, not a height or thickness. Re-key to sample.length.max at_least 15 m.
Verbatim: 'instrumentation feed box (IFS) bringing the instrumentation and the protection heaters taps outside the cryostat.'
Abstract is verbatim: 'polarized via dynamic nuclear polarization at 1 K and 5 T.'

Verbatim in Introduction: 'cooled to 1 K by immersion in a shallow bath of superfluid helium'. The paper also gives 'A base temperature of 0.93 K is achieved with no applied heat load', and the sample warms to 1.08 K under about 1 W, so at_most 1 K for base is justified.
Verbatim: '1 K and 5 T'. The 'CLAS12 solenoid is energized to 5 T'.
Verbatim: 'exposed to approximately 1 W of 140 GHz microwaves'. at_least 1 W is fine.
Verbatim: 'immersion in a shallow bath of superfluid helium'.
Verbatim in section 4.7 (Shim Coils): 'the target samples (2 cm diameter x 5 cm long)'. 20 mm is correct.

The quote is verbatim and 50 mm is correct. Rejected because the key is wrong: the 5 cm is the length of a sample lying along the horizontal beam axis of a horizontal cryostat, not a height or thickness. Re-key to sample.length.max at_least 50 mm.
Verbatim in the NMR section: 'One coil is tuned to the 5 T resonance frequency of protons (213 MHz), and the second to that of deuterons (32 MHz).' NMR leads at the sample justify the flag.
Verbatim in Conclusion: 'measured using a SCT at 4.2 K in magnetic field up to 12 T.'
Same verified quote. The facility is '12 T split solenoid magnet with 15 cm bore providing transverse field'.

The quote is verbatim ('Ic = 23.7 kA, n = 9' at 5 T; the SCT provides up to 45 kA). Rejected because the key electrical.current_leads.max is not in the vocabulary. Also, the current comes from a superconducting transformer inside the bath, not from current leads. Use an existing key, for example module.high_current_conductor_test present, or electrical.current.max at_least 23700 A.
Verbatim: 'The measurements were performed in LHe.'

Verbatim: 'test probes with a cross-section of 30 × 70 mm2 were inserted into the magnet vertically.' sqrt(30²+70²) = 76.16 mm, so 76.2 is correct to one decimal. This is a derived envelope, not a printed number. Keep it flagged as inferred.
Verbatim in II.B: 'A few voltage taps were soldered ... V1 and V2 are for leg A; V3 and V4 are for leg B.'
Verbatim in arXiv:1804.05750: 'The cavity temperature, as measured by ruthenium oxide thermometers throughout the run, was typically 150 mK'.
Same verified quote. The cold space must reach the 150 mK cavity temperature.
Verbatim in Outlook: 'compared to the typical field of 6.8 T for the results reported here.' Equation 1 is also normalised to 6.8 T.

The quote is verbatim ('an 136-liter cylindrical, copper-plated microwave cavity'). Rejected because the key chamber.volume is not in the vocabulary. Re-express it with existing geometry keys such as sample.diameter.max / sample.length.max, or with sample.bore_diameter, using the documented cavity dimensions.

The quote is verbatim ('The refrigerator has a cooling power of 800 µW at 100 mK') and the unit uW exists. Rejected because this is the installed fridge's specification, not a heat load the experiment needs. As a requirement it would wrongly rank candidate refrigerators. Move it to reported_conditions/reported_equipment.

Verbatim: 'Power in the the TM010 mode of the cavity is extracted with a critically coupled antenna, passed through the RF chain ... amplified by a voltage-tunable Microstrip SQUID Amplifier (MSA)'. The source has the doubled 'the the'.
Verbatim in SRF2015 TUPB063 Introduction: 'dividing the averaged measured values of resistivity at 300 +/- 0.1 K and at 10 +/- 0.1 K'. range_within 10–300 K is correct.
Verbatim: 'The card edge connectors pass electrical connections to the sample boards for the four point probe and Cernox temperature sensors.'
Verbatim in SRF2005 TUP47: 'twelve ~75 mm long (~2x2mm2 cross-section) samples'. The any-of keys include sample.length.max, so 75 mm is correct.
Verbatim: 'The clamps also conduct the 100 mA current to the samples, all samples being connected in series.'

The quote is verbatim (footnote 1: 'applying different magnetic fields above ~0.4 T'). Rejected because it describes an alternative NIST 4.2 K method that this profile does not use; its procedure is the ~10 K normal-state reading. Even as a non-mandatory preference it would favour magnet-equipped systems without reason. Drop it, or gate it with a condition for the alternative method.
Verbatim in TUPB063 Abstract: 'The samples are measured inside of an isothermal setup in a liquid helium (LHe) dewar.' TUP47 also uses in-situ evaporation of liquid helium. Non-mandatory is fine.

An equivalent passage is in Table 1 of arXiv:2511.19095v1, which flattens as 'DCR ... <200 mHz/mm² at Vop ... Cryogenic reliable @ 77 K'. The quote is the table row put back together, not contiguous text. 77 K is correct, and Table 2 reports IV results at 77 K.
Verbatim in section 3.1: 'The setup consists of a liquid nitrogen (LN2) dewar where the sensors are placed in order to perform tests at cryogenic temperatures.'
Verbatim: 'performed by a commercial source meter unit (SMU) directly connected to the SiPM through triaxial cables'.

Table 1 gives 'SiPM dimensions ... 6x6 mm2 ... Compatible with the PDS modules' (quote put back together from the table). The diagonal is sqrt(72) = 8.49 mm, so 8.5 is correct. This is a derived value.
Verbatim in arXiv:2204.05378 II.B: 'Voltage–current (V–I) characteristics are measured in boiling He at 4.2 K, in a transverse magnetic field.'
Same verified quote: 'boiling He at 4.2 K'.
Abstract is verbatim: 'At 90%Ic and 15 T, the average gain of MQE ... was 2.5'. All MQE results in Fig. 6 are at 15 T.
Verbatim: 'In the wire critical current, or Ic, measurement, one pair of voltage taps is used. The pair is placed along the center of the spiral sample 50 cm apart.'
Verbatim in arXiv:1909.02994 (light detector calibration): 'With a stable operating temperature of 20.7 mK and a strong NTD polarization for the Ge LDs, negligible nonlinearity is expected.'
Verbatim: 'we could stably operate at 20.7 mK with a few µW of regulation power.' The loaded base is about 20 mK and the empty-cryostat base is 11.5 mK, so at_most 20.7 mK is justified.

Verbatim: 'All crystals have a cylindrical shape with ∼ 44 mm diameter and ∼ 45 mm height'. The paired Ge wafer is 44.5 mm in diameter, so 44 mm slightly understates the module size. Accepted as minimal.
Same verified quote: '∼ 45 mm height'. Crystals are stacked vertically in towers, so height is the right key.
Verbatim: 'We bonded gold wires from the NTDs to flat Kapton pads with gold contacts to provide the electrical readout connection'.
Verbatim: 'The total mass of the 20 Li2100MoO4 crystals used in CUPIDMo is 4.158 kg'. This is the total for the array, not one sample. Acceptable only because it is non-mandatory.

vexp.summary:
I re-fetched all 13 cited sources (arXiv and JACoW PDFs plus the Advanced Conductor IEEE PDF) and searched their full text. Every quote is present, verbatim or as an equivalent passage; the two SiPM Table 1 quotes are table rows put back together. Every number and unit matches.

I rejected 8 of the 57 requirements:
- **Keys not in data/capability_vocabulary.json:** electrical.current_leads.max (LHC dipole #2, REBCO #2) and chamber.volume (ADMX #3).
- **Wrong key:** a horizontal sample length was entered as sample.height.max instead of sample.length.max (LHC dipole 15 m #4, DNP target 5 cm #6).
- **Not a requirement:** ADMX #4 (800 uW at 100 mK) is the installed fridge's specification, not a heat load the experiment needs. RRR #4 (0.4 T field) belongs to an alternative NIST method this profile does not use.

The REBCO probe envelope (76.2 mm) and SiPM diagonal (8.5 mm) are derived values, but the arithmetic checks out (76.16 mm and 8.49 mm). No cryostat seed documents cryogen.type values yet, so the liquid_helium/liquid_nitrogen checks will come out UNKNOWN until one does.

No duplicates. These are related existing profiles but not the same measurement:
- **expansion_a_srf_2k_resonance:** 2.6 GHz dark-photon resonance control, not 1.3 GHz Q0-versus-gradient acceptance.
- **expansion_a_teo2_bolometer:** CUORE TeO2 at about 10 mK, not CUPID-Mo Li2MoO4 with heat-and-light readout.
- **mat_electrical_resistance_low_temperature:** generic PPMS resistivity, not Nb RRR quality control.
- **expansion_a_cicc_critical_current:** SULTAN CICC, not NHMFL REBCO cables.

The history page only says AS Scientific builds Orange cryostats under a non-exclusive ILL licence, so keep the manufacturer field hedged.
Verified on the equipment card: 'Type Orange Ø100 Tmin 1.5K Tmax 320K Instrument Pool'.

The equipment card (type, Tmin, Tmax, regulation and sample Cernox sensors) and the pool table row list no magnet. ILL handles field magnets as separate pool cryomagnets, and the pool table explicitly notes magnet pairing where it exists (e.g. 105ILHV42 'for the 268HTCC81 magnet').

Rejected because the ILL instruction manual contradicts 'cannot be evacuated'. Its sample-introduction procedure says to 'Connect a primary pump to the sample chamber valve' and 'pump it' before admitting 20 cc of helium exchange gas. The sample space can therefore be evacuated, but it operates in exchange gas. Under the vocabulary definition ('Sample space can be evacuated'), not_available/false is not supported. Re-express it as an exchange-gas requirement or mark it unknown.

Rejected because the claim of no evacuated sample space is contradicted: the manual has the sample chamber pumped with a primary pump. No base pressure is documented, so this should be unknown and not documented, not not_available.

Verified: the pool table 'Material in the beam' column reads A5 - AG3 (aluminium) for 82ILHV100. The table explicitly flags windowed units where they exist (107ILHV49 'Al2O3 ... Sapphire windows'; instrument-assigned 175ILHV99 'sapphire windows'), so this row's lack of windows is a parallel explicit entry. Minor: the claim's 'only unit 107ILHV49' holds for the pool list only.
Verified: 'Ø100 x 265' in the pool table row for 82ILHV100.
Verified: 'Ø100 x 265' (diameter x length in mm).
Verified in the ILL instruction manual: 'Once the LN2 and LHe baths are filled, check that the pressure in the vacuum vessel does not increase.' This is the wet Orange cryostat procedure.
Verified: the manual describes filling LN2 and LHe baths.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source: both Quantum Design Oxford Proteox product pages plus the LX and MX brochures and the June 2026 application note, the Bluefors XLDHehp page, the Bluefors LHeP22 page and spec sheet, the Linde L70/LR70 datasheet, the Cryofab CMSH 100 spec sheet and manual, the NIST Orange cryostat page, and the ILL Orange pool table, 82ILHV100 equipment card, instruction manual and history page. PDF text was extracted with pypdf.

I accepted 71 of 76 capabilities and rejected 5:
- ProteoxMX optical_access: the "optional windows" evidence is from the LX brochure only; the MX page and MX brochure never mention windows.
- CMSH 100 temperature.range and temperature.base: the source is the NIST Orange cryostat page, a different instrument. Cryofab's own manual gives about -452°F (about 4.26 K), not 4.2 K.
- ILL Orange 82ILHV100 vacuum.available and pressure.base: the ILL manual says the sample chamber is pumped with a primary pump before exchange gas is admitted, so "cannot be evacuated" is contradicted.

One value was corrected: CMSH 100 pressure.max_working goes from 310.3 kPa (design pressure) to 69 kPa (the documented operating pressure, gauge).

Notes for ingest:
- Linde quotes drop the "≤" in "≤ 4.4 K"; the PDF prints it.
- In the Proteox app note, the vacuum-enclosure text is the Figure 1 caption, not Section 2.1.
- chamber.volume and pressure.max_working are not in data/capability_vocabulary.json. Use cryogen.dewar_volume for volume, and add or re-key the pressure (note it is gauge).
- AS Scientific as builder of ILL unit 82ILHV100 is not documented.

No duplicates: the catalog's Orange entry is the NIST OC-50 (50 mm), a different unit from the ILL 82ILHV100 (100 mm). None of the Bluefors, Proteox, Linde or Cryofab machines is already in data/cryostats, and none repeats within the batch.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 aerospace experiment profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\aerospace_and_space_exploration\experiments.json and changed nothing else in the repository. All requirement keys exist in data/capability_vocabulary.json or the v4 new_keys list, and every quantity converts in cryolean.units.

Skipped to avoid duplicates:
- JSC Chamber A telescope cryo-vacuum (already covered by expa_telescope_cold_alignment).
- Insulation boil-off calorimetry (already covered by expc_energy_insulation_boiloff and expa_mli_guarded_heat_leak).

Source and quote caveats:
- **Solar-array profile (NPO-49655):** Tavily was over its usage limit and a direct download of the Tech Briefs page was blocked, so I read it through WebFetch. Its quotes are short excerpts returned verbatim, not checked against the raw page. The test used a cryostat in a high-vacuum system, not liquid helium, so I added no liquid-helium requirement.
- **Mars PRT profile:** the PDF gives the minus signs as replacement glyphs; I wrote them as '-' in the quote.
- **Pulse-tube cooler profile (Air Liquide LPTC, Cryocoolers 19):** most of that PDF's font cannot be extracted. Only readable passages are quoted.
- **Composite LH2 tank profile:** the PDF temperature for LH2 (-253 C) is garbled. That profile relies on cryogen.type set_contains liquid_hydrogen instead of a temperature requirement.
- **LOX impact profile:** the source is the 1995 NASA paper describing NHB 8060.1C Test 13A, the predecessor of NASA-STD-6001. Impact energy (98 J) has no vocabulary key, so it appears only in the description. -297 F does not convert to an exact mK value, so no temperature requirement was written; cryogen.type decides.
- **CubeSat TVAC profile:** the LSP-REQ-317.01 Rev B values come from the peer-reviewed ICES-2017-102 summary table, not the LSP document itself. The pressure column is the fifth (LSP) column of Table 1.
- **GEVS and ECSS profiles:** these standards set test temperatures relative to each mission's predicted flight temperatures (+/-10 C margin), so neither has an absolute temperature requirement. They decide on vacuum.available, pressure.base and electrical.sample_connections.

No usable key exists for these, so they are described but not checked:
- 90 K cooling power (CryoFILL 120-150 W at 90 K).
- Impact energy.
- Cycle counts.

Extra field: every requirement has an evidence_status field, and every source has accessed = 2026-11-01.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\aerospace_and_space_exploration\equipment.json (accessed 2026-11-01). 8 configurations from 5 manufacturers: LACO Technologies (2 Frontier LN2 TVAC system solutions), Dynavac/Weiss Technik (SmallSat TVS 2400 LN2), Sunpower/AMETEK (CryoTel GT and CT Stirling coolers), IRLabs (HDL-8 LHe and ND-8 LN2 IR detector test dewars), kiutra (L-Type Rapid 3P55 ADR). Every core passport key is present on every configuration; 3 are unknown (listed in not_found). Absences follow the existing catalog convention: install=not_available with value kind unknown. Cryogen-free machines carry cryogen.type as an empty set. Magnet absences for the TVAC chambers and dewars rest on complete specification or component lists (no magnet appears in them), not on marketing silence. These are the weakest absences and worth a reviewer's look. Single stated temperatures are stored as lo = hi per the vocabulary rule: LACO 18x24 platen and shroud at -150 C, LACO 36x40 shroud at -150 C, HDL-8 at 4.2 K and ND-8 at 77 K (both standard, without the low-temperature modification). Experiments that need other temperatures on these will get DOES_NOT_MEET. Sunpower values are nominal; no guaranteed figures are published. Cold-tip diameter is used as sample.diameter.max per family_mapping. vacuum.available, pressure.base, sample.height.max, optical_access and electrical.sample_connections are not_available because the user supplies the cryostat (manual Table 3-4). Dynavac electrical.sample_connections is optional_not_installed and rests only on the optional user thermocouples. The IRLabs HDL magnet and vacuum quotes come from the HDL-5 standard-system drawing, used as representative of the HDL standard system. Thales LPT9310 and HPD/FormFactor ADRs were considered and dropped: Tavily was over quota, formfactor.com blocks scripted access, and no readable Thales datasheet was found. No files under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ were edited.

results.note: ICES-2017-102 PDF p.6: 'a minimum range of temperatures from -14 -3/+0°C to +71 -0/+3°C shall be used for qualification' (LSP-REQ-317.01 Rev.B). The conversion to 259150-344150 mK is correct.

The PDF p.3 (printed p.4) TVCT definition reads 'Thermal Vacuum Cycling Test (TVCT): This test subjects the test article to a series of cycles of hot and cold temperatures in a high vacuum environment'. The quoted 'TV CT'/'tes t' spacing comes from text extraction, but the passage is there. Vacuum is mandatory by definition.

PDF p.7 Table 1: the qualification chamber pressure in the LSP-REQ-317.01 Rev.B column (last column) is 13.3x10-3 Pa (10-4 torr). at_most 0.0001 Torr on pressure.base is correct (13.3e-3 Pa is about 1e-4 torr).

The quote is on PDF p.3. Stronger support is on p.9: 'Electrical interface is all cabling used for functional testing during TVCT. These cables are connected in the CubeSat, and pass to outside the chamber via chamber's feedthroughs'. Mandatory is justified.

CDS Rev.13 3U Acceptance Checklist (Appendix C, Section 4) gives Width 100.0 ± 0.1 mm. The diagonal of a 100.1 mm square is 141.56 mm, so 141.6 mm is right. Caveat: CDS 3.2.3 allows components up to 6.5 mm beyond the rail plane, so 141.6 mm is a necessary lower bound, not the full envelope.
The CDS Rev.13 3U checklist gives Height 340.5 ± 0.3 mm, so the upper bound is 340.8 mm. Correct.
CDS Rev.13 verbatim: '3.2.13 The maximum mass of a 3U CubeSat shall be 4.00 kg.' Optional is appropriate.
ECSS-E-ST-10-03C clause 5.5.4.2a is verbatim on printed p.74.
Clause 5.5.4.2b, printed p.75, verbatim: 'Space segment equipment shall be tested at a pressure of 10-5 hPa or less.' 1e-5 hPa = 1e-3 Pa, so the at_most 0.001 Pa constraint is correct.
Clause 5.5.4.1k is verbatim on p.74. Clauses 5.5.4.1j and l (functional tests before and after, cold switch-on) also require the equipment to be powered in the chamber. Mandatory is justified.
Clause 5.5.4.1g is verbatim on p.74: 'Functional test shall only start after a dwell time greater or equal to 2 hours.' Optional, at_least 2 h.
GSFC-STD-7000B PDF p.261, section 2.6.3.2.4, verbatim. The chamber must be evacuated.
Section 2.6.3.2.4 (PDF p.261): pressure less than 1.33 X 10-3 Pa (1 X 10-5 torr). at_most 0.00133 Pa is correct (the source says strictly less than).
Section 2.6.3.3.1 (PDF p.261) is verbatim. Units are powered and performance-tested at the plateaus (2.6.3.2.3: 'time needed to complete performance testing'), so feedthroughs are needed.

Table 2.6-1 (PDF p.258, 2.6-17) shows Maximum Transition Rate 1.0 °C/min for each level. The quote is a de-tabulated paraphrase of table cells, but the values are there. Note 6 calls these suggested rates, so optional is right. 1 °C/min = 1000 mK/min.
Section 2.6.3.2.3 (PDF p.260) is verbatim: hot and cold operational plateaus last a minimum of 4 hours. Optional, at_least 4 h.
The Tech Briefs NPO-49655 page (fetched with WebFetch; curl got 403) contains '...as a result of 122 thermal cycles' from 50 to 133 K. A 50-133 K range_within is correct.
Confirmed: 'A very high vacuum system was used to avoid the condensation of water at the temperatures required to qualify the SA'.

The quote is real ('There was no change in the electrical continuity of the solar array test coupons...'), but the article does not say continuity was monitored in situ through leads during cycling. It may have been checked only before and after. Mandatory electrical.sample_connections is not justified by the source; at most it should be optional. The profile description ('monitoring electrical continuity') overstates the source.
Coupon '[6 × 5 × 1.5 in. (≈15 × 13 × 4 cm)]' confirmed. sqrt(6^2+5^2) = 7.810 in, so 7.82 in rounded up is a correct lower bound for the clear diameter.
The 1.5 in coupon thickness is confirmed.

NASA N95-31813 p.661 (paper p.1) is verbatim: 'Test 13A of NHB 8060.1C defines the test procedure for the evaluation of the mechanical impact sensitivity of materials in ambient pressure LOX environments.' cryogen.type contains liquid_oxygen.

p.662 is verbatim: 'then the cups are chilled in a container of liquid nitrogen to freeze the sample prior to impact testing in LOX.' Optional is appropriate because it applies only to the 10.1 liquid-cup preparation.
p.662 is verbatim: cups are 'approximately 0.625 inch inside diameter and 0.050 inch deep.' Optional; the inside diameter is a weak lower bound on the cup holder.
NTRS 20170012407 p.24 is verbatim: 'The test met program requirements: (1) stepwise fill with LH2 ... to 90% volume capacity'.

The number is correct: Table 2 (the '2.4 m test outline') says 'Pneumatic test to 0.93 MPa with tank filled with LH2'. But 'pressure.max_working' is not a key in data/capability_vocabulary.json. The nearest existing key is pressure.operating.range (range, Pa), e.g. point_within 930000 Pa. Re-key it before acceptance.
Table 1 (Traceability of 2.4-5.5 m tank) row 'Diameter 5.5 m 2.4 m' confirmed. at_least 2.4 m clear diameter is correct.
Slide 4 verbatim: 'Cooling capacity design point of 120 Watts or greater with goal of 150 Watts during SS operation at 90 K'. point_within 90 K is OK.
Slide 7 verbatim: 'Chilldown performed with LOX at 90% full in the tank'.
Slide 3 verbatim: 'NASA GRC SMiRF Facility with Prototype Test Article in Vacuum Chamber.'

Slide 13 verbatim: 'operated for 31 days in both steady state and transient operations'. 31 d = 744 h; optional. The slides of this third test do not show liquefaction itself (only chilldown and holding LOX with the cooler), so the profile name's 'liquefaction' slightly overstates this source.

Cryocoolers 19 p.147 abstract is verbatim: 'cooling of infrared detectors at temperatures between 50K and 80K with cooling power between 2W and 7W.' The Meteosat Third Generation application is confirmed in the (font-encoded) body text.

'cooling_power.at_80000mK' is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json; only at_20mK through at_20000mK exist. Also, the source says the 2-7 W range varies with cold-tip and reject temperature (Fig. 2) and does not tie 2 W to 80 K. 2 W is more plausibly the low-temperature end, so 'at 80 K' misattributes it. Reject.
Same verbatim abstract sentence; 50 K low end, optional.
NTRS 20160008920 abstract is verbatim: 'to cool a 6x6 array of x-ray microcalorimeters to 50 mK.' at_most 50 mK base is correct.

Table 1 'Detector temperature stability <2 µK rms' for both cryogen and cryogen-free modes is confirmed. The uK unit exists in units.py. Note: the vocabulary describes temperature.stability as a ± value while the source gives rms, so the comparison is conservative-equivalent at best.
p.2 verbatim: 'The heat leak into the detector array, through the Kevlar suspension and readout wires, depends only on the temperature of the housing.' Readout wiring is required for the detector.
p.3 verbatim (Stage 1 sized for 0.65 µW 'for a 24-hour hold time, plus 100% margin'). Optional. Caveat: measured hold time was >42 h in cryogen mode but just over 15 h in cryogen-free mode.
NASA Tech Briefs May 2012 p.32 is verbatim: 'three protoflight/qualification cycles (-135 to 70 °C)'. 138150-343150 mK is correct.
Verbatim: 'a planetary protection cycle to +125 °C for two hours'. 398150 mK is correct. It is part of the same thermal-cycling sequence, so mandatory is reasonable.
Verbatim: 'There were no observed changes in PRT resistances...'. Optional is appropriate because in-situ monitoring is not stated.

vexp.summary:
I checked all 10 aerospace profiles (40 requirements). 37 pass and 3 are rejected. Nine of the ten sources were downloaded and converted to text; the Tech Briefs NPO-49655 page gave curl a 403, so I read it through WebFetch instead.

Rejected:
- **aero_composite_lh2_tank_pressure#1:** 'pressure.max_working' is not a key in capability_vocabulary.json. The 0.93 MPa value itself is correct; it should be re-keyed, for example to pressure.operating.range with point_within 930000 Pa.
- **aero_lptc_ir_detector_80k#1:** 'cooling_power.at_80000mK' is not a key in the vocabulary either. The source also does not tie 2 W to 80 K.
- **aero_solar_array_50_133k#2:** the source says electrical continuity was unchanged after cycling, not that it was monitored through leads during cycling. Mandatory electrical connections are not justified; optional would be.

Caveats on accepted items:
- The CubeSat diameter (141.6 mm) is a lower bound: the CubeSat spec allows parts to stick out up to 6.5 mm past the rails.
- The ADR stability limit is given as rms in the source, while the vocabulary key is a ± value.
- The CryoFILL slides show chilldown and holding liquid oxygen, not liquefaction itself.
- Meteosat Third Generation is confirmed in the LPTC paper body.

No duplicates found, either among these profiles or with the existing data/experiments profiles. The ECSS and GEVS equipment thermal-vacuum profiles are the same kind of test, but under different standards with different pressure limits, so I kept both.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source. LACO pages were read with WebFetch; the Dynavac, Sunpower, IRLabs and kiutra PDFs were downloaded and their text extracted with pdftotext/pymupdf, using block positions to rebuild the scrambled tables. Tavily was over quota.

None of the 7 machines is a duplicate of the 53 files in data/cryostats or of each other.

13 capabilities are rejected:
- **Sample-height keys on the wrong axis:** these keys mean vertical height/thickness, but the batch used a horizontal depth or length.
  - LACO 18x24 used 22 in; corrected to 16 in.
  - Dynavac 2400 used 20 in; corrected to 18 in, since the table is w x d x h = 20x20x18.
  - LACO 36x40 used the 38 in platen length; no vertical clearance is stated, so no fix is given.
- **LACO 36x40 sample diameter:** the 24 in figure is only the 'approximately 24 in' platen width, not a stated working envelope.
- **Sunpower GT and CT sample diameter:** the cold-tip diameters (1 in, 1.65 in) are thermal interfaces, not sample limits, and contradict sample.height being not_available.
- **Optical access, three rejections:**
  - LACO 18x24: a door shroud may block the viewport.
  - Dynavac: the standard shroud is an 'optically dense enclosure', and 'Door viewport' is also listed as an option.
  - kiutra: the absence rests only on a non-exhaustive 'Options include' sentence.
- **Dynavac electrical.sample_connections:** the only evidence is optional thermocouple sensing channels, not connections to the test article.

Other notes:
- IRLabs now sells the 8 in nitrogen dewar as NDV-8; 'ND' today means only the Vega and Rigel models. The values match the 2010 brochure's ND-8.
- Four new keys are missing from data/capability_vocabulary.json: temperature.shroud.range, chamber.volume, cooling_power.at_77000mK and holding_time.static. The units used (Torr, inch, h, L, W) are supported in cryolean/units.py.

Wrote C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\astronomy_and_astrophysics\experiments.json with 10 experiments (ids astro_*), accessed 2026-11-01. I checked every quote against the downloaded source text: each one appears verbatim after whitespace normalisation and has at most 50 words. Every constraint passes cryolean.serialize.constraint. Every key is either in data/capability_vocabulary.json or is one of the v4 new_keys (holding_time.static). No ids or plain_names repeat each other or the existing profiles.

Mandatory requirements use the core passport keys wherever the physics allows: temperature.range or temperature.base, vacuum.available, pressure.base, optical_access, electrical.sample_connections, sample.diameter.max and sample.height.max. Family keys are made mandatory only where the procedure depends on them: electrical.coax_bandwidth.max for the MKID, SIS, FAST and Arecibo readouts; holding_time.static for the 40 h MEGARA LN2 hold; module.magnetic_shielding for the Lynx TES. Cryogen type and cryogen-free status are optional (mandatory=false) because each procedure would work with either cooling method.

Source substitutions:

- MDPI Electronics 14/8/1572 (cryogenic MMIC LNA at 15 K) returned HTTP 403, and the Chalmers 67-116 GHz receiver PDF timed out. They are replaced by two other published 15 K radio receivers: FAST L-band (arXiv:2103.10677, which includes the LNA noise test at 15 K) and the Arecibo 12 m 2.5-14 GHz receiver (arXiv:2308.05826).
- I left out the idea 'cryogenic optical test of telescope mirror segments' because it duplicates the existing expa_mirror_cold_figure and expa_telescope_cold_alignment profiles.

Judgment calls a reviewer may want to check:
- (a) SIS optical_access=present is mandatory. The rationale is physical: the 660 GHz LO and the hot/cold-load radiation must reach the mixer through a window. The report quotes the 660 GHz LO but does not name the window.
- (b) The Lynx source is a mission-design paper (JATIS 2019). The mandatory 42 mK bath comes from its lab test of the UHR array. The 4-8 GHz HEMT and 50 mK ADR requirements come from the flight design and are kept optional.
- (c) Several size gates use the active detector area as a lower bound (H2RG 36.864 mm, MEGARA 61.4 mm) and are optional, because the package size is not stated.
- (d) The MKID operating_duration.max >= 8 h is optional, because a continuous dilution refrigerator has no hold-time limit.
- (e) The MEGARA cryostat is from a 2016 INAOE MSc thesis (a facility integration document). Its quotes come from Table 3.1 and Sections 3.2-5.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\astronomy_and_astrophysics\equipment.json (builder and quote-verification script: C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\tools\build_astro.py; every quote was checked automatically against the downloaded source text, with whitespace and list bullets collapsed, and all quotes are 50 words or fewer). 8 configurations of 8 models from 6 manufacturers: Oxford Instruments NanoScience, Lake Shore Cryotronics, ICEoxford, Advanced Research Systems, kiutra and Bluefors. None duplicates data/cryostats. The catalog's Oxford OptistatDry, Lake Shore CRX/CPX/Janis CCS probe stations and Bluefors LD dilution refrigerator are different machines. Categories covered: LN2 detector/CCD cryostats (OptistatDN-V, VPF-100); closed-cycle detector/receiver cryostats (DRY ICE 3K INV, Bluefors LD-4K); a large cold-plate cryostat for arrays and cold optics (CCS-CP); He-3 sorption for TES/KID (DRY ICE 300mK Benchtop); an ADR for MKIDs/microcalorimeters (kiutra L-Type Rapid 3P55); and a True-UHV cold head for laboratory ice astrochemistry (ARS CS204AB). Accessed 2026-11-01. All values are manufacturer specifications. Conservative choices: '<3K', '<4 K' and '<10K' range bounds are stored as 3, 4 and 10 K. kiutra '(expected)' values are stored at the guaranteed bound. ARS cooling powers and cooldown use the 50 Hz values. Where stability varies with temperature, the worst stated value is stored. The VPF-100 range is limited to 77-500 K because the 65 K pumping manifold is not part of the configuration. Absences: the magnet is not_available for OptistatDN-V (manual component list), VPF-100 and CCS-CP (their complete 7-step configurators offer no magnet), DRY ICE 3K INV (spec table says 'Magnetic Field N/A') and ARS CS204AB (typical configuration and options list). Options that exist but are not fitted are optional_not_installed: windows, magnets, magnetic shielding and Bluefors wiring. Where a configuration includes an offered wiring option, its configuration_basis says so: VPF-100 wired feedthrough, CCS-CP 100 DC wires plus 67 GHz RF, DRY ICE 3K INV wiring kit, DRY ICE 300mK customer DC loom, kiutra 12 RF lines. The ARS pressure.base of 1e-11 Torr is the cold head's UHV rating; the vacuum chamber is supplied by the customer. OptistatDN-V pressure.base uses the manual's pump-down requirement (<1e-4 mbar). VPF-100 uses the stated initial vacuum requirement (~1e-3 Torr at room temperature). In the ARS data sheet, the temperature-range row on the CS204*B sheet is printed with the label DE-202AI, and the quote keeps that label. Main gaps (see not_found): kiutra L-Type and Bluefors LD-4K publish no maximum temperature and no sample-vacuum statement, so temperature.range is missing for both. Experiments written on temperature.range point_within will get NEED_MORE_INFORMATION on those two, but temperature.base requirements will decide. Several cryostats also publish no vacuum level or sample height. During research the Tavily search quota ran out (HTTP 432 usage limit) and the session WebSearch budget was used up. Further candidates (Oxford Instruments Heliox/Proteox, FormFactor/Entropy ADRs, Sumitomo/Cryomech stand-alone cryocoolers, IRLabs custom dewars, Chase sorption coolers) could therefore not be examined; manufacturer pages were reached only by direct URL navigation.

vexp.summary:
I downloaded all 10 sources, converted them to text and checked every quote by normalized matching. All quotes are there: 58 match exactly, and 4 differ only by PDF ligature artifacts (MEGARA #4 and #5, FAST #0 and #3). I accept 60 of 62 requirements and reject 2:

- **astro_megara_ccd_ln2_153k#1:** the key 'holding_time.static' is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json. Re-key it as operating_duration.max, at_least 40 h.
- **astro_alma_sis_mixer_4k_yfactor#2:** the quote about the 660 GHz LO does not show a cryostat window or optical path. Neither 'window' nor 'quasi-optical' appears anywhere in the report, so the requirement needs a better source passage or should be dropped.

Caveats on accepted items:
- **RF windows:** FAST #3, Arecibo #1 and (if re-sourced) ALMA use optical_access for radio-frequency windows. It is the closest key in the vocabulary, but the windows are RF, not optical.
- **Pressure requirements:** the mandatory pressure.base values for H2RG, FAST and INFRA-ICE are what was reached or designed, not stated minimums. They are strict but defensible.
- **cryogen.type:** no seed in the repo shows which tokens cryogen.type takes, so check that 'liquid_nitrogen' and 'liquid_helium' match what the equipment data uses.

Duplicates: none. None of the 10 sources is used by any data/experiments profile or by another industry in research/v4. The closest is aero_adr_xray_microcalorimeter_50mk (Astro-H SXS ADR, NASA NTRS source). It is a different instrument and measurement from the Lynx TES characterization, so it is not a duplicate. The earlier mid-IR array profile in data/experiments (MITTEN, 16 K) is also a different measurement from the H2RG one.

veq.summary:
I downloaded every source myself (PDFs and product pages) and checked each claim against it. Tavily extract was over its usage limit, so I fetched with curl and read the PDFs with pdftotext and pypdf. Working copies are in C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\astro_verify_34968.

No duplicates: none of the 8 machines is in data/cryostats, and none repeats within the batch. The existing oxford_optistatdry, lakeshore_janis_ccs and bluefors_ld records are different models.

Of 92 capabilities, 83 accepted and 9 rejected:
- **OptistatDN-V, sample.height.max:** the source gives the sample holder's length (50 mm), not a maximum sample height.
- **ICEoxford 3K INV and 300mK Benchtop, temperature.stability:** each stores one worst-case value, but neither covers the whole range. The 3K INV states nothing above 50 K, and the Benchtop states nothing between 290 and 400 mK.
- **ARS CS204AB, temperature.range:** the quoted row is labelled DE-202AI, a different cold head.
- **ARS CS204AB, magnetic_field.max:** the "no magnet" claim rests only on the options list not mentioning one. The sheet says "Fully Customizable" and the sample sits in the customer's own chamber.
- **ARS CS204AB, pressure.base:** 1e-11 Torr is the cold head's seal rating; the pressure reached depends on the customer's chamber and pumps.
- **Bluefors LD-4K, sample.diameter.max:** 330 mm is the base flange diameter, not a documented sample size. The existing bluefors_ld record also leaves this unknown.
- **Bluefors LD-4K, cooling_power.at_4200mK:** 1.35 W is the pulse tube's own stage. The same table gives only about 50 mW at 3 K and about 1000 mW at 5 K at the experimental 4K flange.

Accepted points worth knowing:
- **"No magnet" absences:** accepted for OptistatDN-V (complete component lists in the manual), VPF-100 and CCS-CP (complete seven-step order configurators), and DRY ICE 3K INV (explicit "Magnetic Field N/A").
- **VPF-100 pressure.base:** ~1e-3 Torr is the conservative datasheet value. The web spec page says ~1e-4 Torr.
- **CCS-CP sample.diameter.max:** the 200 mm cold plate is accepted because it is the sample mount itself.
- **OptistatDN-V configuration_basis:** it says 500 K needs sapphire windows, but that footnote belongs to the OptistatDN (non-V) table.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 semiconductors_and_electronics profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\semiconductors_and_electronics\experiments.json. The file uses the same layout as research/v4/aerospace_and_space_exploration/experiments.json. Every requirement key already exists in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so this batch adds no new vocabulary.

Sources and quotes: every quote was copied from a document I downloaded and read: the MIL-STD-883 1010.8 PDF, the AEC-Q100 Rev-H PDF, the arXiv PDFs, the Glasgow eprint and the Europe PMC full text. A few quotes are not exact copies:
- The two MIL-STD-883 Table I quotes are table rows as pdftotext extracted them. The location field says which column is condition C.
- In the AEC-Q100 quotes, the degree sign is shown as °C; the PDF encoding garbles it.
- In the Neyens quote, ± replaces a character the PDF encoding garbles.
- In the Refino quote, the subscripts appear as plain 'O2'/'SF6'.

Derived value: the MIL temperature.sweep_rate.max of 13437.5 mK/min is my own calculation, not a printed number (215 K span within 16 min). It is marked non-mandatory.

Range handling: where the cold and hot extremes came from separate table rows, I split them into temperature.range at_most (cold) and at_least (hot). Lean Checker.lean compares at_least against range.hi.

Ideas not used, with the reason:
- JESD22-A104 standalone: no free verbatim source. Its Grade 0 -55/+150 C conditions are covered through AEC-Q100 test A4.
- ThermoStream characterisation: I found no published procedure, only spec sheets.
- Variable-temperature Hall and DLTS: existing profiles expc_semiconductor_cryo_hall and expc_semiconductor_dlts already cover them, so I used 4H-SiC Laplace-DLTS instead.
- MIT MTL cryo-DRIE link: it is a copy of the Dussart 2014 review and gives only generic conditions. I replaced it with the Refino 2021 SENTECH SI 500C recipe (-95 C, 1.0 Pa).
- TU Delft 4 K CMOS: replaced by the TUM 5 nm FinFET (10-300 K) and NPL multiplexed 4.2 K profiles, so it does not duplicate expc_semiconductor_native_mosfet.

Tool limits hit during research: Tavily extract hit its usage limit, the shared WebSearch budget ran out, the Lune daily quota is used up (resets 2026-11-02), and navsea.navy.mil JEDEC PDFs could not be reached.

Gaps:
- Most mandatory keys are core-passport keys. Some non-passport keys are mandatory and may give NEED_MORE_INFORMATION on machines that do not document them: electrical.probe_arms (FinFET, GaN), electrical.coax_bandwidth.max (GaN) and electrical.coax_lines (SFQ).
- No vacuum requirement for the 300 mm cryoprober: the Bluefors page shows a vacuum chamber only in a layout figure, with no quotable value.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\semiconductors_and_electronics\equipment.json (generator script: C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\semi_build\build_semi.py). 8 configurations from 6 manufacturers (inTEST Thermal Solutions, MPI Corporation, ESPEC, Lake Shore Cryotronics, Oxford Instruments Plasma Technology, Bluefors) covering temperature forcing, thermal-chuck wafer probing, thermal shock, LHe/LN2 and cryogen-free cryogenic probe stations (including an electromagnet station for Hall/magnetotransport), cryogenic ICP etch and a <2 K 300 mm wafer prober. None duplicates data/cryostats: the catalog's Lake Shore CRX-VF/CRX-4K/CPX/FastHall and ESPEC EGNX12 are different models. Accessed 2026-11-01. 6 of 8 configurations document every core key except sample.height.max; ESPEC TSE-12-A documents all of them. RESEARCH LIMITS: Tavily returned a plan-quota error on the first call, and the shared WebSearch budget (200 per turn) ran out after 5 searches. As a result, DLTS cryostats (Semilab/PhysTech), Ecopia HMS-5000 Hall systems and humidity climatic chambers could not be sourced. The Ecopia HMS-5300 user manual from a university group was read (80-350 K, 0.55 T permanent magnet, LN2), but it is not a manufacturer document and has no vacuum or optical data, so it was not used. PDFs were read from WebFetch-saved copies with pdftotext, and HTML spec tables through the read-only browser; degree and multiplication signs were restored in quotes. Conversions: Celsius to mK exactly (+273150); 4.5 in = 114.3 mm; Torr kept as Torr ('0.00001'). Conservative choices: the worst-case stability over the standard range is used (FWPX/EMPX nitrogen +/-100 mK, CRX-6.5K +/-25 mK); the 6-arm CRX-6.5K values are used (base 10 K, 10.5-350 K); Bluefors RF bandwidth is recorded as 18 GHz; EMPX homogeneity of 2.6% over 25 mm is stored as 26000 ppm. The ThermoStream transition of 180 K in about 10 s is recorded as 1080 K/min (nominal conditions). For MPI, thermal-chuck stability and rate values were not used because the extracted table columns could not be matched to a chuck type with certainty. JUDGEMENT CALLS TO REVIEW: (1) ThermoStream electrical.sample_connections = true, because the cap sits over the DUT at the tester interface and the user's tester provides the wiring; (2) ESPEC TSE-12-A temperature.range is stored as -65..+200 C, although exposure happens in two bands (-65..0 and +60..+200 C); (3) ESPEC optical_access = false, because the catalog lists the viewing window as an option for the TSD model only; (4) Bluefors temperature.range is lo = hi = 2 K under the single-stated-temperature rule, so 4 K experiments will read DOES_NOT_MEET against it even though the warm end is only undocumented; (5) the CRX-6.5K magnet is recorded as optional_not_installed (ring magnet kit, no field value given). The Lake Shore TTPX and PS-100 specification pages were also read (4.4-475 K, LHe/LN2, ring magnet optional) but left out as near-duplicates of FWPX/CPX. The Oxford PlasmaPro 100 Cobra and Bluefors CWP entries are partial, because only marketing/spec web pages were reachable (brochure and Pre-Installation Guide are gated); their missing core keys are listed in not_found.

results.note: Re-downloaded q-tech PDF (MIL-STD-883G Method 1010.8, 18 June 2004). Table I cold row, whitespace-normalized from the layout text, reads '1 >10 -55 +0 -55 +0 -65 +0 -65 +0 -65 +0 -65 +0' (tolerance -10 on the next line). Condition C is the third column: -65 C (+0/-10) = 208.15 K. Section 3 makes condition C the default with at least 10 cycles. On a range key, at_most bounds the low end, which is correct.
Hot row reads '2 >10 85 +10 125 +15 150 +15 200 +15 300 +15 175 +15'. Condition C is +150 C (+15/-0) = 423.15 K. at_least on temperature.range is correct.

The quote is genuine (section 3.1). But the source gives no rate: 13.4375 K/min is the profile's own inference (215 K / 16 min), so evidence_status 'reference_data' is wrong and should be inferred_estimate. The rule is also about how fast the worst-case load reaches temperature, not a chamber ramp rate, and a two-chamber transfer system never uses this rate. The number is not in the source and the key mapping is unsure, so I am rejecting it.

Re-downloaded AEC-Q100 Rev-H. The page-11 Table 2 entry for A4 TC reads 'Grade 0: -55°C to +150°C for 2000 cycles or equivalent.' -55 C = 218.15 K. The legacy -65 C/500-cycle option is colder, so this bound still holds.
Same A4 passage: +150 C = 423.15 K. Correct.

The A5 PTC entry reads 'Grade 0: Ta of -40°C to +150°C for 1000 cycles.' range_within 233.15-423.15 K is correct. Caveat: the same cell says PTC is 'required only on devices with maximum rated power >= 1 watt or ΔTJ >= 40°C or devices designed to drive inductive loads'. Mandatory holds only because this profile explicitly includes PTC; the description should say PTC is conditional.

Quote verified on page 11 ('Thermal shut-down shall not occur during this test. TEST before and after PTC at room and hot temperature.'). PTC per JESD22-A105 cycles the device while powered, so bias wiring into the chamber is needed. The same PTC-only-for-power-devices caveat applies.

Re-downloaded the TUM DAC 2023 PDF. Section II.B 'Measuring 5 nm FinFET Transistors for the Temperature Range' contains the quote verbatim, and the paper measures 'from 300 K down to 10 K'. range_within 10-300 K is correct.
Verbatim in II.B ('...features a 51 mm diameter sample stage, a vacuum pump, a twostage closed-cycle refrigerator unit...'). vacuum.available present is justified.

The text quote is verbatim. However, the paper's own setup figure, Fig. 1(a), labels only 'Probe 1' and 'Probe 2', so four terminals were contacted with two (multi-tip) probe arms. Requiring 4 arms overstates the need. Corrected to count_at_least 2.
The B1500A quote is verbatim in II.B. The DUT is biased and measured through the probes.
Verbatim in the Fig. 1 caption ('a cryogenic probe station "Lakeshore CRX-VF", a closed-cycle refrigerator...'). Correctly optional.

The quote is verbatim (arXiv:2307.04812: 'base temperature of 1.0 K at the chuck and an electron temperature of 1.6 ± 0.2 K'). But requiring the equipment base to be <= 1.0 K is a property of that prober, not a need of the procedure. The results are reported 'at 1.6 K', and the paper itself calls 1.6 K 'the 1.6 K base temperature of the cryo-prober' when it discusses validating the superconducting gate stack. The existing quantum_spin_qubit_wafer_cryoprobing profile uses at_most 1600 mK. The threshold is not justified as stated.
The abstract quote is verbatim ('cryogenic 300 mm wafer prober ... at 1.6 K'). Whole 300 mm wafers are loaded, so at_least 300000 um is correct.
Verbatim: 'The wafer is brought into contact with the probe pins to electrically connect device pads to voltage sources and current and voltage detectors at room temperature.'

Verbatim: 'The DC/RF measurement was executed using 40A-GSG-100 probes connected to a Keysight PNA-X N5245B.' A two-port S-parameter and noise-parameter measurement needs two GSG probes, so >= 2 is justified.
Verbatim in Section III (LakeShore manual probe station, Model 336, 60 L LN2 dewar, Agilent TPS-compact vacuum pump, 77 K to 475 K). The sample space is evacuated.

Verbatim in Section II: 'Reverse and pulse biases were respectively Vr = -5 V and Vp = 0 V. Pulse widths were tp = 1 ms and 100 ns...'. The diode must be biased and its capacitance read.

Pa is a valid unit, and 1.0 Pa is verified. Caveat: 1.0 Pa is the process (operating) pressure, not a base pressure. Base <= 1 Pa is only a necessary condition, which this constraint correctly encodes. Holding the gas-flow process pressure is not captured.

The quote is verbatim ('photolithography with a photomask by the size of 2″ wafer'), but it describes the photomask, not the etched sample. Verbatim in 4.1 ('Although liquid helium cooling at 4.2 K has traditionally been used, its high cost and limited availability...'). Correctly optional.

vexp.summary:
I checked all 10 semiconductors_and_electronics profiles against freshly downloaded sources. The downloaded files are in C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\semi\v.

Every quote checked was really in its source. Of 41 requirements, 37 are accepted (2 of them with corrected values) and 4 are rejected:
- **MIL-883 #2 (sweep rate):** the 13.4 K/min rate is the profile's own inference, labelled as reference data. The 16-minute rule is about how fast the load reaches temperature, not a chamber ramp rate.
- **Spin-qubit #0 (base <= 1.0 K):** 1.0 K is that prober's chuck spec. The procedure needs about 1.6 K, which the paper itself calls the base temperature.
- **SiC Laplace-DLTS #2 (stability <= 0.1 K):** the source states temperature error, which is not the stability property the key describes.
- **Si nanowire etch #3 (sample >= 2 inch):** the 2-inch size is the photomask's, not the etched sample's.

Two values were corrected:
- **FinFET probe arms:** 4 lowered to 2. The paper's figure shows only Probe 1 and Probe 2.
- **SiC MOSFET temperature range:** narrowed to 650 mK - 25 K. The 300 K point was a room-temperature reference, not a controlled set point.

Two accepted items need a caveat. The AEC-Q100 power temperature cycling applies only to devices rated at 1 W or more, with a junction-temperature rise of at least 40 C, or that drive inductive loads. For the nanowire etch, the 1.0 Pa figure is the process pressure, so the base-pressure limit is only a necessary condition.

There is one duplicate: semi_spin_qubit_300mm_cryoprober repeats research/v4 quantum_spin_qubit_wafer_cryoprobing (same paper, same measurement). The SiC DLTS profile is not a duplicate of the existing silicon DLTS profile, and the AEC-Q100 temperature-cycling profile is not a duplicate of the automotive AEC-Q100 operating-range profile; both measure something different. No existing data/experiments profile duplicates any of these 10.

I re-fetched every source and checked each capability against it: the inTEST ATS-645-M datasheet PDF, the MPI TS2000-SE 14-page data sheet PDF, the ESPEC TSD/TSE catalog PDF from Transcat, the Lake Shore FWPX, CRX-6.5K and EMPX-H2 technical-specification pages, the Oxford Instruments ICP-RIE page and the Bluefors Cryogenic Wafer Prober page. Text was extracted with pdftotext and an HTML-to-text script under C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\verify_semi\dl. Every quote was found in its source.

I rejected 4 capabilities:
(1) ATS-645-M electrical.sample_connections: the datasheet lists only thermocouple DUT sensor ports. Any DUT wiring belongs to the user's tester, not the instrument.
(2) ESPEC TSE-12-A temperature.range: the test area has two separate ranges, -65 to 0 °C and +60 to +200 °C. One continuous 208-473 K range would falsely match steady temperatures between 0 and 60 °C.
(3) ESPEC TSE-12-A sample.height.max of 148 mm: that is the raw inside height. The specification has fixed shelf brackets on 2 levels and 35 mm tall baskets, so the usable specimen height is lower and not stated.
(4) ESPEC TSE-12-A optical_access=false: this should be accepted. My 'accept': false was a mistake; the note on that entry explains why. The viewing window is a TSD-only option and the complete TSE-12-A table has no window, so the absence is supported.

All other values match their sources conservatively. All absence claims rest on complete specifications or explicit statements (for example, FWPX 'Magnetic field: Not an option').

No duplicates: data/cryostats has only lakeshore_crx.json (CRX-VF and CRX-4K, not CRX-6.5K), the Lake Shore CPX and the ESPEC EGNX12. None of the eight new machines appears there, and none is repeated within the batch.

experiments.description: All-fibre heralded qubit amplifier at 1550 nm (Bruno et al., Geneva/NIST/JPL): four MoSi superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (D1-D4) with 70% system detection efficiency, operated at 2.5 K in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler, register the 3- and 4-fold coincidences that herald the teleportation-based amplification.

requirements.rationale: The MoSi SNSPDs reach their 70% efficiency only at T < 2.5 K, so the detector stage must reach 2.5 K or below.
requirements.document_title: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)
requirements.quote: We use MoSi SNSPDs with 70% detection efficiency at 1550 nm, at a temperature T < 2.5 K [27].

requirements.rationale: Each of the four nanowire detectors (D1-D4) must be current-biased and read out electrically to record the 3- and 4-fold heralding coincidences.
requirements.document_title: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)
requirements.quote: The amplification is heralded by a 3-fold coincidence given by a click in the detector D1, which heralds the input photon, followed by D2 and D3, heralding its teleportation.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the detectors were designed for and operated in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler (no liquid-helium bath).
requirements.document_title: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)
requirements.quote: The MoSi detectors were fabricated to obtain maximum efficiency at a wavelength of 1550 nm and for operation at 2.5 K in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler.

experiments.description: Xu et al. (SIMIT) characterise a fibre-coupled NbN microstrip detector (50 um active diameter) at 0.84 K in an adsorption refrigerator (SDE ~92.2% at 1550 nm) and at 2.1 K in a compact closed-cycle G-M cryocooler (SDE > 70%); biased and read out through a cryogenic coaxial cable and a room-temperature bias tee.

requirements.rationale: The >90% system detection efficiency was obtained at 0.84 K; reaching that temperature is needed to reproduce the headline result.

requirements.quote: The SMSPDs are characterized at two different base temperatures: (1) 0.84 K in an adsorption refrigerator and (2) 2.1 K in a compact closed-cycle G-M cryocooler.
