requirements.document_title: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)
requirements.quote: The detector was then biased and read out through a cryogenic coaxial cable, connecting to a DC and RF output port of a bias tee (ZX85-12G-S+, Mini Circuit Inc.) placed at room temperature.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the paper also qualifies the detector (SDE > 70%) in a 2.1 K closed-cycle cryocooler, the practical deployment configuration.
requirements.document_title: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)
requirements.quote: Furthermore, the detector's SDE is over 70% when operated at a 2.1-K closed-cycle cryocooler.

experiments.name: Joule-class picosecond CPA with cryogenically cooled (77 K) Yb:YAG active-mirror amplifiers at 0.5-1 kW average power
experiments.plain_name: Amplify a kilowatt-class picosecond laser using crystals chilled by liquid nitrogen
experiments.description: Reagan et al. (Colorado State) amplify stretched pulses in Yb:YAG active mirrors cooled to 77 K by flowing cryogenic liquid; the 100-mJ stage sits on a cryogenic cooling manifold inside a vacuum chamber and the joule-level stage uses 30 mm x 30 mm x 2 mm composite active mirrors (1.5 J at 500 Hz; 1 J at 1 kHz).

requirements.rationale: The active mirrors are cooled to 77 K, where Yb:YAG becomes four-level with higher cross-section and thermal conductivity.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: The highly reflective face of the active mirror is cooled by direct contact with flowing cryogenic liquid cooled to 77 K[37].

requirements.rationale: The cryogenic cooling manifold carrying the gain medium is enclosed in a vacuum chamber.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: A 5 mm thick, 2 at. % Yb:YAG active mirror is mounted on a cryogenic cooling manifold enclosed in a vacuum chamber.

requirements.rationale: Free-space pump and seed beams must reach the cooled active mirrors and exit after each pass, so the cold enclosure needs optical windows.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: Seed pulses are injected into the amplifier though a thin film polarizer (TFP) and are directed to pass through each active mirror twice.

requirements.rationale: Joule-level active mirrors are 30 mm x 30 mm; the circumscribing diameter is 42.43 mm (rounded up to 42427 um).
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: The active mirrors are composites, consisting of a 30 mm × 30 mm × 2 mm thick 3 at. % Yb:YAG section optically bonded on the four lateral faces to an absorbing Cr4+:YAG cladding

requirements.rationale: Optional: the source cools the Yb:YAG disks with liquid nitrogen; a cryocooler with sufficient lift at 77 K could substitute.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)

experiments.name: Operation of a fibre-pigtailed, bias-tuned quantum-dot micropillar single-photon source in a compact 2.4 K two-stage G-M cryocooler
experiments.plain_name: Run a plug-and-play fibre-connected quantum-dot light source inside a compact 2.4 K cooler
experiments.description: Margaria et al. (C2N/Quandela) attach a single-mode fibre directly to a deterministic QD micropillar whose p-i-n junction is bias-tuned through electrical contact ridges, then operate it in a rack-mounted compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler at 2.4 K for ten-hour stability runs (fibre brightness 20.8%, indistinguishability 97.5%).

requirements.rationale: The pigtailed source was operated at the cryocooler base temperature of 2.4 K (the 5 K free-space setup gave lower indistinguishability).
requirements.document_title: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)
requirements.quote: After completion of the direct coupling process, the fibre-pigtailed source is installed in a compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler operating at a base temperature of 2.4 K.

requirements.rationale: The QD charge state and emission wavelength are set by a bias voltage through electrical contacts on the chip.
requirements.document_title: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)
requirements.quote: For bias voltage tuning, each micropillar on the chip is connected to electrical contacts by four narrow ridges37 (Fig. 1a).

requirements.rationale: Optional: the deployable source runs in a closed-cycle G-M cryocooler without liquid cryogens.
requirements.document_title: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)
requirements.quote: We demonstrate the successful integration of our source in a compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler operating at a base temperature of 2.4 K.

sources.citation: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)

experiments.name: Atomic-frequency-comb preparation on Zeeman sub-levels of an Er:Ti:LiNbO3 waveguide at ~0.7 K and 3 kG (telecom quantum memory)
experiments.plain_name: Prepare a telecom-wavelength quantum memory in an erbium-doped crystal chip at 0.7 K inside a magnetic field
experiments.description: Askarani et al. (Calgary/Delft) cool a fibre-butt-coupled Er3+:Ti4+:LiNbO3 waveguide to about 0.7 K in an adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator, apply up to 5 kG along the c-axis, measure Zeeman-level lifetimes by spectral hole burning (350-800 G) and prepare 0.2-6.4 GHz atomic frequency combs at 1532 nm under 3 kG.

requirements.rationale: Long-lived Zeeman population storage requires spin-polarised Er ions at about 0.7 K.
requirements.document_title: Persistent atomic frequency comb based on Zeeman sub-levels of an erbium-doped crystal waveguide (Askarani et al., arXiv:1907.07780, 2019)
requirements.quote: which is cooled to a temperature of around 0.7 K using an adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator.

requirements.rationale: All AFCs were prepared under a 3 kG (300 mT) field along the crystal c-axis.
requirements.document_title: Persistent atomic frequency comb based on Zeeman sub-levels of an erbium-doped crystal waveguide (Askarani et al., arXiv:1907.07780, 2019)
requirements.quote: are created under the application of a 3 kG magnetic field (oriented along the crystal c-axis), and feature peak spacings of 50 MHz.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the setup exposed the waveguide to fields up to 5 kG (500 mT).
requirements.document_title: Persistent atomic frequency comb based on Zeeman sub-levels of an erbium-doped crystal waveguide (Askarani et al., arXiv:1907.07780, 2019)
requirements.quote: The waveguide is exposed to magnetic fields up to 5 kG oriented parallel to the c-axis of the crystal.

experiments.description: Bian et al. integrate a YBCO-on-LAO HTS filter (925.2 MHz, 2.7 MHz bandwidth) and a cryogenic LNA in a vacuum chamber cooled by a mini Stirling cryocooler of the type used for IR detectors; the microwave devices operate at 71.8 K using 0.325 W of cooling power.

requirements.rationale: The HTS filter and LNA were operated at 71.8 K.
requirements.document_title: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract
requirements.quote: The microwave devices inside the subsystem are working at 71.8 K with a consumed cooling power of 0.325 W.

requirements.rationale: The cold filter and LNA sit in an evacuated chamber on the cryocooler cold finger.
requirements.document_title: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract
requirements.quote: The whole front-end subsystem, including a HTS filter, a LNA, a cryocooler and the vacuum chamber, has a size of only φ 120 mm × 175 mm and a weight of only 3.3 kg.

requirements.rationale: RF input/output and LNA supply lines must reach the cold filter-amplifier chain to measure gain and return loss.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 photonics and telecommunications experiment profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\photonics_and_telecommunications\experiments.json. That file also records accessed = 2026-11-01 and evidence_status for each requirement. I built the file with C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\build_photon.py. All quotes were checked against text pulled straight from the source PDFs and HTML pages.

None of the 10 repeats an existing profile. The existing ones are expc_photonics_snspd_characterization, qd_autocorrelation, silicon_frequency and expa_ybco_rf_filter. The plain_names differ from each other, from data/experiments and from the other research/v4 industry files.

Requirements mostly use core-passport keys: temperature.range, temperature.base, magnetic_field.max, vacuum.available, optical_access, electrical.sample_connections, sample.diameter.max, cryogen.cryogen_free and cryogen.type. The only other keys are temperature.sweep_rate.max (GR-468 needs a ramp of at least 10 C/min) and humidity.range (GR-1221 needs 85-95% RH). set_contains uses {"needed": [...]}, which is the form cryolean/serialize.py reads.

The fibre-coupled detector, quantum-dot source and quantum-memory profiles have no optical_access requirement. The vocabulary defines optical_access as a window onto the sample, and their light arrives by fibre. Cryogen-free operation is marked optional (mandatory=false) wherever the source used a closed-cycle cooler but the physics does not require one.

Ideas from the suggested list that changed:
- **Thorlabs WDM report:** the page could not be retrieved (it is gated), so I used the Telcordia GR-1221-CORE 6.2.8 cyclic moisture test, taken from the ESPEC GR-1221 page.
- **JCU/Cryoelectra HTS cryogenic receiver paper:** it gives no operating temperature. I used Bian et al., Physica C 2010 instead (71.8 K on a mini Stirling cooler). Its quotes come from the abstract on a Consensus record page; I did not get the DOI.
- **Single Quantum SNSPD brochure:** left out because it overlaps the existing SNSPD characterization profile.

Quote formatting:
- The ESPEC quotes are table cells joined in reading order.
- Where pdftotext replaced the en dash, micro sign, multiplication sign or phi with placeholder characters, I put the original symbol back.
- The arXiv:1507.03210 'Detectors' quote is rejoined across a line-break hyphen.

Tool limits during the run: Tavily's quota ran out, the shared WebSearch budget was used up, and Lune's daily quota was exhausted. I read sources by downloading PDF/HTML directly and by WebFetch. A retry of the Thorlabs download was refused by the permission system as bot-check circumvention, and I did not work around it.

I edited nothing under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/.

eq.notes:
I wrote 8 configurations from 4 manufacturers to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\photonics_and_telecommunications\equipment.json. The manufacturers are Montana Instruments, ID Quantique, Quantum Design Oxford and ESPEC. Machines: CryoAdvance 100 with ATSM, CryoAdvance 100 with the OneK-Optic module, ID281 Pro, ID281 SO, OptistatDN-V, OptistatCF-V, ESPEC TSE-12-A and ESPEC Platinous EPX-2J. The 11 core keys are all filled for both ESPEC chambers. pressure.base is missing for every cryostat because no source gives a vacuum level. The SNSPD systems have no user sample size, and ID281 SO also lacks vacuum.available. Every missing key is listed in not_found with where I looked.

Search limits: the web search quota (200 per turn) and the Tavily plan limit ran out early in this run. All sources are manufacturer PDFs and pages I reached directly with WebFetch. PDF quotes come from text extracted out of the fetched PDFs, and table rows that wrap across lines are joined with single spaces. A script checked every PDF quote against the extracted text. Three quotes differ from the extraction only where a word is hyphenated across a line break in the source ('win-dows', 'latch-free'). Quotes from web pages were taken from WebFetch output and were not checked word for word.

Modelling choices:
- Single stated operating temperatures are stored as lo = hi at the conservative bound: ID281 Pro <3 K, ID281 SO <1 K, OneK-Optic <1.2 K.
- Absences use install=not_available (value kind unknown), or optional_not_installed for an option the family offers that is not fitted. Cryogen-free machines carry cryogen.type as the empty set.
- Rectangular chambers: sample.diameter.max is the smaller horizontal dimension and sample.height.max is the vertical clear height.
- SNSPD optical_access is fibre-only. It is recorded as true, and the claim says there is no free-space window.
- EPX-2J temperature.sweep_rate.max is the conservative cooling rate, 4 C/min.
- ESPEC TSE-12-A temperature.range spans its two exposure zones (-65 to 0 C and +60 to +200 C). There is no dwell set point between 0 and +60 C.
- CryoAdvance 100 has no magnet: Montana's system comparison chart offers the Magneto-Optic module only for the CryoAdvance 50.

Weakest evidence: the TSE-12-A optical_access absence relies on the catalog marking the viewing window as a TSD-101-W option. The magnet absences for the SNSPD systems, Optistats and ESPEC chambers rely on their full specification tables containing no magnet.

Candidates I dropped: Single Quantum Eos (the brochure only states 2.5 K, closed cycle, fibre or free-space window), Ricor K508 (a cooler only, with no dewar properties) and inTEST ThermoStream (datasheets sit behind a request form). Nothing outside my output file was edited.

results.note: Verified in arXiv:1507.03210 PDF text (Fig. 2 caption): 'We use MoSi SNSPDs with 70% detection efficiency at 1550 nm, at a temperature T < 2.5 K [27].' at_most 2500 mK matches the condition.

Fig. 2 caption quote verified verbatim. It describes D1-D3 heralding coincidences, which need current-biased, electrically read-out SNSPDs, so electrical.sample_connections present is a reasonable mandatory requirement. The quote supports it only indirectly.

Methods 'Detectors.' verified: 'The MoSi detectors were fabricated to obtain maximum efficiency at a wavelength of 1550 nm and for op-eration at 2.5 K in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler.' The sentence breaks across a column in the PDF. Optional cryogen_free=true is justified.
Section 3 quote verified verbatim. The 92.2% maximum SDE at 1550 nm was measured at 0.84 K, so at_most 840 mK is right.
Verified verbatim (Section 3): biased and read out through a cryogenic coaxial cable to a ZX85-12G-S+ bias tee at room temperature.
Abstract verified: 'the detector's SDE is over 70% when operated at a 2.1-K closed-cycle cryocooler.' Optional flag is appropriate.

Verified in arXiv:0903.3907: Fig. 3 caption reads 'Dark count rate vs detection efficiency at 1550 nm and 2.5 K.' The text says the 250 km data-line detector is the one characterised 'at 2.5 K'. point_within 2500 mK is correct.
Verified verbatim: bias current of 26.5 uA, quantum efficiency 2.65%, noise rate 5 Hz. A current-biased SSPD requires electrical connections.
Verified verbatim: the SINPHONIA sentence about a cryogen-free, closed cycle cryostat system (figure 2b). Optional flag is justified.
Fetched the ESPEC GR-468 page. The table row reads: '5.20 Temperature cycling -40 to 70°C (or 85°C) per Mil-Std 883, method 1010 100 to 1,000 cycles'. The range 233150-343150 mK is correct.
Same row, '(or 85°C)'. The 358150 mK upper limit is correct as an optional alternative.

Verified verbatim on the ESPEC page: '5.20 states: The procedure should agree with Method 1010 of MIL-STD 883C, with a minimum temperature ramp rate of 10°C/min.' The page also notes that Method 1010 limits hot/cold transfer to 1 minute, which is shock-like, so 10 K/min is a floor. at_least 10000 mK_per_min is consistent.

Fetched the ESPEC GR-1221 page. The 6.2.8 row reads: 'Cyclic Moisture Resistance Test 25 to 75°C cycling with 85-95%RH. One -40°C cycle per 5 sub-cycles (Mil-Std 883, method 1004)'. The range 233150-348150 mK is correct.

The quote is real, but 'humidity.range' is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json (185 keys, none for humidity). 'percent' is not a defined unit either, so this requirement cannot be compiled. A humidity key and unit must be added to the vocabulary first, or the requirement must be dropped. Without it the profile reduces to a temperature-range check and loses the defining 85-95% RH requirement.

The quoted text 'Any humidity model with -40 capability' is present, but it says nothing about vacuum. vacuum.available absent is inferred, not sourced. An 'absent' constraint would also wrongly penalise chambers that have a vacuum option they don't use.
Verified in the Cambridge HPL PDF, Section 2.2: 'The highly reflective face of the active mirror is cooled by direct contact with flowing cryogenic liquid cooled to 77 K[37].'
Verified verbatim: 'A 5 mm thick, 2 at. % Yb:YAG active mirror is mounted on a cryogenic cooling manifold enclosed in a vacuum chamber.'

The TFP seed-injection quote is verbatim (Joule-level section). It does not mention windows, but free-space pump and seed beams must reach active mirrors inside a vacuum enclosure, so optical access is physically required. The justification is indirect but sound.

Verified: '30 mm × 30 mm × 2 mm thick 3 at. % Yb:YAG section optically bonded on the four lateral faces to an absorbing Cr4+:YAG cladding'. sqrt(2)*30 mm = 42.426 mm, rounded up to 42427 um. With the cladding the real part is larger, so this is a conservative lower bound.

Verified verbatim: 'For the 1 kHz operation we report here, the disk assembly was cooled by liquid nitrogen to 77 K.' This refers to the regenerative-amplifier disk (front end), as the location says. Optional is fine. Caveat: no cryostat seed documents cryogen.type values, so this will evaluate as unknown everywhere.
Abstract verified: 'measured in the 80–300 K temperature range'. The range 80000-300000 mK is correct.
Abstract verified verbatim (Quantum Electronics 41(11) 1045-1050): 'The spectral and thermooptical characteristics of an Yb:YAG crystal were measured in the 80–300 K temperature range.'
Verified verbatim (Section 2): 'The cryostat was a vacuum chamber with a liquid nitrogen-cooled vessel, which was in direct thermal contact with the specimen under investigation.'
Verified: 'The λ ~ 938 nm pump radiation was directed onto the crystal through an optical window.'
Same verified sentence. A liquid-nitrogen-cooled vessel supports optional cryogen.type contains liquid_nitrogen. Caveat as above: no cryostat documents cryogen.type.

Verified in Europe PMC full text (PMC12354681): the source is installed in a compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler operating at a base temperature of 2.4 K. The paper attributes higher indistinguishability to 2.4 K vs 5 K. point_within 2400 mK is correct.
Verified verbatim: 'For bias voltage tuning, each micropillar on the chip is connected to electrical contacts by four narrow ridges 37 (Fig. 1 a).'

Verified verbatim (Introduction): 'We demonstrate the successful integration of our source in a compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler operating at a base temperature of 2.4 K.' Optional cryogen_free is justified.

Verified in arXiv:1907.07780, Section II: the crystal is cooled 'to a temperature of around 0.7 K using an adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator.' at_most 700 mK is acceptable, though slightly strict for 'around'.
Verified: AFCs 'are created under the application of a 3 kG magnetic field (oriented along the crystal c-axis)'. 3 kG = 300 mT.
Verified: 'The waveguide is exposed to magnetic fields up to 5 kG oriented parallel to the c-axis of the crystal.' 500 mT, optional.

vexp.summary:
I re-fetched every source except one and checked the quotes against the source text (PDFs via pdftotext, ESPEC pages via direct download, the Margaria paper via Europe PMC). Eight profiles check out: quotes are verbatim and numbers and units are correct. Bruno et al. (MoSi SNSPDs below 2.5 K), Xu et al. (0.84 K and 2.1 K), Stucki et al. (2.5 K, 26.5 uA, cryogen-free), both ESPEC pages for GR-468 and GR-1221, Reagan et al. (77 K, vacuum chamber, 30x30 mm mirrors, LN2 front end), Mukhin et al. (80-300 K, LN2 vacuum cryostat, optical window), Margaria et al. (2.4 K G-M, bias ridges) and Askarani et al. (~0.7 K ADR, 3 kG and 5 kG) all match.

Rejected: GR-1221 #1, because humidity.range and the percent unit are not in capability_vocabulary.json. Adding a humidity key is needed or the profile loses its defining RH requirement. GR-1221 #2, because vacuum absent is not supported by the quote. All four Bian HTS front-end requirements, because consensus.app is behind a sign-up wall, ScienceDirect returns 403, and the abstract is elided in Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar. Its source should be replaced with a retrievable primary source.

Notes: the cryogen.type set value 'liquid_nitrogen' is accepted, but no cryostat seed documents cryogen.type, so it will evaluate as unknown. Reagan optical_access is accepted on physical necessity; the quote is indirect.

No exact duplicates. Near-overlaps, not flagged: photon_microstrip_snspd_sub_kelvin vs expc_photonics_snspd_characterization (both measure 1550 nm SNSPD efficiency, but different device, source and temperature: 0.84 K vs 2.5 K). photon_fibre_pigtailed_qd_source vs expc_photonics_qd_autocorrelation (different source and measurement). photon_hts_receiver_frontend_72k vs expa_ybco_rf_filter (both HTS microwave filters near 72-77 K, different systems).

results.note: CryoAdvance-100 data sheet p.3: 'Platform temperature range (with ASTM) <3.4 K - 350 K'. The comparison chart also gives 3.4-350K. lo of 3.4 K is conservative.
p.1 key feature '3.4 K base temperature'.
p.3 'Environment Sample-in-vacuum'. The integrated roughing pump and valves are also stated.
p.1 'Sample-in-vacuum, cryogen-free'. The title says closed-cycle.
Cryogen-free closed-cycle, so the empty set is correct.

Systems comparison chart OPTIONS rows (Variable Temperature / Magnetic Field / <1.2K Add-On) read: CA50 ATSM / Magneto-Optic / -; CA100 ATSM / - / OneK-Optic. The manufacturer explicitly marks no magnetic-field option for the CryoAdvance 100. The chart footer reads 04/2025 although the file name says 06-23-25.
p.3 Optical ports: 5x 50 mm vacuum windows (4 radial + 1 top) with 30 mm internal cold windows.
5 windows (4 radial + 1 top). The chart also gives 4 side + 1 top.
The 30 mm cold window is the limiting aperture, so 30 mm is conservative.
p.2 'Standard I/O included: 4x RF, 25x DC' and '20x DC channels in vacuum chamber'.
'20x DC channels in vacuum chamber' is the conservative count to the sample (the side panel has 25).
p.3 '4x 20 GHz RF channels; semi-rigid lagged coax routed to sample chamber'.
The RF channels are rated 20 GHz (same quote).
Sample chamber 100 mm diameter x 116 mm height inside the radiation shield. This follows the repo precedent of using maximum sample-space dimensions (e.g. OptistatDry BLV).
116 mm height inside the radiation shield (same quote).
'Platform vibrational stability <15 nm ptp at base temperature'. The vocabulary shape is min (lower is better), so this is correct.
'Cooling power 90 mW @ 4.2 K'. The chart also gives 90 mW.

The OneK-Optic sheet gives '<1.2K Platform Temperature with module installed' and also documents operation at 1.2 K (Hold Time @ 1.2K >8 hrs; Cooling Power @ 1.2K), so the point range lo = hi = 1.2 K is a documented operating point. pdftotext puts the values in a shifted column, but the order maps cleanly.
p.1 'Base Temperature <1.2 Kelvin'.
'Temperature Stability (P-P) <10 mK'.
The module is an add-on to the sample-in-vacuum CryoAdvance 100. The CA100 sheet states 'Sample-in-vacuum'.
The CA100 is cryogen-free, and the OneK sheet says 'The closed-cycle system allows for low temperature operation greater than 8 hours with an automated recycle'.
Closed-cycle with an automated recycle, so the empty set is correct.
The comparison chart gives the CA100 Magnetic Field option as '-' and lists OneK-Optic as its <1.2K add-on. This is explicit.
'free space optical access to the sample space via two side optical windows'.
Spec table 'Optical Windows 2 side'.

The text says 'Up to 12 DC and 2 RF connections are possible with side panel feedthroughs'. Sample mounts are offered as 'RF/DC, RF only, DC only, flat sample plate, custom' ('with and without electrical connections'). The configuration_basis names no electrical sample mount, so connections at the sample are not established for this configuration. To accept, add an RF/DC sample mount to the configuration.

12 is an 'up to ... possible' maximum that depends on the chosen sample mount (a flat plate has none). Storing it as an installed count overstates what this configuration has. Accept only once the configuration fixes an RF/DC mount.
Same issue as dc_lines: 2 RF is an 'up to ... possible' maximum that depends on the sample mount, and no mount is specified.
'Interior Sample Space Ø63.5 mm x 40 mm'.
40 mm (same quote).
'Hold Time @ 1.2K >8 hrs' (recycle <3 hrs). Storing 8 h is conservative.

The brochure gives only 'Detector base temperature <3K', an upper bound. No operating point at 3 K is documented, so storing lo = hi = 3 K asserts something the source does not say. temperature.base (min 3 K) already captures the fact conservatively.
Spec table 'Detector base temperature <3K' (G.192.0143-PB-1.4, specs as of June 2026).

The full specification table (detectors, system runtime, base temperature, channels, dimensions, power, interface, operating temperature) lists no magnet for this fibre-coupled detector cryostat. That is a complete spec, not marketing silence.

'Rack-mounted, automated vacuum pump available'. Footnote (5) says the specs are for the rack-mounted vacuum pump option, which the configuration includes. The detectors sit in the evacuated cryostat; there is no user sample space.

Light reaches the detectors only by single-mode fibre (FC/PC), and the claim itself says no free-space window is specified. The project convention (photonics experiments notes) defines optical_access as a window onto the sample, with fibre-coupled systems deliberately excluded. Setting it true would falsely satisfy free-space optical-access requirements.
'Interface Optical inputs: FC/PC RF outputs: SMA female' plus built-in cryogenic amplifiers. Detector bias and readout is how the SNSPD experiments use this key.
'integrated in an automated and compact closed-cycle cryostat'.
Closed-cycle, so the empty set is correct.
Peak SDE '80% to 95% (or better)' and wavelengths '< 500 nm to > 2000 nm' are stated in the spec table.
'Each ID281 system optionally includes our Time Controller Series'. optional_not_installed is correct.
Only 'Detector base temperature <1K' (ID281 SO column) is given, an upper bound with no documented operating point at 1 K. lo = hi = 1 K is not supported. temperature.base covers it.
The ID281 brochure (G.192.0112-PB-1.2) cryostat table: ID281 SO '<1K', ID281 CO '>2K'.
The complete cryostat and detector specification tables list no magnet for this detector-only cryostat.
Fibre-coupled only ('Single mode fibre'; multimode on request), with no free-space window. The project convention excludes fibre-coupled systems from optical_access (a window onto the sample).
The detector readout is specified ('Output pulse width, voltage > 5 ns, > 100 mV'). Bias and readout of the detectors matches the SNSPD experiments' use of this key.

Footnote (5): 'Automated operation of the ID281 SO system gives indefinite continuous operation with a scheduled helium condensation cycle every day.' This is a closed-cycle cryostat with an internal sorption stage.
No external liquid cryogen, so the empty set is correct.
'Runtime at base temperature ≥ 24 hours (5)'. Storing 24 h is conservative.
The SDE and wavelength rows are present in the ID281 spec table.
The ID1000 time controller is explicitly optional. optional_not_installed is correct.
OptistatDN spec table, DN-V (Vacuum) column: '77.2 - 500 K'.
'ideal for experiments which require 77.2 K base temperature'.
'+/-0.1 K (measured over 10 mins)' is stored as 100 mK.
The full Optistat specification and ordering matrix (models, build codes, wiring, accessories, windows, power) contains no magnet. That is a complete specification.
Order code V5 'Sample in Vacuum (500 K)'. The DN-V column reads 'Vacuum'.
'Every cryostat is supplied with 4 x Spectrosil WF windows, fitted radially, and 1 x blank fitted axially.'
4 radial windows (the axial port is blanked).
'Optimised clear beam throughput (15/35 mm diameter aperture for DN and DN-V configurations respectively)'.
Wiring code 100 = '10 DC wires (10 pin)'. The configuration is OS-DN-V5-0-100.
10 DC wires (code 100).
'Maximum sample space 20 mm diameter' (both DN and DN-V).

50 mm is the sample-holder dimension ('20 mm wide x 50 mm long'), not a stated maximum sample space. For DN-V the stated maximum sample space is only '20 mm diameter', with no length. A holder length bounds the sample from above and is not a documented maximum sample height.
Model table, cooling technology for DN and DN-V: 'Nitrogen only'.
Cryogen code DN = Liquid Nitrogen.
'Liquid Nitrogen capacity 1.2 L' (integral reservoir).

'Hold time at 77 K >15 hrs'. The value is correct, but the key holding_time.static is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json (it appears only in research/v4), so it has to be added to the vocabulary before build-db.
OptistatCF spec table, CF-V 'push' column: 4.2-500 K. The pull mode (2.3 K) with pump is correctly not claimed.
4.2 K in push mode is conservative.
'+/-0.1 K (measured over 10 mins)'.
The complete Optistat spec and ordering matrix contains no magnet.
Order code V5 'Sample in Vacuum (500 K)'. The product page says 'A 4K Helium Flow, Sample-in-Vacuum Cryostat'.
4 x Spectrosil WF radial windows supplied.
4 radial windows.
Wiring code 100 = '10 DC wires (10 pin)'. The configuration is OS-HE-V5-712-100.
10 DC wires.
CF-V 'Maximum sample space 30 mm wide x 58 mm long'. The product page says 'Sample Space: 30 x 58 mm vacuum'. Treating the 30 mm width as a disc diameter in the sample plane is acceptable.
58 mm long, as stated for the maximum sample space.

The value (false) is right, but the quote 'A 4K Helium Flow, Sample-in-Exchange Gas Cryostat' comes from the Optistat CF (exchange-gas) tab, not the CF-V. The CF-V tab reads 'A 4K Helium Flow, Sample-in-Vacuum Cryostat'. Alternatively, cite the matrix model table 'Helium or Nitrogen' (CF-V column). Re-source with the CF-V quote.
Matrix cooling technology for CF-V: 'Helium or Nitrogen'. The product page comparison says 'Helium (or Nitrogen)'.
'0.45 L/hr for the CF-V' = 0.0075 L/min (exact).

The catalog gives two disjoint exposure ranges: hot +60 to +200 C and cold -65 to 0 C. The two-zone TSE has no ambient zone, so nothing is documented between 0 and +60 C. The single range [-65, +200] C claims set points in that gap (e.g. 25 C) that are not documented. The NA page's '-65 to 200°C' is the same union. Store the cold and hot ranges separately or leave this key unknown.
NA model page 'Temperature Range -65 to 200°C'. The catalog gives cold exposure -65 to 0 C. 208150 mK is correct.
Catalog TSE-12-A table 'Temperature fluctuation *2 ± 0.5' (IEC 60068-3-5). The NA page gives ±0.5°C.
The complete construction/performance/utility specification and options list contains no magnet.

An air-to-air shock chamber: 'Uniform airflow in the test area', and the cable-port plug 'Prevents air leakage'. The NA page mentions sirocco blowers that circulate the air. The test area is explicitly air-filled.
Same basis as vacuum: an air-filled, air-circulated test area.
The options page tags 'Viewing window' as TSD only. The p.2 footnote assigns the viewing window to the TSD and the recorder/e-stop to the TSE. This is explicit.
Fittings: 'Cable port ID 50mm' and 'Specimen power supply control terminal'. The NA page gives 'Tube for cables to test load, 2" diameter'.
'Inner volume of test area 10.9 L'. The key chamber.volume is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json and needs adding.
Test area W320×H148×D230 mm. Using the smaller horizontal dimension (230 mm) is conservative.
Test area height 148 mm. The NA page gives 150 mm; the catalog value is the more conservative.
'Load capacity of test area 8 kg'.
'Mechanical cascade refrigeration system', 'Rotary 1.5 kW ×2'. The LN2 and LCO2 auxiliary cooling injectors are listed only as options.
No cryogen in the standard configuration, so the empty set is correct.
NA page 'Temperature Range: -70 to 180°C'. The brochure EPX column gives -70°C to 180°C. 203150-453150 mK is correct.
'6°C/min heating 4°C/min cooling -40 to 125°C (Empty)'. The brochure EPX-2J gives 6 / 4 °C/m. Storing 4 K/min, an average rate for an empty chamber, is conservative.
'Temperature Fluctuation (at control sensor) ±0.3°C (up to 100°C)'. It is qualified: only specified up to 100 C.
Brochure '±0.7°C (up to 100°C)' (empty chamber, at supply air). Same qualification: only specified up to 100 C.

veq.summary:
I re-downloaded all 8 source documents (pdftotext) plus the Optistat and ESPEC NA web pages, and checked 102 capabilities: 92 accepted, 10 rejected.

Rejected:
- **OneK-Optic electrical (3):** sample_connections, dc_lines and coax_lines. The source says 'Up to 12 DC and 2 RF ... possible', and that depends on the sample mount; the configuration names no RF/DC mount.
- **ID281 temperature.range (2), Pro and SO:** stored as lo = hi from '<3K' / '<1K'. These are upper bounds, not documented operating points; temperature.base already covers them.
- **ID281 optical_access (2), Pro and SO:** fibre-only. The project convention says optical_access means a window onto the sample.
- **OptistatDN-V sample.height.max:** 50 mm is the sample-holder length, not the stated maximum sample space.
- **OptistatCF-V cryogen.cryogen_free:** the value is right, but the quote comes from the CF exchange-gas tab, not the CF-V.
- **TSE-12-A temperature.range:** the stored [-65, 200] C joins two separate exposure ranges and claims the undocumented 0 to +60 C gap.

All values, units and conversions in the accepted items match. Every not_available absence rests on a full spec/options matrix or an explicit statement: the Montana chart's '-' for the CryoAdvance 100 magnet, ESPEC 'Viewing window TSD' only, and air-filled test areas.

The keys chamber.volume, humidity.range and holding_time.static are not in data/capability_vocabulary.json and need adding before build-db.

Cross-industry duplicates: TSE-12-A (semiconductors) and OptistatDN-V (astronomy).

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 energy_and_hydrogen profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\energy_and_hydrogen\experiments.json as {industry, experiments}. That is the only file I wrote in the repo; the build script is in the scratchpad (build_energy_h2.py). A check confirmed that every id and plain_name is new against data/experiments, and that every key exists in data/capability_vocabulary.json or in the v4 new_keys.

Coverage: HTS tape Ic in LN2 (IEC 61788-26), Ic versus strain at 77 K (Zhou 2016), Ic at 4.2 K and 20 K up to 19 T (Senatore 2024), SFCL subcooled-LN2 cooling system at 71 K / 500 kPa (Hong 2015), SFCL prototype fault-current sharing at 77 K / 200 A (Ali & Banerjee), LH2 boil-off reduction in SMiRF (NASA CBRS), 125,000 L LH2 zero-boil-off tank (NASA IRAS), ortho-para conversion heat exchanger at 30-80 K / 2.1 MPa (Wei et al.), hydrogen-precharged 316plus tensile tests at 77 K and 20 K (Li et al.), and a Roebel HTS cable at 77 K / 500 A (Goldacker).

Mandatory requirements use core-passport keys wherever the physics allows: temperature.range, cryogen.type, magnetic_field.max, vacuum.available, pressure.base, sample.diameter.max, sample.height.max (often as an any-of with sample.length.max) and electrical.sample_connections. They also use these new keys: electrical.current_leads.max, pressure.max_working, cooling_power.at_20000mK, chamber.volume and temperature.shroud.range. The 316plus profile also requires module.cryogenic_tensile or module.cryogenic_tensile_test.

Things the reviewer should know:
1. Tool limits stopped some research. Tavily extract hit its usage limit, WebSearch hit its 200-search cap, Lune's daily quota is used up (resets 2026-11-02; billing page https://luneresearch.com/dashboard/settings/billing), and Consensus is rate-limited (its free-tier notice says Consensus Pro returns more results: https://consensus.app/pricing/?utm_source=claude_desktop). techrxiv and mdpi.com returned 403. So I dropped three ideas: the 2G HTS cable cold test (techrxiv 403), the MDPI LH2 boil-off modelling paper (403), and the ISO 21903 LNG flow measurement (its free preview has no temperature or flow-rate numbers). I replaced them with the arXiv SFCL Hall-mapping paper and the arXiv Roebel cable paper. A real LNG/LN2 flow-calibration profile still needs a facility paper.
2. Some quotes came through WebFetch's summarising model rather than my own PDF text extraction. These are the IEC 61788-26 scope fragments, the Hong SFCL abstract sentences, the Senatore sentences and the Wei et al. abstract. Each one is a short fragment that was asked for verbatim, but they should be spot-checked against the source.
3. Some numbers are worked out from the text rather than printed in it:
   - Zhou: Ic of about 80 A comes from "less than 4 A (i.e., 5%)". This requirement is non-mandatory.
   - IRAS: 18.5 psia is stored as 127554 Pa, rounded up as the unit rules require.
   - IEC: the 77 K temperature quote comes from the Zhou paper, because the IEC abstract only says "liquid nitrogen bath at ambient pressure".
   - IEC: the 300 A current-lead requirement covers the standard's full scope of Ic up to 300 A.
4. Two LN2-at-77 K tape and cable profiles (Goldacker Roebel cable and Zhou strain test) have no mandatory cryogen.type requirement, because their sources do not explicitly say "liquid nitrogen" for that test.
5. The 316plus profile overlaps in theme with the existing expa_hydrogen_304l_tensile and expc_energy_tensile_20k. It is still a different procedure: a different steel, electrochemical charging, and gas-cooled tests at both 77 K and 20 K.
6. Many machines may not document electrical.current_leads.max, pressure.max_working, chamber.volume or temperature.shroud.range. Those pairs will stay NEED_MORE_INFORMATION until the equipment agents document these keys.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\energy_and_hydrogen\equipment.json (builder script: C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\eh2_machines_build.py). 8 configurations, 6 machines, 4 manufacturers (Bluefors Cryocooler Technologies/Cryomech, Stirling Cryogenics, THEVA, Micromeritics); none duplicate the catalog. Research constraint: the Tavily quota was exhausted and the shared WebSearch budget was used up when this task started, so I chose machines from manufacturer sites I could reach by fetching known product URLs and their linked datasheets directly. I read the PDFs from the fetched copies. Categories covered: LN2-bath Ic measurement of HTS tape (TAPESTAR XL / XL-HF); SFCL / HTS-cable LN2 re-liquefaction, sub-cooling and 80 K zero-boil-off cooling (SPC-1, AL600); 20 K helium-loop and LH2 / hydrogen-liquefaction cooling (SPC-1T, AL630); hydrogen-sorption isotherms at 77 K and 25-350 K (3Flex). Not covered: LH2/LNG storage tanks. The Cryofab CLH 100/250 LH2 container datasheets give net capacity 100/250 L, NER 2.0/1.6 % and MAWP 345 kPa (50 psi) but no storage temperature, so they were not used. Also not covered: cryogenic load frames, LNG flow-calibration rigs and variable-temperature high-field Ic facilities. Every core passport key is documented as a value or a sourced absence, except sample.diameter.max and sample.height.max for the two 3Flex configurations (see not_found). Conventions: absences use install=not_available with value kind unknown, as in the sibling industry files. Bare cryocoolers document the cold-end interface diameter (AL600/AL630 127 mm) and sourced absences for sample height, vacuum, optics, wiring and magnet. The SPC-1 and SPC-1T cryogenerators have no sample interface (they cool a process stream or a helium loop), so their sample sizes are recorded as not_available. Conservative choices: (1) AL600/AL630 values are for a 60 Hz supply (50 Hz: 580 W at 80 K, 90 W at 20 K). (2) AL600 temperature.range is 25-80 K and AL630 is 17-40 K because the published capacity data stop there; point requirements above those temperatures will read DOES_NOT_MEET even though the coolers may physically run warmer. (3) SPC-1 cooling power at 77/80 K (400 W) and SPC-1T at 20 K (50 W) are the lower ends of the printed ranges ('400 W to 2,7 kW at temperatures of 50-160 K', '50-175 W @ 20-60 K'), not curve readings. (4) pressure.max_working for SPC-1/SPC-1T is a gauge value (barg). (5) TAPESTAR temperature is 77 K: THEVA's product page states '@ 77 K' for the XL-HF, while the XL/XL-HF datasheets say 'liquid nitrogen temperature' with LN2 at 0.05 MPa overpressure, so the bath may be slightly above 77 K. (6) The 3Flex pressure.base is the lowest pressure of the specified analysis range (1e-6 Torr), not a stated ultimate vacuum. Accessed 2026-11-01.

results.note: IEC webstore abstract re-fetched: 'the test specimen is immersed in liquid nitrogen bath at ambient pressure' is there; liquid_nitrogen is the right cryogen; mandatory is justified.
The Zhou 2016 PDF (utwente) Introduction has the quote exactly. LN2 at ambient pressure is about 77 K, so point_within 77000 mK is consistent with the IEC bath condition.

The quote and the 300 A value are verified in the IEC abstract. Rejected because the key electrical.current_leads.max does not exist in capability_vocabulary.json. The nearest key is electrical.current.max (max, unit pA, 'Maximum excitation current of the installed electrical module'). Re-key it as at_least 300 A.
The scope sentence is verified in the IEC abstract. A DC transport Ic measurement needs sample current and voltage connections, so present on electrical.sample_connections is right.
'applies to test specimens shorter than 300 mm' is verified in the IEC abstract. Optional at_least 300 mm on length/height is a reasonable upper envelope.
The abstract sentence is verbatim in the Zhou 2016 PDF, and 77 K is correct.
Section III.A has the sentence verbatim ('10 uV/m criterion'; the mu glyph is lost in extraction). Four-point transport justifies sample connections.

The quote is verbatim (Section IV.A). Rejected for two reasons. (1) The key electrical.current_leads.max is not in the vocabulary; use electrical.current.max. (2) The 80 A figure is back-calculated from '4 A (i.e., 5%)'. It is not a stated Ic, Table I values are not in the extractable text, and evidence_status experimental_observation overstates an inference.

'Fixation by soldering of the 45 mm tape length...' is verbatim in Section III.A. Optional at_least 45 mm is fine. The separate stress-strain rig used 90 mm samples, but that is not part of this Ic-strain measurement.
The abstract sentence is verified (OpenAlex abstract and the UNIGE open-access full text). range_within 4.2 K to 20 K is correct.
'magnetic fields up to 19 T' is verified. magnetic_field.max at_least 19000 mT is correct.
Section 2 full text: 'we have designed a custom setup for high-current, high-precision critical current measurements' is verified. Transport E-I measurements justify sample connections.

The quote is verified ('up to 2 kA in liquid helium and up to 1 kA in helium gas flow'). Rejected only because electrical.current_leads.max is not a vocabulary key. Re-key it to electrical.current.max at_least 1000 A (optional).
The quote is verified in Section 2. Optional liquid_helium is right for the 4.2 K data.
'on special adapters that host 125 mm-long samples' is verified (Section 2 and the Fig. 2 caption). Optional at_least 125 mm is fine.
The abstract (via OpenAlex; the IOP page is bot-walled) contains 'The normal operation condition of the main cryostat is 71 K and 500 kPa.' point_within 71 K is correct.

The 500 kPa value and the quote are verified. Rejected because pressure.max_working is not in capability_vocabulary.json. The only related keys are pressure.operating.range (range, Pa) and pressure.base. Either add a vocabulary key or re-key this requirement.
The abstract contains 'they are submerged in sub-cooled liquid nitrogen for their stable thermal characteristics'. liquid_nitrogen is correct.
arXiv:2112.00433 PDF: 'although in the present case, we operate down to liquid Nitrogen temperature of 77 K.' is verbatim, and the setup is dipped in LN2 at 77 K.
'The cryostat holds up to 80 liters of liquid Nitrogen with a loss rate of 3 liters per hour.' is verbatim, and the SCFCL setup is immersed in it.

The quote is present (it reads 'IT'/'ISC' without spaces in the PDF), and 200 A is the correct total pulsed current. Rejected because electrical.current_leads.max is not a vocabulary key. Re-key it to electrical.current.max at_least 200 A.

The 12 cm length is verified: the sentence is split by the column layout, and the Table I length is 120 mm. The tube axis is vertical (z measured along the vertical axis). Note that the copper braids are 200 mm, so 120 mm is a lower bound.
The Hall-array readout sentence is verified (as 'VH'; Keysight 34980A). Current leads plus sensor wiring justify sample connections.
NTRS 20150000134 PDF: the 'vacuum of 1x10-6 torr or better' sentence is verbatim. vacuum.available is correct.
The same quote is verified. pressure.base (min shape) at_most 1e-6 Torr is consistent; Torr is in units.py.

vexp.summary:
I re-checked all 10 Energy and hydrogen profiles (42 requirements) against the original sources and accepted 32. Every quote was found in its source; all ten rejections are vocabulary or evidence problems.

Sources:
- I downloaded and text-searched the Zhou, CBRS, IRAS, Ali-Banerjee and Goldacker PDFs and the 316plus arXiv page.
- I read the IEC 61788-26 abstract on the IEC webstore.
- The IOP pages block automated access, so for the SFCL-cooling and ortho-para papers I checked the abstracts through OpenAlex. For Senatore 2024 I used the full text from the University of Geneva open archive.

Rejected:
- **Missing vocabulary keys (9).** These keys do not exist in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so the backend cannot evaluate them:
  - electrical.current_leads.max, used 5 times. Suggest re-keying to electrical.current.max.
  - pressure.max_working, used 3 times.
  - chamber.volume, used once.
  - temperature.shroud.range, used once.
- **Inferred value (1).** The 80 A current in the strain profile is back-calculated from '4 A (i.e., 5%)' rather than stated in the paper. It is rejected as well as having the bad key.

Minor issues (not grounds for rejection):
- Every entry has accessed 2026-11-01, which is after today's date (2026-10-31).
- The 316plus equipment description 'silvered, vacuum-insulated glass' is not in the v2 text, which says only 'vacuum-insulated Dewar chamber'.
- The Senatore profile says the work is for 'compact fusion', but the paper says ultra-high-field magnets in the 30–50 T range.
- The 18.5 psia pressure figure in the IRAS profile understates the 32.3 psia the tank actually reached in the duty-cycle tests.

Duplicates: the 316plus hydrogen-embrittlement tensile profile measures the same thing as the existing expa_hydrogen_304l_tensile profile and overlaps expc_energy_tensile_20k. The other nine profiles are distinct from each other and from existing data/experiments profiles.

veq.summary:
I checked all 5 machines (7 configurations) against their sources. I downloaded and rendered every Cryomech, Stirling, THEVA and Micromeritics PDF to check table rows and graph values, and fetched the THEVA and Micromeritics product pages.

None of them is already in data/cryostats or data/cryolean.db, and none repeats within the batch.

**Rejected: 6 capabilities**
- **AL600 and AL630 `sample.diameter.max` = 127 mm.** That is the diameter of the bare copper cold tip, not a limit on sample size. It also contradicts the "no sample space" basis. It should be not_available or unknown.
- **TAPESTAR XL and XL-HF `sample.height.max` = 20 mm.** That is the reel core width. The vocabulary defines the key as height/thickness, and the datasheet gives the tape limit "Max. thickness 200 µm". Use 200 µm.
- **3Flex, both configurations, `pressure.base` = 1e-6 Torr.** That is the analysis range from the chemisorption column of the spec table; the physisorption column says "1.3 x 10-9 to 1.0 P/P0". It is not a base pressure either, and no ultimate vacuum is documented.

**Accepted with wording fixes**
- **THEVA claims.** The vacuum.available and pressure.base claims say the dewar runs above atmospheric pressure. The 0.05 MPa figure is the LN2 supply requirement, so the claim text needs correcting.
- **SPC-1 `cryogen.type`.** The claim says the heat exchanger "holds" LN2, which the datasheet does not say. It should say the system uses nitrogen as the fluid it liquefies.

**Vocabulary gaps.** These keys are not in data/capability_vocabulary.json, and build validation will reject them until they are added: cooling_power.at_80000mK, cooling_power.at_77000mK, pressure.max_working, holding_time.static, electrical.current_leads.max.

**Graph checks**
- SPC-1 has about 1.1 kW gross and 0.9 kW net N2 at 77 K, so the 400 W lower bound is conservative.
- SPC-1T has about 52 to 80 W at 20 K depending on first-stage load, so the 50 W lower bound holds.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 nuclear and fusion profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\nuclear_engineering_and_fusion\experiments.json. The file has the same content as above, and every requirement in it also carries accessed=2026-11-01 and an evidence_status. I read every quote from the source PDF itself, using alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries or the arXiv abstract page.

To avoid duplicating the existing profiles:
- I left out SULTAN ITER CICC testing, because expa_cicc_critical_current already covers it.
- The ITER coil cold test and the torus cryopump test are already in the catalog. My tritium-panel test is a different experiment: it pumps tritium at the JET Active Gas Handling System.
- The physics batch already has phys_rebco_cable_ic_12t, so I did not add a REBCO cable Ic test.
- The DEMO cryodistillation paper (Butler/Shaw) is a ProSim modelling study with no experiment in it, so I replaced it with a second entry from the TFMC paper: the 50 kA current-lead qualification.

Points the checker should know:
- The SPARC TFMC makes its own 20 T field, so I did not add a requirement on magnetic_field.max.
- The ST40 pellet injector is a published conceptual design based on proven ORNL hardware. Its requirements are marked manufacturer_specification.
- The two HPGe profiles are split on purpose. The lab method requires an LN2 dewar and a crystal at or below 77.15 K, taken from the document's -196 C. The in-situ method requires a cryogen-free system at or below 113.15 K, from -160 C.
- When a source gives a value only as an approximate or achieved condition, I made that requirement non-mandatory. Examples are the TFMC 1e-6 torr vacuum, the ICSI 1.2 bar and 0.3 m3 cold box, and the 30 L HPGe dewar.
- The 20 mm sample diameter for the Cu TGS profile is my calculation: the diagonal of the 13 x 15 mm sample (19.85 mm), rounded up. It is non-mandatory and the rationale says so.
- Pressures were converted exactly: 20 bar = 2000000 Pa and 1.2 bar = 120000 Pa.

The research tools ran out partway through. The WebSearch budget for this turn was used up, Tavily hit its plan limit, and Lune's daily quota is exhausted until 2026-11-02 00:00 UTC (credits can be added at https://luneresearch.com/dashboard/settings/billing). Because of this I could not find sources for other candidates, such as ITER HTS current-lead type tests and post-irradiation REBCO Ic measurements in fission reactors. I did not edit anything under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\nuclear_engineering_and_fusion\equipment.json. 8 configurations from 4 manufacturers (Linde Kryotechnik, Bluefors/Cryomech, SHI Cryogenics, ORTEC/AMETEK), accessed 2026-11-01. Every quote was checked by script against the text of the downloaded page or PDF (pdftotext), comparing with whitespace normalised. Tavily, WebSearch and Lune quotas were exhausted, so pages and PDFs were read directly (curl + pdftotext, built-in browser) from manufacturer URLs. Mirion's Cryo-Pulse 5 Plus page returned 403 or 'page moved'. Not included: SULTAN-type conductor facilities and ITER cryopump test stands (bespoke facilities, already in the catalog as expansion_a_epfl_sultan and expansion_a_iter_cryopump_test); pellet injectors and hydrogen-isotope distillation columns (no commercial datasheets); commercial cryopumps (the SHI Marathon CP datasheet gives pumping speeds and capacities but no cryopanel temperature or base pressure); in-situ irradiation cryostats (no manufacturer page reachable). Absences use install=not_available with the complete standard-scope-of-supply or component list as the scope-defining quote (flags b=false, other shapes kind unknown), following the physics agent's Linde L70 entries. Closed-cycle machines carry cryogen.type = []. Linde LR refrigerators are rated at 4.4 K, so their capacity is not stored under cooling_power.at_4200mK (there is no 4.4 K key); temperature.range is lo = hi = 4.4 K, and cryogen.type includes liquid_helium because the refrigerator delivers 4.4 K helium to the cryostat. SHI marks its minimum temperatures 'for reference only'. For the SHI coolers, temperature.range spans only the documented points (minimum and rating temperature), which may under-state the warm end because the capacity maps are graphical; a reviewer may prefer unknown here. The Cryomech AL600 sheet prints '430 W at 600 K' (a typo for 60 K), which is not used. Conservative values: CH-160D3LT 90 W at 20 K (50 Hz). AL630/AL600 values are certified at 60 Hz, and their configurations state a 60 Hz supply. The MOBIUS hold time is stored as the lower bound of 7 days (168 h) of the printed 'approximately 7–10 days'. HPGe configurations: crystal temperature and sample-space size are not published, so temperature.range/base and sample size are unknown (listed in not_found); all other passport keys are documented. Cooling powers use unit W (registered), not nW. Extra keys used beyond the passport: cooling_power.at_20000mK, cooling_power.at_80000mK (new key), cooling_power.at_4200mK, cooldown_time.max, cryogen.liquid_nitrogen_required, cryogen.dewar_volume, holding_time.static (new key).

results.note: Verified verbatim in the arXiv:2308.12301 abstract, PDF p1: 'A novel liquid-free cryocooler-based cryogenic system provided 20 K supercritical helium.' 20 K = 20000 mK.

Verified in the abstract (spans PDF p1-p2), with the same numbers repeated on p11 and p13: '20.1 T peak field-on-conductor with 40.5 kA of terminal current'. Note: the key electrical.current_leads.max is not in capability_vocabulary.json and must be added to the vocabulary or manifest. The closest existing key is electrical.current.max (pA).

The quote is verbatim in the abstract (p2), and p12 has 'the system confirmed 600 W of cooling power at 20 K'. But 600 W is the capacity the facility provided, not a heat load the test needed. The paper never says the coil test needed 600 W. A mandatory at_least 600 W would wrongly exclude smaller systems that could carry the actual load. Accept only as mandatory:false.

Verified on p10: the case 'serves as a pressure vessel to enable single-pass 20 bar supercritical helium flow'. The abstract also gives a 'maximum design pressure of 20 bar-a'. 20 bar = 2,000,000 Pa. Mandatory is justified because the coolant loop runs at 20 bar. Note: pressure.max_working is not in the current vocabulary.
Verified in the abstract, p1: 'inside a large 20 m3 vacuum cryostat, which contains internal LN2 radiation shields'.

Verified on p1: 'Weighing 10,058 kg (22,174 lb) and utilizing 270 km (168 mi) of REBCO'. On p10 the cryostat support structure is 'designed to properly support the approximately 10-ton TFMC magnet'. The coil is the test object, so sample.mass.max is the right key.
Verified on p10: 'High vacuum in the 10-6 to 10-7 torr range was routinely achieved during experiments.' This is optional and the bound (at most 1e-6 Torr) is correct.
Verified on p10: 'A 35-ton SS316 vacuum cryostat with 20 m3 internal volume'. 20 m3 = 20000 L. This is optional. Note: chamber.volume is not in the current vocabulary.

Verified on p11: 'post-TFMC testing demonstrated stable operation at 50 kA, the maximum current available from the power supply.' The abstract also says the leads were 'experimentally qualified up to 50 kA'. Note: electrical.current_leads.max is not in the vocabulary.
Verified on p10 (Section VI.B): 'A set of binary LN2-cooled 50 kA REBCO current leads and a VIPER cable feeder system were designed and built in-house at MIT PSFC.'
Verified on p11: 'a large LN2 reservoir housed within the current lead vacuum cryostat, which also serves as the cryostat radiation shield.'

Verified on p11: 'external claw pumps provide the ability to subcool the LN2 to 65 K by reducing the vacuum pressure in the chamber.' This is optional, which is correct because subcooling is a capability, not a requirement.
Verified on p11: 'Each of the approximately 3 m tall CLS consists of three sections.' The leads are the device under test, so the enclosure must take a body about 3 m tall. The value is approximate.

Verified in Section III (PDF p5): 'then smoothly lowered to ~7 K and kept stable to ensure good resistance of cryogenic projectiles.' The paper says this was key to reaching launch speeds above 3 km/s, so mandatory is justified. The quoted page numbers (p3/p4) do not match PDF pages 5/6.
Verified on PDF p6: '1.5 W @ 4.2 K on the second (nominal minimum temperature without thermal load is 2.8 K)'. This is optional and is the specification of the upgraded PT415.
Verified on PDF p5: 'The injector features many innovative solutions, such as a cryogen-free cryostat'. It is a design choice, so optional is correct.

Verified on p6: 'can achieve a low temperature of ~ 8 K in this design configuration.' This is the operating point of a conceptual design, not a stated hard requirement. It is acceptable as the barrel freezing temperature. The quote is in Section 3.2, which starts on p5.
Verified on p6: 'The guard vacuum chamber that surrounds the injector to provide thermal insulation has been selected to be a welded chamber'.

Verified on p6: 'The guard vacuum chamber must be pumped to approximately a 10-2 mbar pressure level in order to obtain good thermal performance'. The word 'must' justifies mandatory. 0.01 mbar = 1 Pa.
Verified on p6: '10-inch conflat flanges on the front, top, and sides to connect the barrels, cryocooler, and electrical connections respectively.' Optional is correct.

vexp.summary:
I downloaded all 9 source PDFs and checked every quote against the extracted text. Every quote or equivalent passage is really there, and the numbers and units match. I rejected 7 of the 51 requirements:
- **SPARC 600 W at 20 K:** marked mandatory, but 600 W is what the facility could provide, not what the test needed.
- **JET cryopump height (3.2 m) and diameter (185 mm):** wrong key. These describe the pump vessel, which is effectively the cryostat, not the sample.
- **Lab HPGe, liquid nitrogen marked mandatory:** the NRA method explicitly allows electric cooling as well.
- **Field HPGe, cryogen-free marked mandatory:** the IAEA text says liquid nitrogen is the traditional way to cool in-situ detectors.
- **ICSI 1.2 bar maximum pressure:** the quote is stitched together from a table, and the value is a sample pressure, not the column's working pressure.

One fix: the TGS sample's equivalent diameter is corrected from 20 mm to 19.85 mm, the 13 x 15 mm diagonal.

Three keys used here are not in capability_vocabulary.json: electrical.current_leads.max, pressure.max_working and chamber.volume. They need to be proposed in a manifest before these profiles can be built. Some quoted page numbers are journal page numbers rather than PDF page numbers; they are correct after the offset.

There are no duplicates. The new profiles overlap in topic with the existing ITER coil cold-test and ITER torus cryopump profiles, but they use different setups, temperatures and measurements, and every plain_name is unique.

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 manufacturing experiment profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\manufacturing_and_industrial_processing\experiments.json (same layout as the other industries' files, accessed 2026-11-01). Nothing under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ was touched.

Every requirement quotes its source word for word (at most 50 words) and gives the URL, title and location. Quotes from local text (Europe PMC full text, and the Chalmers, AWS and KSC PDFs run through pdftotext) were checked by script. Quotes from the two MDPI pages and the Springer page were copied from the read-only built-in browser and were not re-checked. Several AWS and KSC quotes contain degree signs that pdftotext garbled; I restored them as ° assuming that is what the PDF prints, and the AWS axis-label quote is pdftotext output only.

Problems during research: the WebSearch budget and the Tavily quota ran out, and OpenAlex, Consensus and scite were rate-limited or blocked. I read sources with WebFetch, Europe PMC full text, local pdftotext of PDFs that WebFetch had saved, and the read-only built-in browser (no sign-in, no forms).

Ideas from the list I did not use:
- **CryoMill grinding of heat-sensitive powders**: duplicates the existing rubber cryomilling profile and the chemistry and biology cryomill profiles.
- **Bombardier bushing PPS 12.04**: the URL returns 404.
- **ASTM D2137 rubber brittleness**: the public page has no numeric conditions.
- **Ayed LN2 supply pressure/flow paper**: 403.
- **D2 nano-carbide paper**: 404.
- **Purdue LN2 shrink-fit paper**: PDF 403.
- **Two papers behind Cloudflare/bot checks** (a cryogenic-treatment paper on cemented-carbide drill bits, and an IOP paper on low-temperature aluminium sheet forming): I did not try to get past the checks.

In their place I added gear-steel cryotreatment in an LN2-aerosol furnace, carburized-steel cold treatment at -80 C, Al 1050 cryorolling, and two KSC acceptance tests.

How some requirements are written:
- **Calculated sample diameters**: in a few profiles sample.diameter.max is the circumscribed diameter of the quoted footprint, rounded up (sheet 60.02 mm, 20 mm cube 28.29 mm, 60x60 mm block 84.86 mm). The arithmetic is in each rationale; the quote holds the source dimensions.
- **Tyre**: sample.diameter.max uses the quoted 13 inch rim diameter as a lower bound. The tyre's outer diameter is larger but is not printed in the source, so it was not computed.
- **LN2 flow not converted**: the Inconel paper gives 0.5 kg/min, which cannot become cryogen.flow_rate.max in L/min without a density assumption. Only the 1.5 bar delivery pressure is used (as pressure.max_working).
- **Temperature for LN2 processes**: to avoid false failures from slightly different ways of documenting LN2 temperature (77 K vs 77.15 K), these profiles rely on cryogen.type containing liquid_nitrogen and on temperature.base at_most a sourced threshold (for the tyre, Tg = 215 K). A point at -196 C (77150 mK) is mandatory only where the procedure itself states -196 C. Where the -196 C figure comes from the Chalmers thesis as a reference value, that requirement is non-mandatory.
- **Gauge vs absolute pressure**: the Chalmers thesis (6.8 bar) and the Inconel paper (1.5 bar) do not say which. I treated the printed value as the needed working pressure.
- **Keys outside the core passport** (all in data/capability_vocabulary.json): dwell.duration.max, operating_duration.max, temperature.heating_rate.range, module.sample_thermometry.

Overlap with other industries: the LNG weld Charpy test at -196 C is similar in temperature to materials' high-Mn steel Charpy profile (mat_charpy_impact_ln2_high_mn_steel) but is a weld-consumable qualification. The plain_names differ from each other and from all existing ones. Its mandatory content is only the -196 C test temperature; the other two requirements are optional.

eq.notes:
Output file: C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\manufacturing_and_industrial_processing\equipment.json. It holds 8 configurations (8 equipment entries) from 6 manufacturers: RETSCH, ZwickRoell, Qualitest (3 machines), Tinius Olsen, Cryogenics International and Cole-Parmer SamplePrep/SPEX. All sources were accessed 2026-11-01. None of them duplicates data/cryostats: the RETSCH CryoMill, the RETSCH MM 400 and the Messer cabinet already in the catalog are different machines. None duplicates another v4 agent either: the SP CharpyCool is already in materials_and_nanotechnology.

Every quote was checked automatically. Each one appears word for word, with whitespace normalised, in the downloaded source page or PDF, and each is 50 words or fewer.

Research constraint: the Tavily quota had run out and the run's shared WebSearch budget was already used up when this agent started. Machines were found by navigating the manufacturers' own websites and sitemaps and reading their pages and PDFs directly. Four categories have no machine because no complete specification could be reached: LN2 cryogenic-machining delivery systems, cryogenic valve test rigs, industrial cryogenic grinding lines and LN2 shrink-fit baths. KGW-Isotherm Kaltgas LN2 cold-gas systems for shrink-fitting and Charpy conditioning were reviewed and rejected because they publish no sample-space dimensions.

Absences (no magnet, no sample vacuum, no base pressure, no window, no sample wiring) are recorded as install=not_available only where a complete technical-data table defines the machine's scope. In two cases the key is left unknown and listed in not_found instead: Cryogenics International publishes no full specification, and the SPEX electromagnetic impactor drive produces a field whose strength is not published.

Sizing conventions:
- Top-loading baths and chambers: sample.diameter.max is the smaller horizontal dimension and sample.height.max is the depth.
- Mills limited by feed size: both size keys equal the maximum feed size.
- ZwickRoell Charpy tempering unit: 10 mm cross-section and 55 mm length.
- Tinius Olsen chamber: follows the family mapping (smaller of interior width and depth; interior height).

Conservative choices:
- QualiBrittle NDA temperature.range is recorded as -120 to -70 C, because the upper end is printed only as 'ambient'.
- NDA stability is +/-2 C, the value for the LN2 range.
- DWTT uniformity of +/-1 C is recorded as a 2 C gradient.
- SPEX sample mass is 50 g from the current page, not the 100 g in the old 6875 handbook.
- Values printed only as 'about' (DWTT cooling and heating speeds, DWTT tank volume) are not recorded.

Two machines have only one documented process temperature, recorded with lo = hi: the SPEX CG-400 (LN2 immersion at 77.34 K, from NIST reference data) and the Cryogenics International CI-1600 (-196 C DCT soak). Experiments that need intermediate DCT ramp temperatures will therefore not be met by the CI-1600 on record.

vexp.summary:
I checked every requirement against its source. Sources were downloaded and searched locally: the three PMC articles, the Chalmers thesis PDF, the KSC-STD-Z-0009 Rev D PDF, the AWS/Boehler PDF and the Springer page.

The two MDPI papers (Coatings 12:281 and Metals 8:808) returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch. scite and Lune were unavailable (scite needs a paid plan; Lune's daily quota is used up). The built-in browser was at its tab cap, with tabs apparently in use by other sessions, so I left them alone. For those two papers only the OpenAlex abstracts could be checked. Requirements confirmed only in Section 2.1/2.2 are marked accept=false as unverified and should be re-checked against the full text.

Systematic problems found:
1. `pressure.max_working` is not a key in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so both LN2-turning pressure requirements (Ti-6Al-4V 6.8 bar, Inconel 1.5 bar) are rejected even though the quotes and numbers are correct. A new vocabulary key is needed.
2. The KSC "vacuum retention" profile cites Section 6.2.7, but every quote is from Section 6.3.2 (Inner Sphere and Internal Pipe Cold Shock, storage vessel), p. 28. 6.2.7 is a different test: 10 microns, 7 days. The content is accepted, but the name, id wording and locations should be corrected.
3. Tyre: the 13 inch value is the rim diameter of the COMSOL simulation model (Section 3.2), not of the tested tyres, so a mandatory requirement is unjustified. If kept, the outer diameter would be about 607.7 mm (fixed_value given), and it should be optional.
4. Al 1050 cryorolling: the height and diameter requirements assume vertical dipping, which the source does not state, so they are rejected as mandatory.
5. The LNG weld -163 C "service check" and the Ti machining 77 K temperature.range are not part of the documented procedures, so both are rejected.

All four X210CrW12 requirements are verified verbatim, including the 2 C/min ramps.

No exact duplicates. Partial overlaps to note:
- mfg_x210crw12_dct_minus180c overlaps the existing generic expansion_b_manufacturing_steel_deep_cryo_treatment (Messer brochure, -160 C, 24 h). It has a different steel, source, temperature and ramp requirements, so it is not listed as a duplicate.
- The Ti and Inconel LN2-turning profiles are the same process family on different alloys and pressures.
- The tyre impact profile differs from the existing rubber cryomilling profile.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source and grep-checked the quotes. Tavily is over quota and WebFetch would not return verbatim text, so I downloaded the pages with curl and extracted the ZwickRoell PDF with pdftotext. Every quote is really on the page. Of the capabilities, 89 are accepted and 9 rejected; 2 accepted ones need corrected values.

Rejected:
- **optical_access = false, 4 machines:** the QualiCHLTC100, QualiBrittle NDA, QualiLTC80 and CG-400 absences rest only on silence (open, top-loaded tanks, a semi-enclosed space with a safety shield, a latched lid).
- **Tinius Olsen electrical.sample_connections = false:** rests on silence; such chambers commonly have ports for strain-gauge leads.
- **Cryogenics International CI-1600 sample.diameter.max and sample.height.max:** the 48 x 24 x 22 in figure is never labelled as interior chamber size, and 'D = vertical' is an inference.

Corrected:
- **CI-1600 temperature.base and temperature.range:** -196 C (77.15 K) is below the boiling point of LN2 at 1 atm (77.35 K), which a nitrogen-vapour chamber at ambient pressure cannot reach. I changed both to the conservative printed value, -320 F = 77594 mK.

Duplicates:
- None of the 8 machines are already in data/cryostats.
- cole_parmer_spex_cg_400 is the same product as spex_sampleprep_6875_freezer_mill in research/v4/food_and_agriculture: the page gives item number 6875.

exp.notes:
Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\automotive_and_transportation\experiments.json: 10 new profiles. None of their ids or plain_names match an existing profile, and each has 3 to 4 requirements, every one with a verbatim quote of 50 words or fewer.

Research limits: the WebSearch budget for this turn and the Tavily, Lune and scite quotas ran out during the run. Sources were therefore pages that could be opened directly (TUV SUD, the iTeh preview of ISO 16750-4, the Infineon KBA, batterydesign.net, PMC, MDPI), plus abstracts found through Consensus whose DOIs were confirmed through Crossref.

Source caveats:
- Liu 2022 (SAE), Hu 2021 (IJHE), Wan 2025 (IJR): the quotes are the publisher abstracts as Consensus indexes them. The publisher pages hit a captcha or were blocked, so I did not open them or check the quotes against them.
- UN 38.3 values come from a TUV SUD test-lab page and AEC-Q100 values from an Infineon KBA, because unece.org and aecouncil.com could not be fetched.
- I could not get the AEC-Q100 temperature-cycling conditions, so that profile only checks the Grade 0 operating range (-40 to +150 C).
- IEC 62660-1 comes from a secondary summary (batterydesign.net), not the standard.

Other choices and caveats:
- ISO 16750-4 temperature code C (Tmin -40 C, Tmax 65 C) was chosen for the cycling profile. Its sweep-rate requirement is my own arithmetic on the quoted profile, using RT = 23 C, which is not in the quote, so it is non-mandatory.
- In Herran 2026 the Binder KB53 is named only for the 25 C discharge before the cells were opened. The text I retrieved does not name the chamber used for the -10 C aging.
- Most of these procedures are climatic-chamber tests. Their deciding keys are temperature.range and electrical.sample_connections. No source gives a sample-size or chamber-volume limit, except the 500 L tank.

Side effect: navigating the browser pane to the aecouncil.com AEC-Q100 PDF made a file-download save dialog appear to the user. I did not retry that URL, and no file was saved through my actions.

The existing automotive profiles (20 K membrane permeation, 304L tensile at 20 K, LH2 composite fatigue) are not duplicated. Nothing under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ was edited.

eq.notes: Output written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\automotive_and_transportation\equipment.json (generator script: C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\auto_equipment.py). 8 configurations from 4 manufacturers (BINDER, ESPEC including the Qualmark EXT line, Thermotron, Memmert). Every core passport key on every configuration has a sourced value or sourced absence, so not_found is empty. Coverage: climatic -40 C (BINDER MK 240), humidity -70 C (MKFT 240), ultra-low -75 C (Memmert TT300E75), LN2 rapid cycling to -100 C (ESPEC EXT2.0), air-to-air thermal shock (ESPEC TSD-101-W mechanical; Thermotron ATS-320-V-LN2 LN2), EV battery charge-discharge chamber (ESPEC ADBC-T) and a temperature-altitude chamber with vacuum to 8 torr (Thermotron FA-16-CH-5-5). Conventions follow sibling files: a missing magnet is recorded as not_available with an unknown value, backed by the complete spec; atmospheric air chambers carry vacuum.available as an installed false flag and pressure.base as not_available; an optional window or port is optional_not_installed with a true flag; compressor-only machines carry cryogen.type as an empty set. electrical.sample_connections is true for standard cable access/entry ports or cable tubes. ESPEC states the purpose for TSD and ADBC; the BINDER, Memmert and Thermotron ports are pass-throughs with no wiring installed, and the integrator may prefer a different reading of bare ports. Weaker absences: optical_access not_available for ESPEC ADBC-T and Memmert TT300E75 rests only on complete spec and option lists that name no window. sample.diameter.max is the smaller of interior width and depth, per family_mapping. temperature.sweep_rate.max stores the slower of the heating and cooling averages (BINDER), or the slower guaranteed ramp (ADBC: 50 K in 60 min, rounded down to 833 mK/min). The EXT2.0 figure of 70 C/min is an empty-chamber average. The ATS-320-V-LN2 temperature range is the family figure of -73 to 200 C. Its LN2-only status comes from the model suffix and the footnotes, which say LN2 is optional only on the ** models. The Thermotron FA access port is standard on the current web page but listed as an option in the 2017 brochure. Not covered: inTEST ThermoStream (datasheets sit behind a request form), LNG/LH2 vehicle tank rigs and ASTM D2137 brittleness testers (no reachable manufacturer spec), Weiss Technik (site would not render) and CSZ (expired TLS certificate). The Tavily quota and the session WebSearch budget were exhausted, so research ran on direct manufacturer URLs through WebFetch and the built-in browser.

vexp.summary: Re-fetched the sources: TUV SUD and Infineon in the browser pane, ISO 16750-4 from the iTeh preview PDF, plus batterydesign.net, PMC, MDPI and an OpenAlex abstract. Accepted 25 of 32 requirements. The UN 38.3, ISO 16750-4 constant-temperature, IEC 62660-1, lithium-plating and cold-cranking requirements are all verified. Rejected the ISO 16750-4 cycling sweep-rate requirement, because the 1.05 K/min value is derived (it depends on room temperature from ISO 16750-1, which allows 23 ± 5 °C) and not printed in the source. Rejected the AEC-Q100 electrical-connections requirement, because its quote is only a definition. Rejected the 30 A requirement on the SAE PEMFC system, because electrical.current_leads.max is not in the vocabulary. All requirements of auto_pemfc_stack_rapid_cold_start and auto_lh2_truck_tank_ln2_boiloff are rejected as unverified: the Elsevier abstracts were behind a Cloudflare challenge, the metadata APIs returned no abstract (publisher-elided), and the web-search budget was exhausted. The LH2 profile also uses two keys not in the vocabulary (chamber.volume, holding_time.static). No duplicates found: each profile is a different test or paper, and none matches an existing data/experiments profile or plain_name.
