veq.summary:
I re-fetched all 8 Automotive and transportation machines from their manufacturer sources. Pages came via WebFetch. The ESPEC ADBC flyer and the Thermotron BC-150 and BC-155 brochures came through as binary PDFs, so I read them locally: the ADBC flyer is image-only, so I read it visually, and pymupdf extracted the text of the two Thermotron brochures.

Duplicates: none. The only related entry in data/cryostats is expansion_b_espec_egnx12.json, which is a different ESPEC model.

Rejected (7):
- ADBC-T magnetic_field.max, optical_access, cryogen.cryogen_free and cryogen.type: all rest on the silence of a 2-page flyer whose spec table does not even give the cooling type.
- Thermotron ATS-320-V-LN2 optical_access=installed: the brochure lists windows as an option, and the product page hedges with "almost all".
- Memmert TT300E75 optical_access=not_available: the technical data is silent on a window.

Corrected (3 refs, on 2 machines):
- Thermotron FA-16-CH-5-5 chamber.volume: 478 L to 453 L. The product page gives 453 L; the brochure gives 478 L.
- Thermotron ATS-320-V-LN2 temperature.range and temperature.base: low end -73 °C to -65 °C. -73 °C is a family-wide claim; the model's own table row is rated -65 to 200 °C.

All other capabilities match the sources and are accepted.

experiments.name: Programmed freezing of Tris-egg-yolk-glycerol bull semen in 0.5 mL straws (5 to -140 °C at 5/40/20 °C/min, Mini Digitcool UJ400) with plunge into liquid nitrogen

experiments.description: ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices: cumin seed is chilled by liquid nitrogen sprayed and blended directly onto it until it reaches a -30 °C set point, then ground in a pin (impact) mill to 50-100 um; cryo-grinding raised volatile-oil recovery by 33.9-43.5% over a conventional mixer grinder.

requirements.rationale: The procedure is mechanical comminution with cryogenic cooling; a machine without a grinding function cannot perform it.
requirements.document_title: Sharma LK, Agarwal D, Rathore SS, Malhotra SK, Saxena SN (2016). Effect of cryogenic grinding on volatile and fatty oil constituents of cumin (Cuminum cyminum L.) genotypes. J Food Sci Technol 53(6):2827-2834. doi:10.1007/s13197-016-2258-0
requirements.quote: Cryogenic grinding of seeds was done using a cryogenic grinder (Spectra cryogenics, India) model Fine Impact Mill 100UPZ

requirements.rationale: The seed is cooled to a predetermined set point of -30 °C (243.15 K) before milling.
requirements.document_title: Sharma LK, et al. (2016). Effect of cryogenic grinding on volatile and fatty oil constituents of cumin genotypes. J Food Sci Technol 53(6):2827-2834
requirements.quote: Liquid nitrogen is added until the temperature of the material is reduced to a predetermined set point (−30 °C).

requirements.rationale: Cooling is by liquid nitrogen sprayed directly onto the seed.
requirements.document_title: Sharma LK, et al. (2016). Effect of cryogenic grinding on volatile and fatty oil constituents of cumin genotypes. J Food Sci Technol 53(6):2827-2834
requirements.quote: Liquid nitrogen is sprayed and blended directly onto the material.

experiments.name: Long-term ultra-low-temperature frozen storage of tuna meat at -45 °C or lower to prevent metmyoglobin (browning) formation
experiments.plain_name: Store sashimi tuna deep-frozen cold enough that its red colour does not turn brown
experiments.description: Nakazawa et al. (Int. J. Refrigeration 2020) stored low-pH and high-pH tuna meat at a range of frozen-storage temperatures over long periods: metMb% rose in low-pH meat held warmer than -40 °C, while no increase occurred at -45 °C or lower regardless of pH, supporting ultra-low-temperature storage of tuna.

requirements.rationale: Colour stability (no metMb increase) needs storage at -45 °C (228.15 K) or colder; either a documented range reaching that low or a documented lowest temperature settles it.
requirements.document_title: Nakazawa N, Wada R, Fukushima H, Tanaka R, Kono S, Okazaki E (2020). Effect of long-term storage, ultra-low temperature, and freshness on the quality characteristics of frozen tuna meat. International Journal of Refrigeration 112:270-280. doi:10.1016/j.ijrefrig.2019.12.012 (IIR FRIDOC abstract record)
requirements.quote: An increase in the metMb% was not observed in meat stored at −45 °C or lower, irrespective of the pH.

requirements.rationale: Storage warmer than -40 °C (233.15 K) increased metMb in low-pH meat; optional because the -45 °C requirement already covers it.
requirements.document_title: Nakazawa N, et al. (2020). Effect of long-term storage, ultra-low temperature, and freshness on the quality characteristics of frozen tuna meat. Int J Refrigeration 112:270-280
requirements.quote: The increase in metMb% was higher in the Low-pH samples stored at temperatures higher than −40 °C.

sources.citation: Nakazawa N, Wada R, Fukushima H, Tanaka R, Kono S, Okazaki E (2020). Effect of long-term storage, ultra-low temperature, and freshness on the quality characteristics of frozen tuna meat. Int J Refrigeration 112:270-280. doi:10.1016/j.ijrefrig.2019.12.012

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 food_and_agriculture profiles to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\food_and_agriculture\experiments.json. The file also gives evidence_status and accessed=2026-11-01 for each requirement. The builder script is at C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\food_exp_agent\build_food.py.

How I chose them: none duplicates the 3 existing expansion_b food profiles (gummy grinding, ice-cream recrystallization, strawberry lyophilization). I skipped probiotic freeze-drying because the biology agent already has bio_lactobacillus_freeze_drying. Wherever possible the requirements use core keys (temperature.range/base, cryogen.type, sample.diameter.max/height.max). Process flags, straw/vial counts, temperature.stability and humidity are mostly marked non-mandatory so they do not cause NEED_MORE_INFORMATION. The one exception is process.cryogenic_milling, which is mandatory for cumin grinding because grinding is the whole procedure.

Points to review:
1. The tuna profile has only 2 requirements (any-of [temperature.range, temperature.base] at_most -45 C, mandatory; plus an optional at_most -40 C). Only the abstract could be reached: the full text is paywalled and my search quota ran out.
2. Two profiles come from the same USDA ARS bull-semen protocol, which describes two different freezing methods: a programmable freezer (Mini Digitcool UJ400) and box freezing in liquid-nitrogen vapour. Their requirement sets differ completely, but you may want to merge them or swap one for a different experiment.
3. The -196 C liquid-nitrogen temperature is a reference value taken from other documents: the Youngs JoVE embryo protocol for the box-freezing profile and FAO Genebank Standards p.4 for sweet potato. The primary sources do not state it.
4. 1 C/h (apple buds) has no exact decimal in mK_per_min, so I wrote it as cooling_rate range_within 16-17 mK/min and explained this in the rationale.
5. No paper source for potato droplet vitrification was open, so I used sweet potato (open in PMC) instead. The cumin URL from the idea list is actually a turmeric 5 C pre-cooling paper, so I used Sharma et al. 2016 (PMC4951436), which grinds at a -30 C set point.
6. Most quotes came through WebFetch extraction of PMC pages and abstract pages; each was returned as a verbatim fragment and none is over 50 words. FAO and USDA quotes were read directly from the PDF text. The blueberry quotes are from the English abstract on spkx.net.cn (full text in Chinese, not read). The litchi quote "− 18 ºC" keeps the source's ordinal-sign character.
7. Tool limits hit: Tavily (plan limit), WebSearch (per-turn budget used up), Lune (daily quota, resets 2026-11-02T00:00Z) and scite (needs a paid plan or trial) were all unavailable. PubMed search started returning nothing toward the end.
8. Housekeeping: early on I overwrote a helper file, pdf2txt.py, in the shared scratchpad folder (C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\pdf2txt.py). It now contains a short pypdf text extractor (args: input PDF, output txt). If another agent's script depended on the old version, it should be regenerated.

Nothing under data/, cryolean/, lean/, frontend/ or paper/ was edited.

eq.notes:
Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\food_and_agriculture\equipment.json (the file has the same content as this result). 8 configurations on 7 equipment entries from 5 manufacturers: MVE Biological Solutions (XC 34/18 semen tank, SC 4/2V Next Generation dry shipper), Martin Christ (Epsilon 2-10D LSCplus pilot freeze dryer), SPEX SamplePrep (6875 Freezer/Mill cryogenic grinder), Minitube (IceCube 14M and 14S semen/embryo controlled-rate freezers) and PHC (MDF-MU339HL-PE -30 C freezer for genebank-type storage, MDF-DC500VX -86 C chest ULT freezer). NIST WebBook is used only as reference data for the liquid-phase LN2 temperature of the XC 34/18. All sources were accessed 2026-11-01. None of these duplicates data/cryostats or the other v4 industry files: the XC 34/18 is not healthcare's XC 47/11, the SC 4/2V New is not healthcare's CryoShipper XC or SC 4/3V, the Epsilon 2-10D is not the 2-4 or 2-6D used in biology and chemistry, and the PHC models are not biology's MDF-DU702VH.

Every configuration documents all 11 core-passport keys, except 3 on the SPEX mill (listed in not_found). Absences (magnet, sample vacuum, base pressure, viewport, sample wiring) are install=not_available and quote the complete specification table or feature list that defines the machine's scope.

Conventions used:
- A single storage temperature is stored as lo = hi: XC 34/18 at 77.34 K from NIST; the SPEX vial in LN2 at -195.8 C from the SPEX handbook.
- Freezers use the guaranteed control range, not the wider setting range.
- Top-loading spaces (chest freezer, IceCube, dewar canisters): diameter = canister diameter or the smaller horizontal dimension; height = canister height or vertical depth.
- Front-loading cabinet: diameter = the smaller of width and depth; height = interior height.
- Freeze-dryer shelf: diameter = the smaller shelf dimension; height = standard shelf spacing (59 mm, 5 shelves).

Points to be aware of:
- XC 34/18 holding_time.static stores the printed 'Normal Working Duration' (123 days, liquid storage under normal use). This sheet prints no separate static hold time, so the value is a lower bound of the true static hold.
- electrical.sample_connections=true on the Christ dryer (standard product-temperature/LyoControl sensors) and the IceCube (Pt-100 product probe) means sensor wiring to the product only, not general power feedthroughs.
- SPEX magnetic_field.max is deliberately not recorded as an absence: the mill applies an alternating drive field to the vial, but its strength is not published.

Not delivered: the WebSearch budget and Tavily quota were exhausted, so only manufacturer URLs that were already known or linked from their own sites could be read, and these categories have no reachable full specification:
- Cryogenic tunnel/IQF freezers: the Linde CRYOLINE MT/SC/TI pages give no temperature or size data.
- Planer Kryo 370: the spec sheet is hosted only on mail/support.planer.com, whose TLS certificate is invalid.
- IMV Digitcool alpha: the flyer lacks the temperature range and cooling rates.
- Walk-in seed-bank cold rooms and dedicated -60 C marine tuna freezers.

vexp.summary: I checked all 10 food and agriculture profiles (37 requirements) against their sources: the USDA ARS bull semen PDF, the FAO I3704E PDF, Europe PMC full text for 4 papers, the PMC page for the cumin paper, the spkx.net.cn abstract and the IIR FRIDOC abstract. Every quote was found in its source and every number and unit conversion is right. I rejected 5 requirements. Four use keys that do not exist in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so they cannot be checked: storage.capacity.straws_0_5ml (in both bull semen profiles), storage.capacity.vials_2ml (sweet potato) and humidity.range (seed genebank). The fifth, food_bovine_embryo_slow_freezing#2, makes liquid nitrogen mandatory for the freezing machine, but the source says a methanol-bath freezer, which uses no liquid nitrogen, also works; it should be optional. Two small corrections that need no rejection: the seed genebank ±3 °C quote is on PDF page 40, not 38; and the apple bud rate of 1 °C/h is 16.67 mK/min, which cannot be written exactly, so the 16-17 mK/min range asks for slightly more than needed. I found no duplicates, either among these 10 or against the existing food profiles (gummy homogenization, ice cream recrystallization, strawberry freeze-drying). Downloaded copies of the sources are in C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\dl (food_* and bull.pdf, fao.pdf).

veq.summary: I re-fetched every source myself: both MVE spec sheets and the MVE/Chart manual, the Christ brochure (pages rendered to check the bold row and the standard/option bullets), the SPEX handbook, the Minitube leaflet and catalog page, both PHC pages and the NIST WebBook. All seven machines are new: none of MVE, SPEX, Martin Christ, Minitube or PHC appears in C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\data\cryostats (53 files), and none repeats within this batch. Five capabilities are rejected: (1) Christ chamber.volume, because the 50 L is printed under the ice-condenser heading and is ambiguous on a double-chamber unit; (2) SPEX optical_access, which rests only on a minimal spec table's silence; (3, 4) IceCube 14M and 14S electrical.sample_connections, because the leaflet never says a Pt-100 sits in a straw or sample; (5) PHC MU339HL sample.height.max, because the 1262 mm empty-cabinet height is not conservative for the 6-shelf configuration. Accepted with caveats: XC 34/18 holding_time.static uses the 123-day working duration, which is a conservative lower bound but not a printed static hold. Christ pressure.base is 'about 0.005 mbar', depends on the vacuum pump, and comes from a generic statement. The SC 4/2V temperature range comes from a 2015 manual covering the legacy SC 4/2V, but it agrees with the 2025 sheet's '-150°C or colder'. SPEX milling.jar_volume is a sample capacity, which is at most the vial volume. Everything else matches the sources exactly, and every unit conversion is correct.

exp.notes: Wrote C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\environmental_science\experiments.json with 10 profiles. Each requirement records evidence_status and accessed=2026-11-01. All ids, plain_names and units were checked: there are no duplicates against data/experiments or other research/v4 outputs, and every unit is on the allowed list. Every quote was read from a fetched page or from pdftotext output of a fetched PDF. pdftotext dropped degree signs and some typographic symbols, so these were put back by hand in the AMT, ACP, FrESH and NRA quotes; checking the PDFs character by character before integration is advised. The three Prometheus protocol quotes came through WebFetch's summarizer and not raw text, so check them against the page too. Search quotas ran out partway through this run (Tavily usage limit, Lune daily limit, WebSearch turn budget), so sources are limited to the idea URLs and pages reachable by direct fetch. Ideas not used: TO-15 canister VOCs, because they duplicate the existing expansion_b_env_whole_air_voc_cryofocusing; and the Radiocarbon sediment-DIC distillation, because its URL redirects to the journal home page. Judgment calls: (1) chamber.volume >= 84 m3 is mandatory in both AIDA profiles because the published expansion-cloud method depends on the large vessel, so only AIDA-scale chambers can pass. (2) HPGe temperature.base <= 77 K follows the NRA manual wording, so an electrically cooled detector documented warmer than 77 K would fail. (3) The Medusa page does not say cryogen-free, so no cryogen requirement was written; module.gc_ms (existing key) is mandatory and will be NEED_MORE_INFORMATION for machines that do not document it. (4) The ice-core archive uses keys ["sample.height.max","sample.length.max"] as any-of for the 1 m core sections; the -24 C examination temperature is non-mandatory. (5) The specimen bank uses the German ESB archive page for the <-150 C, above-LN2 requirement, with the NIST Biorepository as a supporting source; its 10 g portion requirement is non-mandatory. Core-passport keys used: temperature.range, temperature.base, vacuum.available, pressure.base, optical_access, sample.diameter.max, sample.height.max, cryogen.type. Shared new keys used: chamber.volume, temperature.cooling_rate.range.

results.note: Verified on icecores.org/about: 'The main archive freezer ... is held at a temperature of -36°C.' 237150 mK is correct.
Verified: 'The examination room ... is held at -24°C.' 249150 mK is correct. Optional is appropriate.
Verified photo caption: 'Each silver tube on these shelves contains a 1-meter long section of an ice core.' A 1000 mm length on either key, any-of, is reasonable for storage.
Verified in Sect. 2.1 of the PDF: 'Afterwards, the entire system is evacuated to a pressure of 0.3 Pa.'
Verified: 0.3 Pa in Sect. 2.1. The discussion also says lower pressures (<0.3 Pa) may be needed for some soils, so at_most 0.3 Pa is correct.
Verified in Sect. 2.1: 'During the entire extraction process, the samples are heated to 90 C ... trapped in the frozen U-tubes.' 363150 mK is correct.
The intro quote is verbatim, but it describes the general method (citing Ingraham and Shadel). Table A1 of the paper lists the nitrogen cold trap the authors used, so LN2 is supported.
The quote is verbatim in Sect. 3.2.1. A better supporting passage is Sect. 2.4: 'Soils were extracted for 180 min and plant tissues for 90 min.' Optional is appropriate.
Verified on the PrometheusWiki protocol: 'The main line should have a vacuum between 0-30 mTorr.'
30 mTorr = 0.03 Torr. The unit and value are correct.
Verified: 'Once the water is at a boil, freeze the sample collection tube with LN2.'
Verified: '1 inch ignition (sample) tube' is in the materials list. Inch is a defined unit in units.py.
Verified: 'Boil for 60-90 minutes.' The protocol also gives soils 40-45 min and stems 60-70 min. at_least 90 min is the upper end; optional is appropriate.
Verified on the Bristol ACRG page: 'Central to the Medusa-GCMS design is the Cryotiger which cools adsorbent traps to -165oC.' 108150 mK is correct.
Verified: 'T1 is heated to 100oC and back-flushed to transfer analytes to T2, held at -165oC.' The trap cycles span -165 C to +100 C (108.15-373.15 K).

The quoted sentence does not mention GC-MS. An equivalent passage is on the same page: 'This instrument has a unique pre-concentration system coupled with a GCMS ...'. The quote should be replaced with it.
Verified in the abstract: '24 freezing experiments were performed at temperatures between 189 and 235 K ...'
Verified in Sect. 2.1: 'The aerosol vessel can be evacuated to a final pressure of about 0.01 hPa by two large mechanical pumps ...'
Verified in Sect. 2.2: '(2) evacuating the vessel to 0.01 hPa, (3) flushing twice ...' 0.01 hPa = 0.01 mbar is correct.

The quote is verbatim (84 m3), but chamber.volume is not a key in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so this requirement cannot be compiled. It is also doubtful as mandatory: 84 m3 describes this one facility, not a stated procedural minimum.
Verified in Sect. 3.1: 'an Argon-Ion laser beam (99% polarised light at 488 nm) is directed into the chamber via an optical fibre ...' optical_access is in the vocabulary (flag).
Verified in the abstract: 'Cloud cooling rates up to -2.8 K min-1 were simulated dynamically ...' 2800 mK_per_min, optional, is fine.

Verified in Sect. 6: 'with the chamber temperature covering a range of -20C to -65C'. 208150-253150 mK is correct. The profile description says -60 C in one place; the requirement correctly uses -65 C.
Verified in Sect. 2: 'pumping down to below 1hPa and flushed with dry synthetic particle free air.'
Below 1 hPa = 1 mbar. at_most 1 mbar is correct.
The quote is verbatim, but chamber.volume is not a vocabulary key. The facility's size is not a procedural requirement either.
Verified in the EGUsphere preprint, Sect. 2.1: 'Each plate contains 96 droplets of 50 uL each. During a measurement, the bath is cooled from 0 to -35 C at 1 C min-1 ...'
Verified: 1 C min-1 ramp. point_within 1000 mK_per_min is correct.
Verified: '... a floating frame holding two standard 96-well PCR plates, and a USB camera for optical detection of freezing events'.
Verified in Sect. 2.2.1: 'The sublimation is run at around 0.25 mbar pH2O or -34 C.' Sect. 3.1 repeats -34 C. 239150 mK is correct.
Verified in Sect. 2.2.3: 'temperatures as cold as -150 C in the external water trap are needed to reach the required H2O vapour pressure.' 123150 mK is correct.
Verified in Sect. 3.1: 'If the system is leak free, a final pressure of <2 x 10-7 mbar is achieved at the high vacuum side with gas free blank ice'.

For the six PDFs I downloaded them to C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\envpdf and extracted their text with pdftotext. Tavily was over its usage limit, and WebFetch's model refused the two AIDA PDFs. 37 of 40 requirements are accepted. Every quoted value and unit matched the source. Three are rejected: (1) env_aida_sulphuric_acid_homogeneous_freezing#3 and (2) env_aida_desert_dust_ice_nucleation#3 use chamber.volume, which is not in capability_vocabulary.json, and the 84 m3 figure describes the facility rather than a requirement. (3) env_hpge_gamma_environmental_radioactivity#1 maps the 30x25x50 cm lead-shield inner volume to sample.diameter.max, which is the wrong property. One fix to make in an accepted requirement: env_medusa_halocarbon_monitoring#2 should quote 'pre-concentration system coupled with a GCMS' instead of the Cryotiger sentence. Duplicates: env_plant_stem_cryogenic_distillation makes the same measurement as env_soil_plant_water_cryo_vacuum_extraction: cryogenic vacuum distillation of soil and plant water for d2H/d18O, with an LN2 trap. veq.summary:
I re-fetched all the sources: the Stirling SU780XLE, SU105UE and ULT25NEU manuals, the Christ Alpha 1-2 and Alpha 1-4/2-4 manuals plus the brochure, flyer and product page, the Linkam LTS420 and LNP96 pages, and the Julabo MAGIO MS-1000FF technical data. None of the 8 machines is already in data/cryostats, and none repeats within the batch.

Rejections:
- **Christ Alpha 1-4 and 2-4 temperature.range / temperature.base:** the quoted glossary entry itself says 'Single-chamber method (not available for freeze-dryers with an LSCbasic control system)'.
- **Christ Alpha 1-2 temperature.range / temperature.base:** the -20 °C is for freezing inside the condenser chamber. This configuration dries on unheated shelves outside it (double-chamber), and samples must be pre-frozen externally.
- **Christ chamber.volume (all three):** the value is the condenser chamber, not the drying chamber where the samples sit.
- **sample.height.max, SU780XLE and SU105UE:** the full cabinet height is not reachable with 5 shelves installed, or with the SU105UE's fixed shelf.
- **LTS420 temperature.cooling_rate.range:** the LNP96 rating applies to 'specific stages' generically, not to the LTS420.
- **LTS420 magnetic_field.max:** the absence rests only on a short web specification list.
- **Julabo optical_access and electrical.sample_connections:** the bath is open-topped, and it has an integrated external Pt100 sensor input.

Corrections:
- Alpha 1-2 and 1-4 condenser minimum changed to -50 °C (223150 mK), because the same manuals say the condenser ends at approx. -50 to -54 °C.
- LTS420 sample.diameter.max changed to 26 mm, because samples sit on a 76 x 26 mm slide.

Schema notes:
- temperature.condenser.min should be the established key condenser.temperature.min.

exp.notes: Output written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\geology_and_oceanography\experiments.json (10 profiles; ids are all geo_*, none clash with data/experiments; plain_names are unique against the existing catalog and the other v4 outputs). Quotes were read from full texts: the Eawag PDF (pypdf text extraction), the PMC page for Notini 2023, the GO-SHIP PDF (pypdf text extraction), arXiv full text for Qin/Hartmann/Kuhs, and Undermind full-text PDF readers for Liu 2025, Kars and Kodama 2015, Konig 2018, Pradel 2025 and Yamamoto 2018. I cleaned up PDF extraction errors in the quotes; for example, the Beyerle PDF renders the plus-minus sign as '('. The Liu, Kars, Konig, Pradel and Yamamoto quotes came from Undermind's PDF reader and were not checked against the publisher pages, so spot-check them before integration. Tool limits during this run: the shared WebSearch budget ran out, and Tavily, Lune, scite and PubMed calls failed (quota or API errors). Because of that, five of the suggested ideas could not be sourced word-for-word and were replaced: the MARUM 2G 755 u-channel SRM (the page gives only the 150 cm length, no other values), the Oregon State LHe-free SRM blog (TLS certificate rejected), Stanley 2009 WHOI (certificate rejected), Hirai 2001 methane-hydrate DAC (Tsukuba repository under maintenance) and the CGS hydrate PXRD paper (403). The Verwey-cycling idea (Ozdemir/Dunlop EPS 2018) was skipped because it overlaps mat_magnetite_verwey_remanence_cycling. Profile notes: liquid-nitrogen steps that happen in a separate dewar or trap (quench, LN2 traps, sample storage) are mandatory=false so they do not rule out the main cryogenic machine. Konig 2018 tank footprint 105 x 95 cm is given as a circumscribed diameter of 141.6 cm (1416 mm), following the shared sample.diameter.max rule. The Notini 2023 cryostat model appears only in the Supporting Information, which was not read, so reported_equipment says so. Range constraints use the checker semantics in cryolean/smt.py (at_most on a range means the machine's lower bound is at or below the value). Units used: K, mK, T, Pa, mbar, mm, cm, inch, h, all from the allowed list.

The condenser minimum is in temperature.condenser.min. (2) ULT25NEU sample.height.max is the smallest interior dimension (221 mm), because the manual does not say which axis is vertical. (4) The 8604 field of 1.54 T is the value at gap index 5 with standard pole caps, which the cryostat requires. Gaps in coverage: there is no superconducting rock magnetometer. results.note: Verified in Beyerle et al. 2000 (Eawag PDF p.2044): the CCT is held at 14 K for Ne adsorption, and 'the CCT is heated to 100 K to release Ne'. The quote is an elided composite of real sentences. A 14-100 K range is correct.

Verbatim on p.2044: 'cryogenic cold trap (CCT) at 14 K containing a high porosity filter of sintered stainless steel (Nupro SS-2FE-5, 0.5 um) that adsorbs Ne quantitatively'. at_most 14 K is justified.
Verbatim: 'stable within ±0.1 K or better during Ne adsorption' (the PDF text layer renders ± as '('). at_most 0.1 K is correct.
Verbatim on p.2043: the copper tube is connected to the 'ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) extraction and purification line'. The CCT is part of this UHV line.
Verbatim on p.2043: 'reduces the pressure to about 10 -7 mbar'. 1e-7 mbar = 1e-5 Pa, which converts cleanly to uPa. The figure is approximate, so optional is right.
Verbatim on p.2043: T1 and ZEO1 are 'both cooled by liquid nitrogen'. Optional is fine because these traps are on the same line but separate from the CCT.

PMC10339716 Results has 'Spectra collected at 140, 77, 45, 25, and 15 K were fitted using ... (xVBF) model', and the Figure 3 caption has 'Spectra were collected at 25, 10, and ≤5 K.' The quote stitches these two real passages together. A 5-140 K window is correct.

Verbatim: 'The 5 K Mössbauer spectra of samples incubated for 12 weeks revealed the formation of octets'. The captions say ≤5 K, and the Fe(II) octet only appears at 10 and 5 K, so at_most 5 K is justified.
Figure 2 caption verbatim: 'Spectra were collected at 77 K.' 77 K is the routine quantification temperature.

GO-SHIP Hydes et al. NSOP 7 section 5.1 has this verbatim: 'Before freezing ensure that sample bottles are no more than 3/4 full and firmly capped. A deep freezer (at least -20 oC) should be used.' 253150 mK = -20 C is correct. In smt.py, at_most on a range key means the low end is at or below the bound (the space can reach -20 C or colder), so the semantics are valid.
The same verbatim passage, including 'Good air circulation around the bottles in the freezer is important.' at_most 253.15 K on temperature.base is correct.

The quote is real, but the source does not forbid an evacuable space. It only asks for air circulation. flag_is false on vacuum.available ('sample space can be evacuated') would wrongly penalise any equipment that can evacuate. This is an inference the procedure does not support, so drop it.
arXiv:1803.02244 Table 1 row 5 verbatim: '5 H2O 268 3.5 8.28 11.85474(2) 98.3(3) 85.6(4)'. 268 K is the H2O formation temperature. D2O runs used 271 K.

The data is right: Table 1 row 8 shows 15 MPa. The key is not: 'pressure.max_working' is not in data/capability_vocabulary.json, and validation.py rejects unknown keys. The nearest existing key is pressure.operating.range (unit Pa) with point_within 15000000 Pa, but its description is gas-handling pressure interval. A new vocabulary key would need to be proposed, so reject as written.

Verbatim: 'pressure was manually maintained to the set point within 0.1-0.2 MPa. All formation reactions ran for 3 weeks.' 3 weeks = 504 h. The paper notes conversion is incomplete even after 3 weeks, so the duration matters and mandatory is justified.

Verbatim: 'Al-vial with an inner diameter of 6.7 mm or in a larger PFA-jar ... inserted into a precooled custom-built pressure vessel ... circulating cryostat bath'. at_least 6.7 mm is a valid lower bound. The vial's outer diameter is larger, so this understates what the vessel must take.
Verbatim: 'the pressure cell was rapidly quenched in liq. N2 and pressure was concomitantly released.' Ice spheres are also made by spraying into LN2. Optional is appropriate.
Verbatim: 'Hydrate samples were placed in a cooling stage (Linkam THMS600) and measured at 113± 0.1 K under the ambient pressure of liq. N2.'
The same sentence gives 113±0.1 K, so at_most 0.1 K is correct.

Verbatim: '50x long-working distance objective (Olympus) and 100 um confocal hole. The laser beam focused on the surface of hydrate samples within a diameter of around 1.1 um'. Optical access is mandatory.
Verbatim: 'ground and sieved under liq. N2 ... and stored under liquid N2.' The THMS600 also runs on LN2. Optional is fine.

Frontiers in Earth Science 2025 (10.3389/feart.2025.1661858) section 2.3 verbatim: FC samples 'cooled from 300 K to 5 K in a 5 T field ... recorded during zero-field warming to 300 K.' MPMS XL-7 confirmed.
Verbatim: 'For the ZFC protocol, samples were first cooled to 5 K in zero field, then subjected to a 5 T pulse'.
Verbatim LTC sentence, 'magnetizing samples at 300 K in a 5 T field', is present. 5 T at_least is correct; the vocabulary unit is mT.

Verbatim: 'AC susceptibility was measured on this subset at frequencies of 1, 10, and 111 Hz during warming after zero-field cooling to 5 K.' module.acms is the right key. Optional is fine because only a 9-sample subset was measured.
Earth Planets Space 2015 verbatim: 'The sample is then cooled down to 5 K in a 2.5 T magnetic field, and the LT-SIRM is measured during warming to 300 K (FC for field cooled).'
Verbatim: 'A low temperature (LT)-SIRM was imparted at 5 K at 2.5 T.' Also 'Low-temperature measurements (down to 5 K) were made with a Quantum Design ... (MPMS)'.
Verbatim: 'SIRM ... imparted at room temperature (300 K) at 2.5 T was first measured in a zero magnetic field (trapped field <150 μT).' at_least 2.5 T is correct.

The quote is verbatim, but the shielded room houses the separate room-temperature 2G SQUID rock magnetometer used for NRM/ARM. It is not the cryogenic MPMS that this profile matches against. Attaching module.magnetic_shielding to the cryostat requirement set mixes instruments, so drop it.
Frontiers in Earth Science 2018 6:234 verbatim: 'Three ambient temperatures (−15°C, −25°C, and −40°C) were chosen'. The freezer is settable from 0 to −45°C. range_within 233150-258150 mK is correct.
Verbatim: 'water tank (ca. 105 × 95 × 99 cm; Figure 1A) holding natural, open ocean seawater'. A cold space of at least 99 cm height is justified, though the figure is approximate ('ca.').

The dimensions are verbatim. The 1416 mm is derived, not printed: sqrt(105²+95²) = 141.598 cm, rounded up to 1416 mm, and the arithmetic is correct. Accepted as a conservative circumscribed-footprint proxy; the origin should be marked inferred.

Nature Communications 2025 (s41467-025-59608-2) Methods verbatim: 'The cooling elements, cooled by circulation of cooling liquid from a cryothermostat bath, had a bottom of the temperature of −5.1 ± 0.1 °C.' 268050 mK is correct.
The same sentence gives ±0.1 °C, which equals 0.1 K. at_most 0.1 K is accepted.
Verbatim: 'Freezing lasted 19 h to ensure that the ice thickness attained a plateau ... (Fig. S8).' Optional, at_least 19 h, is fine.

The quote is verbatim ('set aside at −20 °C and scanned by micro-X-ray-tomography'). But -20 °C core storage happens in a separate freezer. Putting a point_within 253.15 K on the same temperature.range as the −5.1 °C cryothermostat requirement mixes instruments and would bias matching, so drop it.

Frontiers in Earth Science 2018 6:48 verbatim: 'low-temperature demagnetization (LTD; Ozima et al., 1964) was conducted on a specimen by soaking it in liquid nitrogen for 10 min and then leaving it at room temperature for 30 min in a zero field.'
Verbatim: 'applied the Tsunakawa–Shaw method ... to 169 specimens cut from one-inch cores of all sites'. The inch unit exists in units.py. at_least 1 inch is correct.
Verbatim: '... in a zero field.' A zero-field environment during the LTD cycle is part of the procedure, so mandatory is justified. module.magnetic_shielding is the closest key.

exp.notes:
The full output is in C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\metrology_and_calibration\experiments.json. It has 10 profiles. Each requirement has a quote, location, accessed=2026-11-01 and evidence_status. The checks passed: ids are unique, plain names are unique and differ from the existing profiles, every key is in data/capability_vocabulary.json or research/v4/vocabulary.json, and every quote is 50 words or fewer.

Search tools ran out during the work. Tavily, Lune and WebSearch hit their quotas, and Consensus hit a rate limit. Sources were read with WebFetch, plus direct downloads of BIPM PDFs into the scratchpad that were turned into text with pdftotext.

Some quotes are not first-hand. The quotes from the PMC, NIST and Cryogenic Ltd pages came through WebFetch's summary, which presented them as verbatim. The two quotes for the cryocooled PJVS IEEE abstract come from the Consensus abstract record. All BIPM and Isotech quotes are copied from the PDF text.

Three planned experiments were dropped. The microthermometry-stage calibration paper on HAL was blocked by bot protection. The GaAs QHR system from Cryogenic Ltd only states 'up to 14 Tesla', which is not a requirement of the procedure. The NIST cryogenic radiometer would duplicate expc_metrology_optical_watt. In their place are the BIPM ICVGT and helium vapour-pressure scale realizations.

These experiments use only core keys, plus electrical.coax_lines, temperature.stability, operating_duration.max, chamber.volume and cooling_power.at_4200mK. A missing machine value for those extra keys will not block a verdict when the requirement is non-mandatory.

Some requirements are marked non-mandatory on purpose:
- cryogen.type liquid_nitrogen for argon, because NIST also has a closed-cycle apparatus.
- cryogen.cryogen_free for the graphene QHR and capsule-SPRT experiments.
- liquid_helium for the vapour-pressure scale and RRR.
- The 0.902 mK nuclear-stage option for PLTS-2000.

In metro_pjvs_10v_cryocooled, cooling_power.at_4200mK at_least 270 mW is approximate because the source figure is at 4.3 K, so it is non-mandatory. The CCC requirement for a 76.2 mm bore comes from the vendor cryostat spec, not from a stated insert size, so it is also non-mandatory.

There is some overlap with existing profiles. metro_pjvs_10v_cryocooled is about cryogen-free PJVS operation, while the existing expc_metrology_josephson_dc is DC transfer against an INRIM PJVS. metro_ccc_resistance_bridge and metro_graphene_qhr_tabletop are related, since both use a CCC, but they are separate procedures.

results.note: Verified in Argon-2018.pdf, slide 5: 'The Triple Point Of Argon (83.8058 K) to the Triple Point of Water (273.16K)'. 83805.8 mK point_within is correct.
The NIST SPRTCL page (nist.gov/node/1896016) has the quote verbatim and lists argon TP 83.8058 K, U=0.14 mK (k=2). The argon has to be frozen, so base <= 83.8058 K is physically justified.
Slide 15 has the quote verbatim: 'It has re-entrant tube to accommodate either a funnel of liquid nitrogen for cooling or an SPRT for calibration'. Optional status is appropriate.

The quote 'The melt lasted some 4 hours' is on slide 25. However, plateau length is a measured property of the sealed cell, not something the procedure demands of the apparatus. operating_duration.max is the equipment's continuous operating duration, so this is the wrong property. Recommend dropping it or moving it to reported_conditions.
Table 1 in the BIPM CCT cryogenic fixed-point guide lists T90/K 13.8033, 24.5561, 54.3584, 83.8058. The range 13803.3-83805.8 mK is correct.
Table 1 gives the e-H2 triple point as 13.8033 K. The sample must be frozen below it, so base <= 13803.3 mK is justified for the full four-point procedure.
Section 2.2 has the quote verbatim: 'the whole being enclosed in a vacuum jacket for thermal isolation'.
The quote about melting by intermittent heat input is verbatim (calorimetric method section). Heat pulses and thermometer readout need electrical leads; 'present' is a valid kind for a flag key.
Verbatim: 'Nowadays preferably cryostats designed around closed-cycle cryocoolers are applied...'. The same section says liquid-refrigerant cryostats were traditional, so optional status is correct.
ICVGT guide section 1 has the quote verbatim: 'In the range from 3 K to the triple point of neon (24.5561 K)...'. Range 3000-24556.1 mK is correct.
Verbatim: '(a point between 3.0 K and 5.0 K, 13.8033 K, 24.5561 K)'. Reaching 3 K is needed to cover the defined range, so base <= 3000 mK is consistent with the range requirement.

The quote is verified ('typically one litre', section 5). However, chamber.volume does not exist in data/capability_vocabulary.json, so the requirement cannot be compiled. Remove it or move it to reported_conditions.
VPS guide section 1 has the quote verbatim: 'In the temperature range from 0.65 K to 5.0 K, the ITS-90 is defined...'. Range 650-5000 mK is correct.
Verbatim: 'ranges 0.65 K to 3.2 K for 3He; 1.25 K to 2.1768 K for 4He...'. base <= 650 mK is needed for the full 3He range.
Section 3.2 has the quote verbatim: 'copper thermometer blocks containing vapour-pressure bulbs were suspended inside a vacuum jacket'.
Verbatim: 'In both cases, the vacuum jacket is immersed in a liquid 4He bath.' The next sentence prefers closed-cycle cryocoolers, so optional status is correct.
PLTS-2000 guide has the quote verbatim: 'around the pressure minimum, at Tmin = 315.24 mK'. base <= 315.24 mK is needed to pass through the normalization minimum.

The quote is verbatim, but it comes from the cell-filling paragraph. It still says measurements extend 'up to 1 K', and the introduction defines the PLTS-2000 as 0.902 mK to 1 K. Range 315.24-1000 mK is a justified subset.

Verbatim: 'EDA emphasizes the need to use 3-terminal connection ... each plate of the capacitor is connected to a separate coaxial line'. Two plates means two coax lines minimum, so count_at_least 2 is correct.
The introduction has the quote verbatim ('in the range from 0.902 mK to 1 K'). Optional status for full-scale coverage via a nuclear stage is appropriate.
PMC6604640 has the quote verbatim: 'Maintaining a temperature below 4 K is still very feasible even after applying nearly 250 uA'. The base reached was 2.7 K, so base <= 4000 mK is reasonable.
Verbatim: 'The cryogen-free system reaches temperatures as low as 2.7 K and was operated at 5 T for all measurements.' 5000 mT is correct.
Verbatim: 'The sample is mounted onto a transistor outline (TO-8) package or a 32-pin leadless chip carrier (LCC-32).'
The NIST CPEM 2018 abstract has the quote verbatim ('maintained in a 5 T table-top cryocooler system'). Optional status is appropriate.
The Cryogenic Ltd re-condensing cryostat page has the quote verbatim: 'more than 250 milliwatt can be absorbed at 4.2 K.' The CCC and SQUID operate in the 4.2 K bath.

The quote 'nominally 5 litres of liquid helium at 4K' is verbatim. But the same page lists 'No cryogens required for start-up or operation' (the helium is liquefied in situ from gas), and cryogen-free CCC systems exist. Making liquid_helium a mandatory supplied cryogen is not justified; it should be mandatory=false.

The CCC product page says the bridge 'is ideally suited to routine calibration work on four terminal resistance standards'. That is equivalent to the paraphrased quote, which is not verbatim. The quote text should be corrected to the actual wording.

Verbatim: 'Re-condensing liquid helium CCC cryostat with 3 inch (76.2 mm) bore access'. The CCC insert is the loaded object and the mm-to-um conversion is fine. Acceptable as optional, though it is a bore dimension rather than a true sample diameter.
Verbatim: 'control the bath temperature to the sub milli-Kelvin level.' Optional at_most 1 mK is acceptable.
The IEEE TIM abstract (via OpenAlex) has the quote verbatim: 'A 1.32 mA step width ... was achieved at an operating temperature of 4.3 K.'
The abstract has the quote verbatim: 'The quantum accuracy of the PJVS is maintained at temperatures up to 4.8 K.' Chip temperature <= 4.8 K is a valid upper bound on the attainable base temperature.

The abstract has the quote verbatim ('successfully operated a PJVS circuit on a cryocooler'). The profile is defined by cryocooler operation, which separates it from the existing liquid-helium expc_metrology_josephson_dc profile.

The quote is verbatim, but 270 mW is the net cooling that particular cryocooler delivered at 4.3 K. It is not the chip's dissipation requirement, and a cryocooler gives less at 4.2 K than at 4.3 K. Encoding it as cooling_power.at_4200mK >= 270 mW states the wrong temperature and treats an observed capacity as a demand. Move it to reported_conditions.
The NIST publication record has the quote verbatim ('Flat-spot measurements of various quantized voltages produced with all of the sub-arrays ...'). The biased subarrays need electrical leads.
The Lake Shore recalibration list has 'Cernox calibration, 1.4 K - 325 K' under item CAL-CX-1.4L. Range 1400-325000 mK is correct.
Same listing (CAL-CX-1.4L). The lowest point is 1.4 K, so base <= 1400 mK is justified.
The Lake Shore Cernox spec page has the quote verbatim: '10 mV or less for T > 1.2 K' (recommended excitation). Resistive readout needs leads.

PMC4551274 abstract and section 1 have the quote verbatim ('measured at 273 K (the ice point) and 4.2 K'). NIST actually reported 4.03 K because of local pressure, but the 4.2-273 K range is the defined RRR span.

Verbatim: 'the transverse magnetoresistance data were all less than or equal to 5 T'. Table 1 shows trimming at 5 T versus 8 T changes RRR by only about 0.3, so 5 T is sufficient for the field-suppression and Kohler procedure named in this profile. Zero-field methods exist, but this profile names the field method, so mandatory is acceptable.
Verbatim: 'where l is the distance between the voltage taps and A is the cross-sectional area of the sample'.
Verbatim: 'Because liquid helium boils near 4.0 K at the atmospheric pressure of our test site'. Optional status is appropriate.

vexp.summary:
I checked all 10 metrology profiles (39 requirements) against their sources: 34 accepted, 5 rejected, and no duplicates.

Sources read: the Isotech argon PDF, four BIPM CCT guides (cryogenic fixed points, interpolating gas thermometry, vapour pressure, PLTS-2000), the NIST SPRTCL page, PMC6604640, the NIST CPEM 2018 record, two Cryogenic Ltd pages, the PJVS abstract via OpenAlex (the IEEE page did not load), the Lake Shore pages and PMC4551274.

Rejected:
1. argon#3: the 4 h melt length describes the cell, not a demand on the apparatus.
2. icvgt#2: `chamber.volume` is not in `capability_vocabulary.json`.
3. ccc#1: `liquid_helium` cannot be mandatory. The vendor page itself says "No cryogens required for start-up or operation" (helium is liquefied from gas on site), and cryogen-free CCCs exist.
4. pjvs#3: 270 mW is what that cryocooler delivered at 4.3 K. It is neither the chip's need nor a 4.2 K figure.

Fix needed but accepted: the ccc#2 quote is paraphrased. The real wording is "ideally suited to routine calibration work on four terminal resistance standards".

Duplicates: none. The cryocooled PJVS profile overlaps with the existing liquid-helium `expc_metrology_josephson_dc` but differs by its mandatory cryogen-free cooling. The capsule cryogenic fixed-point profile overlaps with the long-stem argon SPRT profile but uses a different instrument, cryostat and temperature range. All plain_name values are unique.

veq.summary:
I re-fetched every source myself with curl and pdftotext: all the Isotech data sheets and product pages, the Isotech Argon 2018 seminar, the Fluke 7380 User's Guide and product page, the MI 6800C brochure and page, the MI 6820T data sheet and page, and the Cryogenic Ltd CCC page, flyer, m-CFMS flyer and CFMS brochure v5.2.

All quotes were found. None of the 8 machines is already in data/cryostats (the folder has 53 files; no Isotech, Hart/Fluke 7380, MI or Cryogenic Ltd re-condensing/m-CFMS entries), and none is repeated within this batch.

Value corrections:
- **Isotech 459 temperature gradient:** 5 mK changed to 10 mK, from the vertical profile of ±0.01 °C at -150 °C.
- **Isotech 459 sample height:** 466 mm changed to 460 mm. The data sheet itself lists 'Immersion Depth 460mm'.
- **MI 6820T base temperature:** 3.6 K changed to 4 K. The '< 3.6 K' figure is a cryocooler cold-head row; the sample is only documented at 'Operational temperature < 4 K'.
- **m-CFMS sample diameter:** 30 mm changed to 5 mm. The installed DC transport module allows 5 mm x 10 mm samples at most; 30 mm is the VTI bore.

Rejections:
- **Absences resting on marketing silence or inference:**
  - optical access on the 6800C, the CCC cryostat and the Isotech 471 (its lid evidence comes from the superseded 2018 version).
  - magnetic field on the CCC cryostat.
  - vacuum and base pressure on the 6800C, the m-CFMS and the CCC cryostat. All are pumped VTIs or reservoirs; the CCC page even says to flush the cryostat using a small vacuum pump.
- **CCC cryostat temperature stability:** it needs the Lake Shore controller, which the configuration excludes.
- **MI 6820T temperature range:** no variable range is documented.
- **m-CFMS module.electrical_transport:** the vocabulary defines this key as the AC option, but the configuration has the DC module only.

Notes:
- **Cooling power at 4.2 K:** both MI systems' 0.9 W figures were accepted as cold-head ratings, matching the existing repo convention (CRX ev_ls_0012).
- **Keys missing from the core vocabulary:** holding_time.static and chamber.volume are not in data/capability_vocabulary.json. Both are already used in other research files.
- **Source PDFs:** the downloads and extracted text are in C:\Users\Rahma\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Rahma-CryoLean\e0ff960e-6e13-4d25-b7a1-50ccd6d09f12\scratchpad\dl (files 459.pdf, 471.pdf, 461.pdf, m7380.pdf, 6800c.pdf, 6820t.pdf, cccflyer.pdf, qhr.pdf, cfms.pdf and their m_*.txt).

The device envelope used for the size requirements is the ORTEC Detective-X HPGe identifier (39.5 x 16 x 21 cm), which is rated for -20 C to +50 C.

requirements.rationale: The chamber must cover the full -20 C to +50 C operating range (253.15-323.15 K).

exp.notes:
I wrote 10 defense_and_security profiles with 41 requirements to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\defense_and_security\experiments.json. That file also stores evidence_status and accessed=2026-11-01 for each requirement. Every key exists in data/capability_vocabulary.json or in research/v4/vocabulary.json. None of the plain_names matches an existing profile in data/experiments or research/v4.

Research limits: Tavily hit its plan limit, WebSearch used up this turn's budget, and Lune used up its daily quota. I read the sources with WebFetch and with local pdftotext on the PDFs WebFetch fetched, plus one Consensus search. Quotes from layout-extracted PDFs have their spacing collapsed, and I put the degree sign back where the PDF glyph broke.

Judgement calls:
1. MIL-STD-810H does not set fixed test temperatures. I used the Table 502.7-I values: -46 C for Cold (C2) and -51 C for Severe Cold (C3). Method 503.7 tells users to pick cold-region temperatures from that table.
2. The ANSI N42.34 size requirements assume the ORTEC Detective-X is the device under test. Its 39.5 x 16 cm footprint has a circumscribed diameter of 426.2 mm, rounded up to 427 mm; the height is 21 cm.
3. The Ricor K508 profile uses the maker's rating points as the acceptance test.
4. The HPA report gives no crystal temperature, so the 77 K HPGe requirement comes from the Japanese NRA method No.7. I extracted and checked that PDF myself.
5. The Twente degaussing quotes come from the abstract on the University of Twente publication page because the full PDF returned 403. Kilo-amp-turns cannot be turned into a current-lead rating, so no current_leads requirement is written.
6. The Hingst Joule-Thomson cooler source is a Consensus abstract record. I could not confirm a DOI.
7. There are three overlaps with other batches. The Stirling-cooled HPGe profile is close to nuc_hpge_insitu_electric but covers a different use (checking people for internal contamination). The two IR cooler profiles are close to aero_lptc_ir_detector_80k. The temperature-shock profile is close to the semiconductor thermal-cycling profiles.

Not done: there is no military space thermal-vacuum (SMC-S-016) profile, because no source could be reached once the search budgets ran out. The Teledyne FLIR and Kunming reliability papers state MTTF figures but no cold-tip or heat-load test conditions, so the cooler life test only appears as a non-mandatory operating_duration requirement of 27,000 h.

eq.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\defense_and_security\equipment.json. 8 configurations, 7 machines, 5 manufacturers (RICOR, ORTEC/AMETEK, Mirion/Canberra, Tristan Technologies, Tenney/TPS). Categories covered: integral rotary Stirling IR coolers (K508 77 K class, K562S HOT 95-150 K), Stirling/electrically cooled HPGe RIIDs (Detective X, Falcon 5000), HTS 77 K SQUID magnetometer (G377), MIL-STD-810 Method 503 / MIL-STD-883 1010 thermal-shock chambers (Tenney TS2-2, TS2-8), thermal-vacuum chamber (Tenney economical TVAC). Not covered (no reachable spec text this run; the WebSearch budget and Tavily quota were exhausted): linear split Stirling/pulse-tube coolers (Thales/AIM sites unreachable; the Teledyne FLIR FL-100 brochure gives MTTF only), HTS degaussing systems (research demonstrators, not catalog products), stand-alone MIL-STD-810 climatic chambers (already covered by the automotive BINDER/ESPEC/Thermotron files). Conventions: for RIIDs temperature.range/base are the instrument operating (ambient/measured-object) range, since the measured source is outside the instrument and the crystal temperature is unpublished; external-measurement instruments (RIIDs, G377) record sample.diameter/height as not_available (no sample space), which makes size-requiring experiments DOES_NOT_MEET. Bare cryocoolers: temperature.range = cold-tip range, sample.diameter.max = cold-finger OD (8 mm, from the K508 drawing callout 'O.D. Ø8', read from the rendered datasheet image, and the K562S text '8mm Cold Finger'), vacuum.available false (dewar supplied by the IDCA integrator). Tenney TS2 numbers come from an image-only spec-table PDF that was rendered and transcribed; the TS2 product load '200*' is footnoted as the carriage limit with recovery to be reviewed by the factory. Optional windows/ports follow sibling files: optional_not_installed with flag true; TS2 2-inch traveling port counted as electrical.sample_connections=true (pass-through, no installed wiring). Falcon 5000 evidence is the 2015 DHS SAVER market survey (reference_data), not a Mirion datasheet (mirion.com returned 403). Tristan G377 datasheet is dated 2007 but the model is still listed on tristantech.com/general. Typical-only values (Ricor and Detective X cool-down) are stored as published since no guaranteed value exists. Cooling power stored in mW (vocabulary canonical nW; exact conversion). Tenney TVAC cryogen-free assignment rests on the economical configuration's listed features (fluid chiller, packaged vacuum); the LN2 cold trap is listed among custom-line special features.

results.note: Verified in the PDF on p. 502.7-4, Table 502.7-I: the Cold (C2) row reads -37 to -46 C for both ambient air and induced. -46 C = 227.15 K is correct. The procedure says to use the test plan's low operating temperature, so choosing the C2 extreme is the profile's own design decision, and it is supported by the table.

The quote is verbatim (p. 502.7-8, Step 1). It mentions only 'operational configuration', not cables, so the electrical port is an inference. That is acceptable only because the requirement is non-mandatory.

The -51 C value for Severe Cold (C3), ambient and induced, is correct (p. 502.7-4). Caveat: the quoted string is a pdftotext layout artifact. Verified verbatim on p. 502.7-5, para 2.3.2 b (explosives, munitions, rubber and plastics). The 72 h minimum is correct. Non-mandatory is reasonable.

Verified verbatim, para 2.3.2 c(1). Fix the location: the passage is on p. 503.7-4, not 503.7-5. Verified verbatim on p. 22, clause 7.1.1 of ANSI N42.34-2006. 253.15-323.15 K is correct. The radtek.cn host appears to be a third-party copy of a copyrighted IEEE standard. Keep quotes short and consider citing the IEEE listing.

Using one product's envelope is the profile's design choice, and the description states it. A footprint diagonal is a reasonable stand-in for the diameter key.

'(250J@80K@23°C): 5 min. typ.' was confirmed. The vocabulary key means time to reach base temperature, but this spec is a loaded cool-down to 80 K, a typical value. Fine as non-mandatory.

The quote is verbatim (p. 2): MTTF of approximately 27,000 h. But MTTF is a statistical reliability figure, not a documented continuous operating duration. Mapping it to operating_duration.max (at_least 27,000 h) uses the wrong property and would wrongly rule out nearly every machine. Drop it, or move it into missing_information/notes.
Verified verbatim in the UT research portal abstract (INEC 2020, doi 10.24868/issn.2515-818X.2020.068): 77-85K using (subcooled) liquid nitrogen.

The quote is verbatim and 'liquid_nitrogen' is a valid v4 token. But the mandatory flag is not justified. What the procedure needs is HTS coils held at 77-85 K, which a cryocooler could also provide. The sister profile def_hts_squid_mad_tensor_77k marks LN2 non-mandatory for exactly this reason. Also, no equipment in data/ documents cryogen.type yet, so a mandatory set_contains would leave every match UNKNOWN. Accept if changed to mandatory=false.
Verified verbatim in the abstract: 'up to 1 or 2 kAturns'. The coils carry transport current, so current leads are needed. Mandatory is justified.

Verified on tristantech.com/general: the G377 is a '77K Geophysical Magnetometer SQUID System', and the T877 data-sheet link is labelled '(77K)'. The quote describes the G377 rather than the T877, but the HTS line is consistently 77 K.

Verified: 'using liquid nitrogen as a refrigerant for reduced cost and portability.' Non-mandatory is justified.
The consensus.app page is blocked by Cloudflare for direct fetches. I verified the full abstract (Hingst 2003) through the Consensus search API: 100 K (-173 C) in under 2.3 s from a 323 K soak.

Verified in the abstract. '2.3' as an exact decimal string is allowed by SCHEMA. Note that cooldown_time.max means 'time to reach base temperature', while this is time to 100 K from a +50 C soak. Mandatory is justified because fast cool-down is the whole point of the procedure.

Verified in the abstract: the demonstrated system used argon with CF4 or CH4. 'compressed_argon_jt' is an allowed v4 cryogen.type token. Caveat: the abstract also names nitrogen as a possible spray gas ('e.g. Argon, Nitrogen'), so argon is the demonstrated choice, not the only possible one.

vexp.summary:
I checked 37 requirements in 10 Defense and security profiles: 35 accepted, 2 rejected. I re-fetched every source myself: MIL-STD-810H 502.7/503.7, ANSI N42.34-2006, the ORTEC Detective-X data sheet, HPA-RPD-045, NRA Method No.7 and the Teledyne FLIR white paper as PDFs (curl plus pdftotext, written to a fresh scratchpad folder, verify_def); the Ricor K508 and Tristan pages with WebFetch; the UT degaussing abstract with curl; and the Hingst spray-cooler abstract through the Consensus API, because consensus.app blocks direct fetches. All quotes and numbers match.

Rejected:
- def_hot_mwir_idca_120k#5: an MTTF of about 27,000 h is mapped to operating_duration.max, which is the wrong property.
- def_hts_degaussing_ln2_77_85k#1: the liquid-nitrogen cryogen.type requirement is marked mandatory. A cryocooler could also hold 77-85 K, and no equipment documents cryogen.type yet. Accept it if made non-mandatory.

Must be fixed before ingest:
- cooling_power.at_77000mK and humidity.range are missing from data/capability_vocabulary.json. They exist only in research/v4/vocabulary.json, so they must be registered before build-db, or those requirements will not compile.

Smaller fixes:
- Location errors: the 503.7 RH/temperature passage is on p. 503.7-4, not -5. The NRA No.7 PDF page numbers are about 1-2 pages off (by my extraction, PDF p. 27 and p. 30).
- The C3 quote 'Northern Asia (some areas), -51 -51' is a PDF-layout artifact that mixes C2 location text with C3 values. Replace it with the Table 502.7-II 'Severe Cold' line.
- The ANSI N42.34 source is hosted on a third-party site (radtek.cn) that looks like an unauthorized copy of the IEEE standard.

Duplicates: none exact. def_hpge_stirling_incident_body_monitor overlaps in hardware with research/v4 nuc_hpge_insitu_electric (both use a battery-powered, electrically cooled ORTEC Detective). They measure different things (people vs ground), but they set different temperatures: 77 K here against at most 113 K there.

veq.summary:
I re-downloaded and read all 10 sources: both RICOR product pages and 2019 datasheets (drawings checked visually), the ORTEC Detective X brochure (htds.fr, rev 051917), the DHS SAVER RID survey, the Tristan HTSGeoSystems.pdf, the Tenney thermal-shock brochure and spec table (image table checked visually) and the Tenney TVAC brochure 09032026. Every quoted string and numeric value is in its source, and all unit conversions are exact.

Accepted: all of RICOR K508 and K562S, ORTEC Detective X and Tristan G377, most of Tenney TS2-2 and TS2-8, and most of the TVAC entries.

Rejected (12):
- **Falcon 5000-20 (7):** every not_available absence (magnetic_field, pressure.base, optical_access, electrical.sample_connections, sample.diameter.max, sample.height.max) and vacuum.available=false. They rest on a DHS market-survey summary, not a complete spec. A full Mirion spec sheet is needed.
- **Tenney TS2-2 and TS2-8 (2):** electrical.sample_connections=true/installed. A 2-inch traveling port is a cable pass-through, not installed sample connections.
- **Tenney TVAC economical (3):**
  - magnetic_field absence: it rests on a brochure for custom chambers, not a complete spec.
  - cryogen_free and cryogen.type: the brochure lists an 'LN2 Cold Trap' under Special Features without marking it custom-only, so 'no cryogen' is unproven.

Vocabulary gaps: the keys cooling_power.at_77000mK, holding_time.static and chamber.volume are not in data/capability_vocabulary.json and must be added before ingest.

Duplicates: none. No RICOR, ORTEC, Canberra/Mirion, Tristan or Tenney machine appears in data/cryostats, data/*.json or cryolean.db, and none is repeated within the batch.
